records.question: Why was he called 'Bishoy the Jeremian'?
records.answer:
St. Bishoy was called "Bishoy the Jeremian" because of his deep love for the Book of Jeremiah, which he memorized and held in special regard. It is said that while reading this book, he would often see the prophet Jeremiah himself, which highlights the profound connection he felt with the text and the prophet. This unique experience of seeing Jeremiah during his readings contributed to his nickname, reflecting both his spiritual depth and his dedication to the Scriptures [3][4]. 

His intense devotion to prayer and fasting, alongside his commitment to the word of God, further solidified his reputation as a saint who embodied the teachings and spirit of the Scriptures, particularly those of the prophet Jeremiah [3].

His Love for the Salvation of All Souls: 
Saint ‘Bishoy’ had a disciple named ‘Isaac,’ who descended to the world 
and was seduced by a Jewish woman to forsake his faith, and he was converted 
to Judaism and lived with her . When he happened to encounter some monks, 
he asked them to tell St. ‘Bishoy’: “Your son, the Jewish ‘Isaac,’ has fallen and 
seeks from you to pray on his behalf to God to save him.” On hearing that, the 
woman said: “Even if ‘Bishoy’ come to me, I shall seduce him.” On returning 
to the monastery, the monks forgot what happened. Then, they were asked by 
the saint: “Has someone asked you to tell me something? ” They answered in 
the negative. The saint asked them whether they have encountered the Jewish 
‘Isaac,’ so they told him what happened and what ‘Isaac’ and the Jewish 
woman said. At that moment, they saw the saint retreat three steps backward 
and make the sign of the Cross on himself at each stage. Astonished, the monks 
said; “Even you, father, fear that woman?” St. ‘Bishoy’ humbly answered: “My 
children, the woman was the cause of the fall of ‘Adam,’ ‘Samson,’ ‘David’ 
and ‘Solomon.’ Who would be the poor ‘Bishoy’ to challenge her?!  Nobody 
can overcome the tricks of Satan in wo men, except that one whom God is 
with.” He kept praying and fasting for the sake of his son ‘Isaac’ until God 
saved him, and he came back and repented. 
Forsaking Scetis: 
In the year 407 AD, the first attack of the Berbers on the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ took place. At that time, the monks escaped from the desert. St. ‘John 
the Short ’ asked St. ‘Bishoy’: “ Do you fear death, O man of God? ” He 
answered him: “No, but I fear a Berberian would kill me and goes to hell 
because of me!” 
St. ‘John the Short ’ went to mount ‘Kalzam,’ near the monastery of Abba 
‘Anthony’ where he reposed . Whereas, St. ‘Bishoy’ went to ‘Ansena’ (the 
village of ‘Sheikh Abbadah’ near ‘Mallawy’), and he lived in the mountain . 
There, he formed a close relationship with ‘St. Abba ‘Paul of Tamouh,’ and 
sought from the Lord not to be separated from him when they would repose , 
and God granted them their wish. 
St. ‘Bishoy’ remained in his expatriation until he reposed on the 8th of Abib 
in the year 417 AD, after reaching 97 years of age. He was buried in the castle 
of ‘Meniat el-Saqar’ near ‘Ansena.’ When St. ‘Paul of Tamouh’ reposed, St. 
‘Athanasius’ of ‘Ansena’ gathered the two saints'  bodies and buried them 
together in the monastery of abba ‘Bishoy’ in ‘Ansena’ (Monastery of El -
Bersha). The bodies of these two saints were returned to the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ during the patriarchate of the 52nd pope Abba ‘Yusab I’ (831-849 AD).

wept, and raised his eyes to heaven and cried out: “My Lord and my God! If 
you heal me of this illness; I shall repent, return to You and worship You 
with all my heart .” ‘Bishai’ (Peter) was healed,  and he  did not forget his 
promise to the Lord, but he was inflamed in his heart with an intense longing 
to experience the monastic life. He forsook the sheep he was shepherding, and 
set forth to the monastery where he met with St. ‘Bigol,’ the uncle of St. 
‘Shenouda’ (who was to become the Archimandrite in Mount Adriba). 
His Monastic Life: 
God used the illness to bring that young man out of the covetousness of the 
body, which would destroy the soul . Once he tasted the real spiritual life, his 
heart got filled with so much joy to set forth firmly and be willing to do so 
many labors enduring daily so many harsh sufferings with a joyful heart.  
He lived with St. ‘Bigol’ in a  fantastic friendship, partaking together in 
monasticism and worship without ever getting bored, watching the nights, and 
opposing the temptations of the devil. 
God granted him an exalt ed capability beyond the limits of human 
endurance; he used to fast, in a way that defied imagination, for a whole month 
not tasting anything, and by a fantastic Divine allowance, he would stand the 
entire night praying. God, in His love, granted him to ha ve the deeds of other 
people revealed before his eyes, which he used to support them on the life of 
true repentance. Because of God's grace working in him, many people came to 
him from all over Egypt to seek his blessings . They benefited greatly by his 
spiritual sermons, and he also wrote essays for the monks and those in the 
world. 
Through the friendship of th is saint with St. ‘Bigol,’ he was present when 
the young Abba ‘Shenouda the Archimandrite;’ St. ‘Bigol's’ nephew, first came 
out in the wilderness in  his 7th year of age. He was clothed by his uncle the 
holy monastic Eskeem, in obedience to an angelic proclamation, and the 
presence of St. ‘Bishai.’ The three of them, despite the difference in age, 
worked with one spirit in a fantastic fellowship, realizing the saying of the wise 
‘Solomon’: “A threefold cord is not quickly broken.” (Eccl. 4:12). 
Each of them built for himself a cell on the mountain and another one near 
the church . I t so happened that while th ey were setting forth to visit A bba 
‘Jehnes’ (John) on Mount ‘Assiut,’ they heard a voice from heaven saying: “I 
have chosen you, O ‘Shenouda’ an Archimandrite.” 
St. ‘Bishai’ reposed in the Lord on the 5th of Amshir, and was shrouded by 
St. ‘Shenouda.’ From his body, many signs and wonders appeared, which were 
all documented by Abba ‘Shenouda,’ who wrote his biography and described 
his ascetic life.

to fast the whole week and eat only on Saturdays. His prayers and fasting got 
to hand in hand with his intense love for the word of God. He memorized most 
of the Holy Bible by heart. The Book of ‘Jeremiah’ had a special place in his 
heart; that it was said that he used to se e the prophet Jeremiah during his 
reading of his Book; that he was called ‘Bishoy the Jeremian.’ 
He considered hand-work as a significant part of building his spiritual life. 
He believed in the saying : “If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat. ” (2 
Thess. 3:10). His friend Abba ‘John the Short’ said about him that when a rich 
man brought to him plenty of gold as a donation, he told him: “The dwellers 
of the wilderness have no need of gold and should not have any of it. Go instead 
to the villages of Egypt and distribute it to the poor. God bless you.” After the 
man went his way, and the saint returned to his cell, Satan came to him, saying: 
“You fatigued me so much, O Bishoy .” And, the saint answered him: “Since 
your fall, and all your fatigue is in vain.” 
His Fellowship with our Lord Jesus; 
Through his pure heart, he used to meet often with the Lord Jesus Christ on 
a friendship level . He used to see Him, to talk with Him , and to enjoy His 
Divine proclamations. It was said that, having been so persiste nt in his great 
ascetic life and prayers that the Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him, saying: “My 
chosen vessel ‘Bishoy,’ peace be with you; I saw your labor and strife, and 
behold, I shall always be with you!”  
Another time, as our saint remained a long time fasting, the Lord appeared 
to him, saying: “You labored too much, My chosen vessel Bishoy!” The saint 
answered Him: “It was You O Lord who labored for me, but I have not labored 
at all!” 
A third time, the Lord appeared to him, saying: “Rejoice, My chosen vessel 
Bishoy. Do you see this mountain? I shall send you monks to fill that mountain 
to worship Me.” The saint asked Him: “Will You sustain them, Lord, in such a 
barren wilderness?” The Lord answered: “If they love one another and keep 
My commandments, I shall sustain them in everything!” The saint asked Him: 
“Will You save them from all the anguishes and afflictions mentioned in the 
Gospel?” The Lord answered: “Whoever fears, obeys Me and keep My 
commandments; I shall save him from all temptations! ” He then blessed him 
and ascended.

him and blessed him . The saint worshipped Him and washed His feet with 
water in a basin, then the Lord ascended . St. ‘Bishoy’ drank from that water 
and left a portion for his disciple . The saint sought from him more than once

BISHOY, ST. ABBA 
Our great saint abba ‘Bishoy’ represents the simple life striving in the Lord, 
that was founded upon the love fellowship with the Lord Jesus Christ. He had 
a personal relationship with Jesus that broke the obstacles down to open up the 
heart by the Holy Spirit that the Heavenly Groom would transfigure within it 
and reign with power and dominion! 
St. ‘Bishoy’ was born in ‘Shansa,’ a village in the governorate of ‘El-
Menufyia,’ around the year 320 AD. He was one of six brothers, whose father 
reposed when they were relatively young, and their mother raised them  up. 
One day the mother saw an angel who came to tell her: “The Lord says to you: 
‘Give Me one of your children to serve Me all the days of his life. ’” She 
answered: “Sir, they are all for the Lord. Let Him take whomever He chooses.” 
The angel put his hand on this saint, and said: “This is a good laborer for the 
Lord.” Being weakly built and frail in the body, his mother asked the angel to 
choose another one; but he answered her: “The Lord said ‘My strength is made 
perfect in weakness.’” (2 Cor. 12:9). 
In Scetis (Shiheet): 
Having reached twenty years of age in the year 340 AD, the young ‘Bishoy’ 
set forth to the wilderness of ‘Scetis,’ where he became a disci ple of Abba 
‘Bemwah’ (Bemen), the disciple of St. ‘Macarius’ (300-391 AD). There, he 
worshipped in seclusion for three years without going out of his cell. He grew 
in virtue and had his heart inflamed with love for God. 
Life in Seclusion: 
When Abba ‘Bemwah’ reposed in the Lord, his two disciples Abba ‘Bishoy’ 
and Abba ‘John (Yeĥness) the Short,’ spent the whole night praying to seek the 
guidance of God . An angel appeared to them and said that Abba ‘John the 
Short’ should remain alone in that location . In obedience, Abba ‘Bishoy’ left 
the place forsaking his friend, and d ug for h imself a cave near the southern 
rock, about two miles away from Abba ‘John the Short.’ 
His Strife: 
As he loved prayer, he made a hole in a high spot on the cave wall, then he 
fixed a wedge in it and tied one end of a rope around it . Then, he used to tie 
the long hair of his head with the other end of that rope; so that whenever his 
head would get heavy and drop down due to sleepiness, the rope would pull it

BISHAI OF ANTIOCH, ST. 
(The martyr) 
‘Bishai’ (Abshai) was the brother of St. ‘Hur’ (Abahur) of Antioch. He was 
ordained as a priest because of his piety . His brother and his mother went to 
Alexandria, where they were martyred. Their brother, the priest, went there to 
take care of their bodies . Then, he felt the longing to partake in  their crowns. 
So, he set forth to the governor to proclaim his faith, endured sufferings until 
he died. In vain, the governor attempted to burn their bodies. 
The Church celebrates his feast on the 1st day of the short Coptic month: 
‘Nasie’ (the forgotten days). 
 
BISHAI, THE HERMIT, ABBA 
The biography of Abba ‘Bishai the Hermit ,’ known as Abba ‘Bishai’ the 
dweller of the two graves at the entrance of ‘Tod’ (Mount Tod, east of the Nile 
river opposite to ‘Armant’), was linked to those of SS. ‘Pasantaos’ and ‘Sorus.’ 
The three of them were considered among the first monks who became 
disciples of St. ‘Pachom,’ the father of the ‘Koinonia’ (Coenobite). 
He was a hermit who worshipped God from his early age and labored in his 
prayers day and night . He was also known for his love of the book of the 
prophet ‘Jeremiah;’ so that it was said that every time he read it, he would find 
the prophet ‘Jeremiah’ himself before him, kiss his head, then watch him 
ascending to heaven (which also happened to him when he read the other books 
of the prophets). 
Giving his body no rest, he loved doing metanoias and long watching of the 
nights. After completing his strife, he reposed in the Lord on the 25th of Kiahk. 
His body was buried in his church, from which many signs and wonders 
appeared. 
 
BISHAI, ST. ABBA 
The story of this saint reveals the fantastic plan of God for the salvation of 
every soul; how He uses every tool to draw them to Him, and how He sets 
them on the highest level if they receive His call and respond to it. 
This saint, also (called ‘Peter’), was born in the village of ‘Epsona,’ a suburb 
of ‘Akhmim.’ In his youth, he walked in an evil path; but God did not leave 
him there but allowed for him to fall ill, and in a night vision , He revealed to 
him the place of the eternal sufferings  which he was heading to . He bitterly

on the basin, he found it empty. When the saint told his disciple what happened, 
he regretted it badly and was in bitterness for his disobedience. 
As the monks knew that the saint would see the Lord now and then; they 
sought from him to intercede for them to enjoy seeing Him as well, so the Lord 
promised to appear to them on the mountain at a particular time. The brethren 
greatly rejoiced , and all of them set forth toward the mountain . The saint, 
because of his old age , was at the rear . There, he encountered an old er man 
overcome with weakness and frailty, not able to walk, and none of the passing-
by monks cared to help him. Saint ‘Bishoy’ asked if he may carry him, and he 
did carry him and walked without feeling any labor . However, the older man 
started to get heavier and heavier; and the saint perceived that He was no one 
but the Lord  Jesus Christ Him self. He then looked at Him and said: “The 
heaven is not wide enough to accommodate You, and Your majesty shakes the 
earth; how can a sinner like me carry You? ” To this, the Lord  Jesus Christ 
smiled at him and said: “Because you carried Me, My beloved ‘Bishoy,’ your 
body will never see decay!” Then, He disappeared. St. ‘Bishoy's’ body is still 
kept in his monastery without de terioration up to this very day . Once the 
brethren knew about what happened, they grieved deeply for passing by that 
Old Man and not gaining the blessing of carrying Him. 
An Encounter with St. Ephraim the Syrian: 
By a Divine arrangement,  Mar ‘Ephraim the Syrian ’ came once to meet 
with Abba ‘Bishoy.’ As St. ‘Ephraim’ talked in the Syrian tongue, while St. 
‘Bishoy’ talked in the Cop tic tongue; the later sought from God to give them 
both the ability to understand each other without the need for an interpreter, 
and God granted them that, and they managed to spend a tremendous spiritual 
time together. St. ‘Ephraim’ learned from St. ‘Bishoy’ about the monast ic 
experiences of the Egyptian fathers, particularly of St. ‘Macarius the Great.’  
After a week, St. ‘Ephraim’ left. Then, a brother came to seek St. 
‘Ephraim's’ blessing, but when St ‘Bishoy’ told him that he just left, the brother 
started to run to catch him. St. ‘Bishoy’ called him and said he would never be 
able to because St. ‘Ephraim’ was carried away by a cloud. It was also said that 
St. ‘Ephraim’ has left behind his stick, in front of the cave of St. ‘Bishoy.’ 
Emperor Constantine visited Him: 
St. ‘John the Short’ once went to visit his friend St. ‘Bishoy,’ and while he 
was still outside his cell, he heard him talking to someone inside. Knocking on 
the door and entering, he found no one with the saint. Asking him with whom 
he was talking, he answered: “Emperor Constantine came to visit me and told 
me: ‘I wish I have abandoned my kingdom and became a monk; for I did not 
imagine how the monks enjoy such an honor and great glory . I see how those

It was said that, so many people were so impressed by the work of God with 
him and his endurance with joy for all these tortures he under went, that they 
set forward to proclaim their faith in Jesus the Lord, and that on the day of his 
martyrdom, 95 persons received with him the blessed crowns of martyrdom. 
      [The Synaxarion of Rene Basset: 10 Mesra] 
 
BIPHA, ABBA 
(The martyr) 
He was martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Diocletian’ (284-305 AD) around 
the year 303 AD. Hearing about the persecution, he consi dered it a chance to 
enjoy the heavenly kingdom. With an inflamed zeal, he stood in the middle of 
the city to urge the believers to become martyrs with joy. A multitude gathered 
around him proclaiming their longing to receive the crown of martyrdom and 
outlined in a procession led by ‘Bipha’ himself. Once they reached the palace 
of the governor, they publicly proclaimed their faith. Accusing him of sorcery, 
the governor started to torture him. 
The hand of God was with him all the way. When they pressed him with the 
hinbazeen, the angel of the Lord came down and broke it, and inflicted some 
of the soldiers with paralysis . However, with incredible love, ‘Bipha’ healed 
them. When he was placed on a bed heated by fire, the angel extinguished the 
fire. Provoked to anger, the governor ordered to chain him and take him around 
the town while being whipped, to make him an example to the others . He 
received all that with joy and gladness of the heart. When he was brought back 
to prison, he supported his fellow prisone rs and held them fast into the f aith. 
Then, he saw the heavens opened , and as though a person of light carrying a 
crown was calling him to receive it. On the next day, he was tied to the tail of 
a horse to be drawn and bruised. They finally cut his head off, and he received 
what his heart desired. The feast of his martyrdom is celebrated by the Coptic 
Church on the 24th of Toba. 
 
BISHAI ANOUB, ST. 
(The martyr) 
He was a soldier  in the days of ‘Cyprian,’ the governor of ‘Atrib’ (now 
Banha). When Emperor ‘Diocletian’ (284-305 AD) stirred up persecution on 
the Christians, this soldier came forward and proclaimed his faith in the Lord  
Jesus Christ. He was arrested, and the governor tortured him, but when he did 
not forsake his faith, or deny his Christ, his head was cut off in ‘Matarieh’ in 
the region of ‘Ăin-Shams;’ a suburb of Cairo, on the 19th of Paona.

his dark prison, as though he was attending a banquet, with a shining exultant 
countenance. 
When the governor condemned him to death, the saint put on his white altar 
attire, and when the deacon asked him why, he said: “My son, I am going to 
my wedding celebration; a day for which I longed all my life.”  
He received the crown of martyrdom on the 27th of Kiahk. 
 
BESSARION THE GREAT, ST. 
The Church in the East and the West cherish that amazing father ‘St. 
Bessarion the Great.’ The Coptic Church celebrates his repose on the 25th of 
Mesra, whereas the West celebrates it on the 17th of June. That Egyptian father 
lived in the 4th century; and was likened by his admirers to ‘Moses,’ ‘Joshua,’ 
‘Elijah,’ and ‘John the Baptist .’ He was said to have lived for a while along 
with the wild beasts in the wilderness. 
His Sojourn: 
He was b orn to Christian parents , and he loved the angelic life since his 
childhood. He felt a stranger in this world , and that feeling never left him all 
his life on earth. He first set forth to Abba ‘Anthony the Great,’ where he stayed 
under his guidance for some time. Next, he went to St. ‘Macarius’ and became 
one of his disciples. Then, he wandered in the wilderness like an immigrating 
bird who owned nothing, settled nowhere, and awaiting his eternal comfort.  
St. ‘Bessarion's’ disciples told about him that he lived like a flying bird or 
a wild animal in the wilderness , spending his life without any disturbance or 
worries. He was never preoccupied with a place to live in, food to eat or even 
to have books to read. He was completely free of any worldly desires, feeding 
upon the hope in the things to come, fortified by the strength of faith . He was 
living with perseverance like a prisoner being led from one place to another, 
perpetually enduring the nakedness and the cold under no roof , occasionally 
enjoying the sun's warmth, and wandering in the wilderness like the stars. 
He often enjoyed his wandering in the desert, as if he was sailing into an 
open sea. During his wandering, if he happened to come to a monastery where 
monks live in a life of fellowship, he used to sit outside the gate weeping and 
wailing like someone whose boat sank and left him stranded on the shore, and 
when a brother would come out to find him in  that condition, sitting like a 
beggar; he would generally approach the saint gently , saying: “Why are you 
weeping, my fellow man? If you need anything, as much as possible, we could 
give it to you. Please, rise, come in, and partake in our table and be comforted.” 
The saint would answer  him: “I cannot live under a roof, a s long as I would

records.question: Why did Christ tell us to pray it in the plural?
records.answer:
Christ instructed us to pray the Lord's Prayer in the plural to emphasize the communal nature of our faith and to reflect our unity as members of the Church. This approach encourages us to pray not just for ourselves but for all believers, aligning our will with God's desire for the salvation of everyone. St. John Chrysostom notes that by saying "our Father," we are reminded to make our supplications for the entire body of believers, not just for individual needs. This reflects the idea that we are all part of one family under God, which St. Augustine also highlights by stating that in this prayer, "the lord and the slave are brethren" under one Father [1][2].

Moreover, St. Cyprian emphasizes that the Lord, as the Teacher of peace and unity, intended for prayer to be a collective act. He points out that we do not ask for our own needs alone but for the whole community, reinforcing the notion that our prayers should be public and common, reflecting our interconnectedness as a people of faith [1][2]. Thus, praying in the plural fosters a spirit of love and solidarity among believers, aligning our hearts with God's will for all humanity.

57 
4 
The Model Prayer  
“Our Father who art in heaven” (Matt. 6:9–15, Luke 11:2–4). 
931. Why is the Lord’s Prayer important? 
St. Augustine says, “The Son Himself, as you heard when the Gospel was read, taught 
His disciples and His faithful ones this Prayer. Good hope have we of obtaining our cause, 
when such an Advocate  has dictated our suit. The Assessor of the Father, as you have 
confessed, who sits on the right hand of the Father; He is our Advocate who is to be our 
Judge. For from thence will He come to j udge the living and the dead. Learn then, this 
Prayer also which you will have to repeat.”163 
St. Cyprian  says, “Let us, therefore, beloved brethren, pray as God our Teacher has 
taught us. It is a loving and friendly prayer to beseech God with His word, to come up to 
His ears in the prayer of Christ. Let the Father acknowledge the words of His Son when we 
make our prayer, and let Him also who dwells within in our breast Himself dwell in our 
voice. And since we have Him as an Advocate with the Father for our sins, let us, when as 
sinners we petition on behalf of our sins, put forward the words of our Advocate. For since 
He says, that whatsoever we shall ask of the Father in His name, He will give us (John 
16:23), how much more effectually do we obtain what we ask in Christ’s name, if we ask 
for it in His prayer! (cf. John 14:6)”164 
932. Why did the Lord Christ bid us to pray the Lord’s Prayer in the plural? 
God bids us to love our neighbor, so we pray for fellow believers the same way we pray 
for non-believers. In so  doing, our will is in harmony with the will of God, who wills all 
people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim. 2:4). Even in his 
private room, the believer ought to pray in the name of the entire Church, because he is a 
member of the Church.  
St. John Chrysostom  says, “He teaches, moreover, to make our prayer common, on 
behalf of our brethren also. For He says not, ‘my Father, which art in Heaven,’ but, ‘our 
Father,’ offering up his supplications for the body in common, and nowhere looking to his 
own, but everywhere to his neighbor’s good.”165  
St. Augustine says, “You have begun to belong to a great family [by being baptized]. 
Under this Father, the lord and the slave are brethren; under this Father the general and the 
common soldier are brethren; under this Father the rich man and the poor are brethren. All 
 
163 St. Augustine of Hippo, Sermons on Selected Lessons of the New Testament 8.1 (NPNF I/6:284) amended. 
164 St. Cyprian of Carthage, Treatise 4: On the Lord’s Prayer 3 (ANF 5:448). 
165 St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew Homily 19.6 (NPNF I/10:131) amended.

Catechism of the Coptic Orthodox Church – Volume 2  
58 
Christian believers have various fathers on earth, some noble, some obscure; but they all 
call upon one Father which is in heaven … Therefore do they understand that they are 
brethren, seeing they have one Father. Now let not the lord disdain to have his slave for a 
brother, seeing the Lord Christ has vouchsafed to have him for a brother.”166 
In a similar vein St. Cyprian says in his commentary on the Lord’s Prayer: “Before all 
things, the Teacher of peace and the Master of unity would not have a prayer to be made 
singly and individually, as for one who prays to pray for himself alone. For we say not ‘My 
Father, which art in heaven,’ nor ‘Give me this day my daily bread;’ nor does ea ch one ask 
that only his debt should be forgiven him; nor does he request for himself alone that he may 
not be led into temptation, and delivered from evil. Our prayer is public and common; and 
when we pray, we pray not for one, but the whole people, becau se we the whole people are 
one. The God of peace and the Teacher of concord, who taught unity, willed that one 
should thus pray for all, even as He bore us all in one. This law of prayer the three children 
observed when they were shut up in the fiery furna ce, speaking together in prayer, and 
being of one heart in the agreement of the spirit; and this the faith of the sacred Scripture 
assures us, and in telling us how such as these prayed, gives an example which we ought to 
follow in our prayers, so that we may be such as they were: ‘Then these three,’ it says, ‘as if 
from one mouth sang a hymn, and blessed the Lord’ (Hymn of the Three Young Men, 
Dan.3:51 LXX). They spoke as if from one mouth, although Christ had not yet taught them 
how to pray … Thus, also w e find that the apostles, with the disciples, prayed after the 
Lord’s ascension: ‘They all,’ says the Scripture, ‘continued with one accord in prayer, with 
the women, and Mary who was the mother of Jesus and with His brethren’ (Acts 1:14).”167 
933. Why do we address God thus: “Our Father who art in Heaven”? 
In our prayers, as children of God, it is fitting for us to raise our hearts to heaven and 
entreat Him who is heavenly, eternal, and divine. 
St. Augustine says, “Parents sometimes when they have begotten on e, or two, or three 
children, fear to give birth to anymore, lest they reduce the rest to being beggars. But 
because the inheritance which He promises us is such as many may possess, and no one is 
left in poverty; therefore has He called into His family th e peoples of the nations, and the 
Only Son has numberless brethren; who say, ‘Our Father, which art in heaven’ (Matt. 6:9). 
Let us then consider, beloved, whose children we have begun to be; and let us live so as 
becomes those who have such a Father. See, how our Creator has condescended to be our 
Father!”168

25 
become in a special manner the temples of God when earthly thoughts cease to interrupt 
our continual remembrance of Him.”54 
Tertullian says, “Prayer is alone that which vanquishes God  [cf. Gen. 32:22–30; Matt. 
11:12]. But Christ has willed that it be operative for no  evil: He had conferred on it all 
its virtue in the cause of good. And so it  knows nothing save how to recall the  souls of the 
departed from the very path of death, to transform the weak, to restore the sick, to purge the 
possessed, to open prison-bars, to loose the bonds of the innocent. Likewise it washes away 
faults, repels temptations, extinguishes persecutions, consoles the faint -spirited, cheers the 
high-spirited, escorts travelers, appeases waves, makes  robbers stand aghast, nourishes 
the poor, governs the rich, upraises the fallen, arrests the falling, confirms the standing. 
Prayer is the wall of  faith: her arms and  missiles against the foe who keeps watch over us 
on all sides. And, so never walk we unarmed. By day, be we mindful of Station; by night, 
of vigil. Under the arms of  prayer guard we the standard of our General; await we 
in prayer the angel’s trump … What more then, touching the office of  prayer? Even the 
Lord Himself prayed; to whom be honour and virtue unto the ages of the ages!”55 
St. Hesychius of Jerusalem  says, “‘Oh, that I my request  may be fulfilled  before the 
Lord.’ Should my prayers ascend on high, my enemies would perish, and the righteous 
person would stand firm (Wisd . of Sol.  5:1); the net would be broken, and the bird would 
be liberated  and fly freely (Ps. 124:7) ; the oppressors would bow their heads , and the 
oppressed would rejoice (Matt. 5:10–12).” 
Second: Prayer propagates the spirit of inner joy. St. Cyril the Great says, “For it is, I 
affirm, the duty of those who set apart their lives for His service, not to be sluggish in their 
prayers, nor again to consider it as a hard and laborious  duty: but rather to rejoice, because 
of the freedom of access granted them by God; for He would have us converse with Him as 
sons with a  father. Is not this then a privilege worthy of being valued by us most highly? 
For suppose that some one of those possessed of great earthly power were easy of access to 
us, and were to permit us to converse with him with full license, should we not consider it 
as a reason for extraordinary rejoicing? What possible doubt can there be of this? When 
therefore God permits us  each one to offer our addresses unto Him for whatever we wish, 
and has set before those who fear Him an honor so truly great and worthy of their gaining, 
let all slothfulness cease that would lead men to an injurious silence therein; and rather let 
us draw near with praises, and rejoicing that we have been commanded to converse with the 
Lord and God of all, having Christ as our Mediator, who with God the Father grants us the 
accomplishment of our supplications. For the blessed Paul somewhere writes, ‘Grace be 
unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ ’ (2 Cor. 1:2) . 
And He somewhere Himself said to the holy apostles, ‘Hitherto you have asked nothing in 
 
54 St. Basil of Caesarea, Letters 1–185 2.4 (FOTC 13:9). 
55 Tertullian, On Prayer 29 (ANF 3:691).

36 
once draw near unto God, beseeching His aid, and crying out against those who resist His 
glory: just as also the mighty Moses did; for he said, ‘Arise, O Lord, and let Your enemies 
be scattered, and let all th ose who hate Your Name flee awa y’ (Num. 10:35). And the 
prayer also uttered by the holy apostles  … ‘For behold their threat enings,’ that is, prove 
their opposition to be in vain, and grant unto ‘Your servants, that with freedom of speech 
they may speak Your word.’”96 
914. Why did the Lord Christ pray? 
St. Cyril the Great says, “for what, forsooth, does He [Christ] pray, if He is full, and 
needs nothing that is the Father’s? To this we reply, that He permits Himself, in accordance 
with the manner of the dispensation in the flesh, to perform human actions whenever He 
wills, and as the season requires, without being liable to blame for so doing. For if He ate 
and drank, and is found partaking of sleep, what is there absurd, if also having humbled 
Himself to  our measure, and fulfilled human righteousness, He not unfitly offered up 
prayer?”97 
“All that Christ did was for our edification, and for the benefit of those who believe in 
Him; and by proposing to us His own conduct as a sort of pattern of the spiritua l mode of 
life, He would make us true worshippers. Let us see, therefore, in the pattern and example 
provided for us by Christ ’s acts, the manner in which we ought to make our supplications 
unto God. We must pray secretly and in concealment, and with no on e seeing us : … ‘ But 
you, when you pray, go into your inner room’ (Matt. 6:6). For we ought to pray, not 
seeking after glory, but ‘lifting up holy hands ’ (1 Tim. 2:8), while the soul, as it were, 
mounts aloft to the contemplation of God, withdrawing from al l tumult, and quitting 
worldly anxiety. And this we must do not with fickleness, nor with a listless feebleness; 
but, on the contrary, with earnestness and zeal, and a patience worthy of admiration: for 
you have heard that Jesus did not merely pray, but th at He also passed the night in this duty 
… Though divinely begotten as the Word by God the Father, yet He humbled Himself unto 
emptying, even to becoming our brother, by being made like unto us, and similar in all 
things to the inhabitants of the earth, si n only excepted. For having become like unto us 
from His exceeding gentleness and love to mankind, He disdains not human things: but sets 
before us His conduct as a type of goodness unto the end, that we may be earnest in 
following His footsteps.”98 
St. Cyprian says, “If He who was without sin prayed, how much more ought sinners to 
pray? And if He prayed continually, watching through the whole night with uninterrupted

45 
times daily, although their precise timing was not yet specified, being a well -established 
practice inherited by the  Church from Jewish tradition , which includes the prayers of the 
third, sixth, and ninth hours. Jungmann 124 believes that these prayers are based on  Daniel 
the prophet (Dan. 6:10) who was accustomed to go to his house, open his windows towards 
Jerusalem, and kneel to pray three times a day.  
The Didache does not mention the morning and night-time prayers, perhaps because the 
faithful would pray these communally, so there was no need to command the people to pray 
them. This is apparent  in the Didascalia’s commandment to bishops: “When you teach, 
command and remind the people, that they be constant in the assembly of the Church; so 
that you be not hindered, but that they be constantly assembled, that no one diminish the 
Church by not assembling,  and make smaller by a member the body of Christ.”125 The 
Didache mentions the Lord ’s prayer because while Christians were accustomed  to 
participate in the synagogues in singing psalms and in the Jewish prayers , they could not  
share the Lord’s prayer with them.  
The Acts of the Apostles describes the practice of praying the canonical hours in the 
early Church. Of the third hour we read: “For these are not drunk, as you suppose, since it 
is only the third hour of the day” (Acts 2:15). Of the sixth hour : “Peter went  up on the 
housetop to pray, about the sixth hour” (Acts 10:9). Of the ninth hour : “Now Peter and 
John went up together to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour” (Acts 3:1). And 
of the midnight prayer: “But at midnight Paul and Silas were prayin g and singing hymns 
to God, and the prisoners were listening to them” (Acts 16:25). 
St. Basil the Great says, “Prayer time should cover the whole of life, but since there is 
absolute need at certain intervals to interrupt the bending of the knee and the ch anting of 
psalms, the hours appointed for prayer by the saints should be observed. The mighty David 
says, ‘I rose at midnight to give praise to you for the judgments of your justification’  (Ps. 
119:62); and we find Paul and Silas following his example, for they praised God in prison 
at midnight (Acts 16:25). Then too, the same  Prophet says: ‘Evening and morning and at 
noon (Ps. 55:17). Moreover, the coming of the Holy Spirit took place at the third hour, as 
we learn in the Acts when , in answer to the Pharis ees who were jeering at the disciples 
because of the diversity of tongues, Peter said that they were not drunk who were speaking 
these words: ‘seeing that it is  the third hour’ (Acts 2:15). Again, the ninth hour recalls the 
Lord’s Passion, which took place  that we might live (Matt. 27:45; M ark 15:33–34). But, 
since David says: “Seven times a day I have given praise to you, for the judgments of your 
justice” (Ps. 119:164), and the times for prayer which have been mentioned do not make up 
this seven-fold apportionment, the mid-day prayer should be divided, one part being recited 
before the noon repast and the other afterward. In this way, the daily seven -fold praise of

of Notre Dame Press, 1959): p. 99.

24 
which abide in us, but with that craving and infirmity of the flesh which are not in Him, and 
have not His words abiding in them.  For to His words, at all events, belongs 
that prayer which He taught, and in which we say,  Our Father,  who art in  heaven 
(Matt. 6:9). Let us only not fall away from the words and meaning of this  prayer in our 
petitions, and whatever we ask, it shall be done unto us … But when His words abide only 
in the memory, and have no place in the life, the branch is not to be accounted as in the 
vine, because it draws not its life from the root.”51 
Abba Isaac, the disciple of St. Anthony,  says, “We sometimes ask for things opposed 
to our salvation and that we are most providentially refused our requests by Him who sees 
what is good for us with greater right and  truth than we can. And it is clear that this also 
happened to the teacher of the  Gentiles when he  prayed that the messenger of  Satan who 
had been for his good allowed by the Lord ’s will to buffet him, might be removed, 
saying: ‘For which I besought the Lord thrice that he might depart from me. And He said to 
me, My grace is sufficient for you, for strength is made perfect in weakness ’ (2 Cor. 12:8–
9).”52  
Pope Gregory the Great  says, “why is it that Paul three times besought the Lord and 
did not merit to be heard, but was told: My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made 
perfect in weakness  (2 Cor. 12:9). Did the great preacher not ask in the name of the Son? 
Then why didn’t he r eceive what he asked? … The Son’s name is Jesus. Jesus means 
‘saviour’ or ‘saving.’ One who asks in the Saviour’s name asks what pertains to actual 
salvation. If what he asks for is not for his good he is not asking the Father in Jesus’ name. 
Hence the Lord says to his apostles while they were still weak, Up to now you have asked 
nothing in my name  (John 16:24) … That is the reason too why Paul was not heard. If he 
had been freed from temptation it would not have been of help to his salvation … consider 
your requests, I beseech you, and see if you are asking in the name of Jesus, if you are 
asking for the joys of eternal salvation … Seek first the kingdom of God and his justice, and 
all these things will be given you as well (Matt. 6:33).”53 
901.  What are the effects of prayer? 
First: The soul is inflamed with the love of God. St. Basil the Great says, “Prayers, too, 
following reading, take hold upon a fresher and more vigorous soul already stirred to a 
longing for God. And prayer which imprints in the soul a clear conception of God is an 
excellent thing. This abiding of God in our memory is the indwelling of God.  Thus we

Abraham from these stones’ (Luke. 3:8). For the mystery of the calling of the Nations is 
manifested before through the prayer of Jacob.”260 
Fourth: The silent prayer of a pure heart: “We may come to the prayer of silence which 
Hannah, the mother of Samuel, prayed (1 Sam. 1:13). It was acceptable before God, it 
opened up her barren womb and caused her shame to depart, and she gave birth to a 
Nazirite and a priest (1 Sam. 1:10–16).”261 
947. What is the hidden (or secret) prayer to which the Lord Christ invites us?  
St. Clement of Alexandria says, “Prayer is, then, to speak more boldly, converse with 
God. Though whispering, consequently, and not opening the lips, we speak in silence, yet 
we cry inwardly. For God hears continually all the inward converse.”262 
St. Aphrahat says , “Again our Savior taught the prayer and said, ‘You should pray 
secretly to the Hidden One; He sees everything’ (Matt. 6:6). For he said, ‘Enter the inner 
chamber and pray secretly to your Fathe r, and the Father who sees in secret will reward 
you’ (Matt. 6:6). But why, my beloved, did our Savior teach and say, ‘Pray to your Father 
in secret with the door closed?’ I will explain this to you as much as I have understood. For 
he said, ‘Pray to your Father in secret with the door closed.’ What is the door that he said to 
close? If not your mouth, which is (the door to) the temple in which Christ dwells as the 
Apostle said, ‘You are the temple of the Lord’ (1 Cor. 3:16), for him to enter into your 
inner man, to this house, cleanse it from everything that is unclean, while the door, that is 
your mouth, is to be closed. If that was not so, how would you understand this matter? For 
if it happens to you that you were in a land, and there is no house and doo r, would you not 
pray in secret? Or if it happens to you again that you were on the top of a mountain, would 
you not pray?  
“And our Savior showed this that God knows the will of the heart and of the thought, 
just as our Lord said, ‘Your Father knows what you need before you ask Him’ (Matt. 6:8). 
It is written in the prophet Isaiah, ‘Before they who were chosen by me call, I will hear 
them, and before they make the cry I will answer them’ (Isa. 65:24). Isaiah said again about 
the wicked, ‘Even though you mu ltiply prayer I will not listen’ (Isa. 1:15). He said again, 
‘They may cry in my ears with a loud voice, but I shall not hear them’ (Ezek. 8:18). But he 
said this about deceitful prayer, which is not accepted. For you must hear with excellence 
all the words, then you will understand their power.”263

records.question: What name was he given at baptism?
records.answer: At baptism, St. Takla Haymanot was given the name **Fish Hazion**, which means "the Joy of Zion." This name reflects his early life and the blessings he received from God, as he was raised in a pious environment by his parents, who were devoted to the poor and the needy. His mother, Sarah, played a significant role in his upbringing, emphasizing the importance of charity and faith from a young age [1][2]. Later, after his encounter with the Archangel Michael, he was renamed Takla Haymanot, which signifies his new mission and dedication to a life of celibacy, prayer, and preaching [1].

lived a life of purity and chastity; and when his parents urged him to get 
married, he refrained, proclaiming his desire to live a celibate life . However, 
when they forced him to do so, he lived with his wife like brother and sister 
until she reposed in the Lord. Then, the metropolitan of Ethiopia ordained him 
as a priest. His mother reposed on the 22 nd of Mesra, and his father followed 
her after only four days. 
This young priest lived in his parent’s house for another seven years. Then, 
it happened one day when he went out to hunt animals, that the Archangel 
Michael appeared to  him and told him that such action is not befitting for a 
priest, but he should instead dedicate h is life to prayers, to the study of the 
Holy Bible and teaching. He told him also that God has granted him the gift of 
healing of the sick and performing miracles, and that his name from now on 
would not be Fish Hazion, but Takla Haymanot. It was also said that the Lord 
Jesus Christ put His hand on him and blessed him after calling him to the 
preaching work and promised to be with him and support him . The saint then 
distributed all his parents’ wealth on the poor , bid farewell to the inhabitants 
of his city, and set forth to preach. 
His Preaching and Monastic Ministry: 
St. Takla Haymanot set forth to the region of Katata, where its inhabitants 
worshipped the idols, the trees, and the sun. There, the people were stirred up 
against him, mainly that they heard the voice of the devil from the tree, their 
idol, seeking from them to send him away. As for him, he stood afar, faced the 
East, raised his hands, and prayed, asking God to destroy that tree. So, the tree 
was uprooted and moved toward the saint, and then the devil confessed 
publicly that he was leading the people to vanity. On his hands, God performed 
so many miracles, which caused many to believe and be baptized in the water 
of the River. The region’s prince was saddened by uprooting that tree because 
it was producing a high income for him. And, when he came to inspect it, he 
found out that the saint ordered to use its wood to build a church. However, the 
prince fell ill , and the saint healed him in the name of the Holy Trinity . This 
miracle made him, his wife Acrocina and his three sons, get baptized , and the 
children's names were replaced with Christian ones. Together with them, many 
other people were also baptized . His ascetic life merged with his preaching 
work, so he was a true hermit who spent most of the forty days fasting period 
in the wilderness in a robust ascetic way, to come b ack to his brethren and 
children to care for them with stronger love. 
The people got so attached to him, but in obedience to the Lord’s 
commandment, he had to move from one city to another in Ethiopia, to preach 
the Gospel, and to oppose the idol worship a nd the works of sorcery . So, he 
faced significant troubles and opposition; but God supported him with the

her the good news that she would be granted a child who would be a cause of 
blessing to so many.  
In the morning, she put on the royal attire and was escorted to the king who 
greatly rejoiced to see her . He rewarded the soldiers with precious gifts and 
sought from them to bring her to the idols’ temple to hold an official celebration 
of their marriage. The king came into the temple, worshipped before the idols; 
while she stood waiting for God to rescue her . Then, suddenly a lightning, 
thunder and earthquakes took place; and the Archangel Michael came down to 
carry her to the church, where she used to pray with her husband the priest. 
On seeing how splendid she looked in her royal attire with her face covered 
with a veil; her husband assumed that she was one of the royal household. She 
revealed her identity to her husband and told him about all that God did for 
her. They both glorified God and gave Him thanks to His great mercies. In the 
evening, Sarah saw a lighted pillar in the middle of her house, with its top in 
heaven and embracing many dive rse birds; and toward which many peoples 
and kings looked with marvel. The priest, on the other hand, saw as though a 
shining sun was underneath his bed, surrounded by many stars that shone on 
the whole universe. In that very night, Sarah conceived the blessed child, who 
was born on the 24th of the month of Kiahk. 
His Childhood: 
In the biography of St. Takla Haymanot, many events were mentioned about 
God’s work within him during his childhood. Among these was that: after his 
parents sold all that his mother Sarah brought from the palace of the king from 
splendid attire, gold, silver, and pearls and distributed their price on the poor , 
the land went through a severe famine, and so many people were suffering . 
The mother was crying bitterly longing to give something more to the poor . 
The suckling baby, seeing her tears, pointed his little hand toward a small cup 
of flour and touched it . The flour started to flow heavily from that cup . His 
mother hastened to bring all that she had in her kitchen for the suckling to 
touch with his hand to let her have plenty to give to the poor.  The little child 
was baptized, and called by the name ‘Fish Hazion ,’ (meaning: the Joy of 
Zion), to be raised in a life of piety and worship with a spirit of asceticism, 
along with humility and love for everyone. 
His Ordination: 
Having reached 20 years of age, the metropolitan of Ethiopia Abba ‘Girguis 
II’ ordained him as a deacon in the days of the 75 th Pope, St.  Cyril III of 
Alexandria (1235-1243). During the ordination, the metropolitan kissed him, 
declared that he would be beloved by God and that the angel of the Lord would 
always accompany him with a sword of fire in his hand . St. Takla Haymanot

miracles and the healings He performed through him. 
Besides his preaching work, he lived as a Father to so many monks . In the 
monastery which the sain t founded in the Amhara region, he practiced the 
monastic life with the spirit of worship and watching the nights, in addition to 
serving the others and ministering to the poor . The monks of the area 
considered him as an angel and not as a normal human bei ng. The monastery 
turned into a center of preaching. It was said that the Abbot of that monastery 
died, and he was bitterly mourned by all . Here, St. Takla Haymanot came to 
where the corpse was and prayed to God, who raised the monastery ’s Abbot 
from the dead. The nephew of the risen man was a priest, and he came rushing 
to cry at the feet of the saint seeking his forgiveness. He confessed to him that 
he used to envy his uncle on what God has granted him of gifts, and how badly 
he was aspiring to occupy his  place as the Abbot of the monastery after his 
death. And, asked the saint to pray on his behalf, and commended him for his 
holy life and his love even for those envious people. 
When the saint felt that temporal glory would chase him after raising that 
monastery’s Abbot from the dead, he cried out to the Lord to take him away 
from that place. The Archangel Michael advised him to go to the monastery of 
St. Istifanos (Steven), headed by ‘Iyasus Mo’a’ ( =Jesus overcomes) . He 
forsook the region of Amhara, until he reached the river, where the angel 
walked along with him on the water to reach that monastery. 
St. Takla Haymanot dedicated his time to worship and making metanoias 
with incredible perseverance that the Lord allow ed him to see the heavenly 
Jerusalem and the thrones of glory prepared for those who strive. There, he 
heard a voice calling his name, telling him that he would be counted among 
the 24 priests and was given a golden censor to raise incense with them, and to 
praise the Lord along with them . From that monastery , he moved to the 
monastery of Abuna Aregawi on the high mountain of Debre Damo. There, he 
met with Abbot Yoĥannes (John), the Abbot of the monastery and the spiritual 
mentor of Iyasus Moʹa. Abbot Yoĥannes clothed St. Takla Haymanot with the 
monastic Great Eskeem, and he remained there for 12 years practicing the 
ascetic life. Then, after bidding the Abbot of the monastery and the brethren 
farewell, they tied him to a rope to bring him down from the monastery on the 
top of the mountain to the valley below. However, during that process, the rope 
was torn, and everybody assumed that the saint would fall to his death . But, 
behold! They watched how amazing wings emerged out of the saint’s back to 
let him fly and get down safely. That is why he is often portrayed like a Cherub 
with six wings. Then, the saint kept moving from one monastery to another; 
and the power of God kept working with him and within him.  
It was also said that he went to Jerusalem, where he met with the 78th Pope 
of Alexandria, St. Gabriel III (12 68-1271); he got the blessing of the Holy

passages.text:
365 
 
Ĥabib was a first -class ecclesiastical man who elaborately knew by heart all 
the Church hymns and sang them with the spirit of prayer in a very touching 
voice. With that beginning, Yousef Ĥabib became the teacher of the Church’s 
young men and boys and let them absorb the spirit of the Fathers . He raised 
them on the love of the church and her hymns. Then, when the church came to 
have a cantor, her beautiful choir of deacons and her affairs started to settle 
down. Yousef Ĥabib withdrew himself in humility and self-denial and shifted 
his whole effort towards a new field to revive our ecclesiastical heritage.  
Yousef Ĥabib, for a long time, has been fond of the biographi es of the 
Saints, in particular of those whose fragrant life stories had not been published 
before. He started to travel to the desert monasteries to search in their libraries 
treasures about what was hidden, and he brought to light tens of biographies 
and rare stories. He also used to research in the libraries of the Coptic Museum 
and the library of the Patriarchate, etc.  He even purchased a permanent train 
travel permit to go back and forth to Cairo twice a week for that purpose . He 
used to translate, res earch in the biographies of the Saints and their sayings , 
then returned home to publish them in small booklets, to the benefit of ministry, 
and for the improvement of the souls. 
In his extreme asceticism, he used to spend all his retirement income on 
these tasks with joy, and save nothing of it for himself . The many books and 
booklets he published on his own did not bring him any funds. He always lived 
poor without any possessions, ascetic , and a hermit in his appearance, food, 
drink, and attire. And, in this, he lived until he departed from this world. 
With the establishment of the church of Abba Takla Haymanot  in the 
borough of Ibrahimieh, Alexandria; he considered it his responsibility and 
without hesitation, he took upon himself to minister in the new ch urch. In all 
the Holy Liturgies and eves, he carried out the duties of the cantor and the 
deacon, with a steadfast spirit and self-denial. 
It so happened once, during raising the evening incense, while the church 
was at its beginning, and her books were no t complete; sometimes, they did 
not find a Holy Bible to read the Gospel of the Prime hour in Arabic. So, he 
simply took the Coptic Katamarus ( Καταμερος) book and read to the people 
the Arabic Gospel, directly translating it from Coptic to Arabic.  
His Life Style: 
He lived by himself, dwelt alone, and always he would say: “My 
supplication from my Lord Christ, is to give me the great grace to continue 
walking on my feet until the day of my departure from this world. I do not want 
to burden anybody with serving me or looking after me.” God granted him his 
wish, for he was never inflicted by any disease which would make him in need 
of help from anyone. His firm principle of life was to refrain from having any

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 218
passages.text:
218 
 
her in her small cell until the day she  would depart. She remained there for 
only two weeks, then she became ill and delivered her soul to God, leaving for 
us a great living example of the e levated work of God within the life of 
humans, no matter how evil or defiled their lives may be. 
 
TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. 
St. Takla Haymanot occupies a prominent standing in the Ethiopian Church 
as being one of the pillars of the Ethiopian monastic life . He lived during the 
years 1215-1313 and was the cause of salvation to so many . His father, the 
priest Tsega Zeab (=Gift of Faith), was married to a charming and rich girl by 
the name of Egzie Haraya ( =Choice of God) or Sarah  in Hebrew. They both 
lived a life of piety, loving the poor and the needy. Not having any children, 
Sarah sought from her husb and to distribute all their possessions on the poor 
and to release all their slaves and maidservants . After asking her not to have 
them act in a rush  on that matter,  her husband , the priest , found her still 
persistent in her position. So, he rejoiced in he r counsel and did according to 
her heart’s desire. The slaves and the maidservants were intensely grieved, for 
they used to feel as members of the household , and some of them sought to 
remain with them in the house as brothers and sisters, which they did. 
When the pagan Ma tolomy became the king of Ethiopia, he started to 
persecute the Christians. He sent his soldiers everywhere around to apply their 
acts of violence against the Christians . One of the soldiers reached the house 
of the priest and planned to kill him with his spear. But, the priest managed to 
flee from his ho me and dived into a lake . The soldier stood by on the shore , 
waiting for him to come out of the water to kill him. After spending a long time 
waiting, the soldier assumed that the priest ha d already drowned. However, it 
happened that when the priest dived in the lake, he found the Archangel 
Michael covering him as though in a tent . Later on, when he came out of the 
water, he found that his wife was taken as a captive and the church was 
devastated. He then cried bitterly. 
It happened that when the soldiers realized how beautiful the wife Sarah 
was, they brought her up to their king as a precious gift . He ordered them to 
keep her in one of his houses and adorn her with gold, silver, expensive jewelry, 
and magnificent attire. On the other hand, she abstained from the superb food, 
and her tears never ceased to flow. By night, when all went to sleep, she took 
off the precious attire and put on her simple garment, prayed to God seeking 
salvation fro m that evil situation . And, she asked the intercession of the 
Archangel Michael, whose feasts she used to celebrate every month, by giving 
many gifts to the poor. Then, God sent his archangel to comfort her and to give

passages.text:
79 
 
the Great. He practiced the life of solitude in the Western Desert, in the  
province of ‘El-Ashmonein.' He lived in a cave in which he shot himself in to 
contemplate. Despite his strict asceticism, he did not cease to practice the 
handwork to give to the poor. He also cared to counsel the brethren, and God 
granted him the gift of  performing miracles. In other words, his solitude was 
founded on an open heart full of love for God and men. His disciple ‘Ephraim’ 
gave us a concise account of his life. 
His Life as a Monk: 
The saint was born to Christian parents; they raised him on the fear of the 
Lord. He grew loving the life of seclusion and contemplation, together with 
his love for the needy. 
While still a young man, he spent a lot of time among the monks and was 
trained on the ascetic life and the handwork to be able to give alms to the poor. 
When he became a monk, his love for solitude grew stronger that he lived in a 
very dark cave, where God granted him a fountain of water to drink from. He 
trained himself on fasting, by eating once a day in summer and once every two 
days in winter . He practiced the perpetual prayers and was making 300 
metanoias by day and 300 by night until his skin stuck to his bones and came 
to be as a burnt stick. 
A Spiritual Center: 
Despite his great love for the life of solitude, he did not shut off his heart 
nor his cave in the face of his brethren. But his dwelling place turned into a 
center of spiritual radiation. The elder monks residing on the mountain used to 
come to seek his counsel, and he used to inflame their hearts with longing for 
the Christian perfection in the Lord. 
His Prophesying About the Death of the King: 
His disciple once saw him sad, and on asking him about the reason, the saint 
told him that on that day, the soul of emperor Theodosius the Great was sought, 
and the bonds of the State order w ere about to come apart. The disciple made 
a note of the prophecy date, and after some time, when he descended to the 
world, he came to know that the emperor has died on that exact day. 
Examples of His Miracles: 
1- A priest once came to him inflicted with a s kin disease that exposed the 
bone of his forehead. And, despite the persistence of his disciple in seeking 
from the saint to come out and pray for the sick priest, he did not pay 
attention to him. Finally, he explained to his disciples that, because the 
priest has defiled the house of God by adultery and taking the church money 
to spend on his evil desires, he had no liberty to seek healing from God. 
Later on, he had compassion on him and asked his disciples to tell the priest

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 294
passages.text:
294 
 
barefooted on the live coal. The saint did not hesitate to take his sandals off 
and walked steadily on the live coal, as though on a lawn grass. Then, he started 
to rebuke the governor, that he should confess the Lord Christ who can turn 
the live coal into dew. The governor, however, accused him of sorcery.  
Finally, when the saint entered into a debate with the governor , he ordered 
to cut his head off, in Via Labicana, 3 miles away from Rome . The Western 
Church celebrates the feast of the martyr Tiburtius on the 11th of August. 
 
TIGRIUS, THE PRIEST, ST. 
This saint’s name is bound to that of Eutropius the reader; both of them had 
suffered great tribulations on account of their friendship to St. John 
Chrysostom (349-407 AD). St. Tigrius was a priest in Constantinople and a 
close friend of the archbishop John Chrysostom. Tigrius initially used to work 
as a slave in a house of one of the elites and they made him eunuch . Later on, 
owing to his faithfulness and piety, his master rewarded him by giving him his 
freedom. St. Tigrius had an exalted love toward the poor and he led a holy life 
that made him loved by everyone . Then, he was ordained as a priest; despite 
being eunuch1. As a priest, he showed an intense zeal in shepherding his flock 
and great love toward the poor and the strangers. St. Tigrius attended the Oak 
Tree Council, which condemned his friend, the archbishop John Chrysostom. 
And, after the later was sent into exile, the governor Optatius who was a pagan, 
called him and made him taste intense sufferings, in an attempt to please 
empress Eudoxia. Accusing him and Eutropius, of being trouble -makers and 
that they were behind burning the magnificent cathedral down . He was so 
violently whipped that his bones were exposed, his body was combed by sharp 
iron combs, and was finally exiled to Mesopotamia. 
 [Fr. Tadros Y Malaty: St. John Chrysostom, 1980, pp. 98-100]  
 
TIKHON, BISHOP OF AMATHUS, ST. 
St. Tikhon (Tychon) is considered one of the early bishops of the city of 
Amathus. That city was located where the city of Limassol is now on the 
southern coast of Cyprus. He was a man of the 5th century, and the inhabitants 
of the island honored him as being ‘The Wonder -Maker’ and considered him 
as ‘The Intercessor of the Vine-dressers’, for which the island is famous…

MARY (The martyr) 
This saint was born in Atrib. Later on, she got married to a good man 
called Theodore and gave birth to a son, whom they called Sergius. When her 
son went to the governor Kyriacos and confessed h is Christianity, the 
governor tortured him, brought the statue of an idol, and ordered him to 
worship it. The young man, instead, kicked the statue and it fell down 
shattering into pieces. Before such a scene, the governor Kyriacos instantly 
believed in Christianity, saying, “A god, who cannot save himself, how could 
he save others? ” The minister Ohius then came forward and took over 
torturing Serguis with fire and other means. When Serguis’ mother and sister 
arrived at the torturing spot, they kept weeping for seeing him in that manner. 
However, that minister ended up having Serguis’ head cut off by the sword. 
His mother, Mary, his father, and his sister then came forward and 
confessed the name of the Lord Christ, and had their heads cut off by the 
sword too. They all received the crowns of martyrdom on the 13th of Amshir. 
 [Female Martyrs of Christianity, p. 91] 
 
MATHOY, FATHER

It happened that the elder Mathoy (Mathos) once came out of Raythu to go 
to Magdelon with his brother. The bishop of the area took hold of him and 
ordained him as a priest. Afterward, while they were having dinner together, 
the bishop said to him, “Forgive me, father, I know that you did not want 
that, but I dared to do it to be blessed through you.” The elder Mathoy 
humbly answered, “To some extent, my mind did wish it, however, 
something was disturbing me, that I do not want to get separated from my 
brother because I am not used to do my prayers alone.” The bishop  told him, 
“If you think he is worthy, I may ordain him as a priest too.” Fr. Mathoy 
answered, “I do not know if he is worthy or not; all I know is that he is much 
better than me.”

records.question: من هو الأنبا موسى الأسود؟
records.answer:
الأنبا موسى الأسود هو أحد القديسين البارزين في التاريخ المسيحي، وقد وُلد بين عامي 330 و340 م. وُصف بأنه كان من قبيلة من قبائل البربر، وكان في بداية حياته يعيش حياة شريرة، حيث كان عبدًا لرجل يعبد الشمس، وعُرف بأنه كان رئيسًا لعصابة من قطاع الطرق. كان يتمتع بقوة بدنية كبيرة، مما ساعده في أعمال النهب والسطو، حتى أنه كان يسرق الخراف ويذبحها بسهولة، مما يدل على حياته المليئة بالشرور والرذائل، حيث قيل إنه "لا توجد رذيلة لم يكملها" في تلك الفترة من حياته [1].

لكن بعد فترة من حياته، بدأ موسى يشعر بالندم على أفعاله الشريرة، وكان يرفع وجهه إلى الشمس طالبًا أن يعرف الإله الحقيقي. قاده هذا البحث إلى برية شيهيت، حيث التقى بالقديس إيسيذورُس، الذي أصبح مرشده الروحي. اعترف موسى بكل خطاياه أمامه، وبدأ في رحلة التوبة، حيث أُعمد وتقبل التعليم الروحي [1][2].

بعد فترة من الزمن، طلب موسى أن يصبح راهبًا، وقد تم توجيهه من قبل القديس إيسيذورُس إلى القديس مقاريوس الكبير، الذي علمه حياة الرهبنة. كان موسى معروفًا بتوبته الصادقة، حيث اعترف بجميع خطاياه علانية في الكنيسة، ورأى القديس مقاريوس كيف أن ملاكًا كان يمسح خطاياه من لوح أسود حتى أصبح اللوح أبيضًا [1][2].

تُعتبر حياة الأنبا موسى الأسود مثالًا قويًا على التوبة والرحمة الإلهية، حيث تحول من حياة الشر إلى حياة القداسة، وأصبح قديسًا يُحتفى به في الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية.

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 116
passages.text: ✞ موسى الأسود الشهيد نشأته نكاد لا نعرف شيئًا عن ماضيه قبل توبته غير أنه كان أسود اللون، ويبدو أنه كان من قبيلة من قبائل البربر. وكانت حياته شريرة حتى قيل أنه لا توجد رذيلة لم يكملها. أما عن ميلاده فهو ما بين سنة 330 و 340 م ويبدو أنه كان عبدًا لشيخ قبيلة تعبد الشمس، لكن من فرط شروره طرده سيده، فاشتغل بأعمال النهب والسطو والقتل. وكان ذا جسم ضخم جبار يساعده على ذلك، وقيل أنه بسبب هذه المؤهلات صار رئيسًا لعصابة قطاع طرق. وكمثال على قوته البدنية أنه في أحد الأيام عبر النهر وسرق خروفين من راعي غنم وذبحهما وعبر بهما ثانية إلى الشاطئ الآخر للنهر. إيمانه بالسيد المسيح مع كل ما كان يفعله من شرور كان يرفع وجهه ويخاطب الشمس كالإله الحقيقي طالبًا أن يعر ِّفه ذاته، فسمع صوتًا يرشده أن يذهب إلى هذه البرية ليلتقي برهبان برية شيهيت وكانت شهرتهم في ذلك الوقت ذائعة جدًا. ذهب إليها حاملاً سيفه وتقابل مع القديس ايسيذورُس قس القلالي خارجًا من قلايته ليذهب إلى الكنيسة، فارتعب من منظره. فسأله الشيخ: "ماذا تريد يا أخي هنا؟" أجابه موسى: " قد سمعت أنك عبد الله الصالح، ومن أجل هذا هربت وأتيت إليك لكي ما يخلصني الإله الذي خلصك ". وكان يطلب منه بإلحاح وخشوع: " أريد أن أكون معك، ولو أني قد صنعت خطايا كثيرة وشرورًا عظيمة ". أخذ يسأله عن حياته، فاعترف له بكل ما صنع من شرور. ولما رأى أنبا ايسيذورُس صراحته أخذ يعلمه ويعظه كثيرًا بكلام الله وكلمه عن الدينونة العتيدة، وتركه لتأملاته. أخذ موسى يذرف الدموع الغزيرة، إذ كره الشر وعزم على التخلص منه، وكان الندم الحار يجتاح نفسه ويُقلق نومه مثل شبح مخيف. جاء إلى أنبا ايسيذورُس وركع أمامه واعترف بصوتٍ عالٍ بشروره وجرائمه في انسحاق يدعو إلى الشفقة وسط دموع غزيرة، فاصطحبه إلى الأنبا مقاريوس الذي وضعه تحت رعايته وأخذ يعلمه ويرشده برفقٍ، ثم منحه نعمة العماد، وسلمه إلى أنبا ايسيذورُس لكي يعلّمه. رهبنته بعد مدة طلب موسى من الأب ايسيذورُس أن يصير راهبًا، فأخذ ايسيذورُس يشرح له متاعب حياة الرهبنة من جهة تعب البرية ومحاربات الشياطين والاحتياجات الجسدية، وقال له: "الأفضل لك يا ابني أن تذهب إلى أرض مصر لتحيا هناك". وكان هذا على سبيل اختبار موسى، لكن بعد أن رأى ثباته وصدق نيته أرسله ثانية إلى القديس مقاريوس الكبير أب البرية. اعترف موسى علانية في الكنيسة بجميع خطاياه وقبائحه الماضية. وكان القديس مقاريوس أثناء الاعتراف يرى لوحًا عليه كتابة سوداء، وكلما اعترف موسى بخطية مسحها ملاك حتى إذ انتهى الاعتراف وجد اللوح أبيضًا كله. بعد ذلك وعظه الأنبا 580

passages.text: يحجبه عن العمل الكنسي خاصة الحفاظ على الإيمان المستقيم. هذا ما أدركه فالنس الأريوسي، إذ شعر بالدور الرئيسي الذي يقوم به قادة الفكر الرهباني في هذا الشأن، لذا نُفي القديس إيسيذورس إلى إحدى الجزر بمصر، مع المقاريْن وهيراكليد والأنبا بموا وغيرهم، من أجل دفاعهم عن الإيمان بلاهوت السيد المسيح. رجل صلاة لعل سر ِّ القوة في حياة هذا الأب الروحي حتى نال هذه القامة العظيمة، هو حبه للصلاة، فقد اهتم في السنوات الأولى من رهبنته أن يعتكف في القلاية لا يكف عن الصلاة حتى أثناء عمله اليدوي. كثيرًا ما كان يقول: "لنجتهد في الصلاة فيهرب العدو، ولنجتهد في التأمل في الله فننتصر". مع حبه الشديد للصلاة كان لا يكف عن العمل، فكان لا يتوقف عنه حتى عندما تقد َّم في السن، ولما طُلِبَ منه أن يستريح قليلاً أجاب: "لو حرقوا إيسيذورس ونثروا رماده في الهواء، فإن هذا لا يكفي تقديمه للرب كعلامة عرفان للجميل، مقابل ما صنعه يسوع المسيح بمجيئه إلى العالم". حب ُّه لخلاص الآخرين اشتهر الأب إيسيذورس بما وُهِبَ له من نعمة فريدة في الحلم والاهتمام بخلاص الآخرين، لهذا متى وُجد إنسان قد يأس الكل منه وأرادوا طرده، يحتضنه ويهتم به يقو ِّمه بحلمه وصبره. لعلنا نذكر كيف كان الأنبا موسى الأسود وهو مُحارَب بالزنا بعنف، يجد في إيسيذورس القلب المُت ِّسِع بالحب، ففي ليلة واحدة انطلق أنبا موسى من قلايته التي على الصخرة "بترا" إلى قلاية أبيه إيسيذورس التي بالقرب من الكنيسة ليزوره إحدى عشرة مرة، والأب يستقبله ببشاشة ويرد له رجاءه في الرب. مرة أخرى إذ اشتدت الحرب جدًا بالأنبا موسى حتى كاد يفقد رجاءه، فلم يحتمل البقاء في القلاية، أصعده معه إلى سطح القلاية وطلب منه أن ينظر إلى الغرب ليرى جمعًا من الشياطين في حالة هياج شديد يستعدون للهجوم، ثم طلب منه أن ينظر إلى الشرق ليجد جمعًا أكثر من الملائكة القديسين والجنود السمائيين في مجد بهي واقفين ليسندوا المجاهدين، فامتلأ أنبا موسى رجاء. موهبة إخراج الشياطين 417

passages.text: أخرى في السنة الثالثة قام أبا بيهور بالعمل نفسه وعاد إلى ديره كما فعل سابقًا دون أن يتقاضى أجرة. بينما كان الطوباوي فرحًا لأنه غُبن في أجرته امتدت يد المسيح على ذلك البيت، فحمل المزارع أجرة الطوباوي وصار يتنقل بين الأديرة يبحث عنه، وبعد صعوبة ومشقة وجده فسقط عند قدميه وتوسل إليه أن يقبل الأجرة التي له. أما القديس فرفضها قائلاً: "ربما تكون في حاجة إليها، أما أنا فالله يهبني أجرتي"، وإذ ألحّ الرجل متوسلاً أن يقبل الأجرة سمح له القديس أن يقدمها للكنيسة. ❖ كان أبا بيهور يأكل وهو يمشي، فسأله أحد الإخوة: "لماذا تأكل هكذا يا أبتي؟" قال: " لا أريد أن يكون الطعام ،مهنة إنما يكون ًعملا اًثانوي ". ❖ انعقد في الإسقيط اجتماع بسبب أخٍ أخطأ فتكلم الآباء أمام أبا بيهور فظل صامتًا. ثم نهض وخرج يحمل على كتفه كيسًا مملوءًا رملاً، ووضع قليلاً من الرمل في سلة وحملها أمامهم. فلما سأله الآباء عن سبب تصرفه هذا، قال: " هذا الكيس ءالملي بالرمل هو خطاياي الكثيرة العدد قد تركتها ورائي لئلا أحزن بسببها ،فأبكي أما خطية أخي فهي أمامي انشغل بها إذ أنا ،أدينه مع أنه لا يليق بي أن أفعل ،هكذا إنما يجب بالأحرى أن أضع خطاياي نصب عيني واهتم بها اًمتضرع إلى الله أن يغفر لي ". عندئذ قام الآباء قائلين: بالحقيقة هذا هو سبيل الخلاص. ❖ هذا التصرف شبيه بتصرف القديس أنبا موسى الأسود الذي حمل كيسًا مملوءًا رملاً على ظهره، وكان به ثقب والرمال تتسرب منه، قائلاً إنه وضع خطاياه وراء ظهره لئلا ينظرها وقد جاء ليدين أخاه. passages.text: بإيست برانزوك: ] والطقس في الكنيسة هي أدوات قوية وجميلة تجعلنا ملتصقين بالله، وتسمح لنا بنظرة خاطفة للحياة السماوية. استخدم الآباء أنغام موسيقية متنوعة، وطقوس متباينة خلال الفصول المختلفة من السنة، خلال الأصوام والأعياد تسمح لنا بالتلامس الروحي للصلوات والأسرار التي تقدمها عبادتنا. هذا الأمر واضح على وجه الخصوص في سبت الفرح )ليلة أبوغلامسيس( حيث يجتمع المؤمنون معًا ويسهرون بالقرب من قبر المسيح طوال الليل، يشهدون لنصرة الصليب على ظلمة الهاوية. نرى في الصلاة الأولى التي يتغن َّى بها الكاهن على باب الهيكل الملكي كما أمام القبر، يترنم بالمزمور 151 : "أنا الصغير بين إخوتي". وكأن الكنيسة تشرح لأبنائها الذين يمارسون طقس سبت الفرح، أنه وإن كان مظهر الصليب فيه ضعف المسيح بخضوعه للموت، إلا أنه هو الذي يُحَط ِّم الموت. عندئذ يقف المؤمنون ويطوفون في موكب داخل الكنيسة، يمسكون الشموع ليُعلِنوا أن المسيح هو النور الذي يبدد الظلمة. كل لحظة من لحظات هذه الليلة هي درس حيّ يُلهب قلوب المؤمنين، ويقوّي إيمانهم. ننطلق من كل قصص الخلاص )سوسنّة، والثلاث فتية في أتون النار، ودانيال في جب الأسود...( إلى تسابيح رائعة تعلن قوة السيد المسيح ولاهوته، مثل لحن "أجيوس أثاناتوس ناي نان" أي "أيها الخالد ارحمنا"، حتى نبلغ إلى السماء بالقراءات والألحان التي في سفر الرؤيا. هكذا تنطلق الكنيسة بأبنائها من قبر الجمعة العظيمة إلى أورشليم السماوية، واحتفالات القيامة 134

passages.text: الجديدة بواسطة الماء والروح وذلك كخلقة العالم، إذ كان روح الله يرف على المياه 383 . [ ب فلك نوح والطوفان: هنا يظهر الماء كأداة إدانة للعالم الشرير، وإن كان الفلك وسط المياه يظهر كأداة خلاص لنوح وعائلته حيث يدخل بهم إلى عالم جديد. نظر الرسول بطرس إلى الطوفان والفلك، فرأى صورة رمزية حيّة للخلاص في المعمودية ) 1 بط 3 : 18 - 21 .( ويقول القديس جيروم : ] حمامة الروح القدس نحو نوح بعد أن خرج الطائر الأسود )الغراب( وصارت كما لو كانت متجهة نحو المسيح في الأردن 384 [. ج عبور البحر الأحمر والسحابة: يقول القديس بولس: "فإني لست أريد أيُها الأخوة أن تجهلوا أن آباءَنا جميعهم كانوا تحت السحابة، وجميعهم اجتازوا في البحر، وجميعهم عُمدوا لموسى في السحابة وفي البحر" ) 1 كو 10 : 1 - 2 .( وكأن الرسول بولس قد رأى كنيسة العهد القديم في أيام موسى النبي قد اجتازت المعمودية رمزيًا. فالبحر يشير إلى جرن المياه، والسحابة التي ظللتهم تشير إلى الروح القدس، كقول الكتاب: "أرسلت روحك فغطّاهم" )خر 15 : 10 .( د مياه "مارة": في طقس الكنيسة القبطية يصلي الكاهن أثناء تقديس مياه المعمودية، قائلاً: "أنت أمرت الصخرة الصماء فأفاضت الماء لشعبك )عد 29 : 11 (، وأيضًا المياه المُرّة نقلتها إلى مياه حلوة..." هكذا تتطلع الكنيسة إلى تحويل مياه "مارة" المُرّة إلى مياه حلوة كرمز للمعمودية. ه. عبور يشوع نهر الأردن: في الليتورجيا القبطية وأيضًا الإثيوبية الخاصة بتقديس مياه المعمودية، بعد الإشارة إلى المياه الخاصة ببدء الخليقة والطوفان وعبور البحر الأحمر ومياه مارة وصخرة حوريب، ورد الحديث عن مجموعة أخرى هي: "عبور يشوع بن نون نهر الأردن، وقبول ذبيحة إيليا بالماء ) 1 مل 18 : 33 - 36 (، وشفاء نعمان السرياني في نهر الأردن ) 2 مل 5 : 14 .( وقد ورد الحديث عنها في أعمال العلامة أوريجينوس ومن بعده أخذها الآباء عنه، لذا يرى دانيلو أن هذه المجموعة إسكندرانية المنشأ، نشأت عن التقليد الليتورجي لكنيسة الإسكندرية، وإن ما جاء عنها في أعمال أوريجينوس لا يمثل رأيًا شخصيًا بل يعكس فكر كنيسته وتقليدها في ذلك الحين 385 . يقول أوريجينوس إنه بعد عبور نهر الأردن سقطت أريحا إشارة إلى هلاك الإنسان القديم الشرير 386 . كما يقول أيضًا إن من يذهب إلى الأردن لا يهرب إليه في صمت، بل يحمل معه الأبواق التي تعلن الأسرار الإلهية، كارزًا بالبوق السماوي 387 . و قبول ذبيحة إيليا على جبل الكرمل )1 مل 18 : 33 - 38 :( يقول القديس أثناسيوس الرسولي: ] )إيليا أعوانه وصحبه فحفروا خندقًا مثالاً للمعمودية، وأن يصبّوا على ذلك كله ماءًا فصبّوا، وقال لهم ثنوا فثنوا، وثلثوا فثلثوا قياسًا لتثليث غطسات المعمودية، وامتلأ الخندق ماءً. ثم صلى إلى الرب أن يستجيبه بنارٍ، فنزلت نار من السماء فأكلت القربان

records.question: من هو مارمرقس الرسول؟
records.answer:
مارمرقس الرسول هو أحد الشخصيات البارزة في التاريخ المسيحي، وهو كاتب إنجيل مرقس، الذي يُعتبر أحد الأناجيل الأربعة في العهد الجديد. وُلد مارمرقس في القيروان (حاليًا في ليبيا) من أبوين يهوديين، وكان له صلة قرابة مع الرسول بطرس، حيث يُعتقد أنه كان ابن عم زوجته أو ابن عمتها. نشأ في أسرة متدينة، وكان له دور كبير في الكنيسة الأولى، حيث كان من بين السبعين رسولًا الذين اختارهم السيد المسيح للخدمة، وقد شهد العديد من الأحداث المهمة في حياة المسيح، بما في ذلك عرس قانا الجليل[7][10].

مارمرقس هو أيضًا مؤسس الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية، حيث يُعتبر أول من بشر بالمسيحية في مصر. وفقًا للتقاليد، أسس الكنيسة في الإسكندرية، حيث كان له دور كبير في نشر الإيمان المسيحي وتعليم الناس. يُعرف عنه أنه كان له تأثير كبير على الحياة الروحية والثقافية في مصر، وقد أسس المدرسة اللاهوتية الشهيرة في الإسكندرية، التي أسهمت في تعليم العديد من العلماء واللاهوتيين[4][10].

استشهد مارمرقس في الإسكندرية، ويُحتفل بعيد استشهاده في 29 هاتور، حيث يُعتبر رمزًا للشجاعة والإيمان. يُرمز له بالأسد، وهو رمز يُستخدم في العديد من الثقافات للإشارة إلى قوته وجرأته في الدفاع عن الإيمان[4][8].
