Butler, May 5. ✞ هيلاري أسقف بواتييه القديس St. Hilary of Poitiérs هو أسقف مدينة بواتييه ولاهوتي وأحد آباء الكنيسة في القرن الرابع، كان معاصرًا للبابا أثناسيوس الرسولي. كثيرًا ما كان القديس أغسطينوس يستعين به في مقاومته البيلاجيين Pelagians . ويصفه القديس جيروم بأنه: " من أكثر الرجال فصاحة وقوة من اللاتين في مقاومة الأريوسيين ". نشأته وُلد هيلاري في بواتييه وكانت أسرته من أشراف بلاد الغال Gaul )فرنسا نال قسطًا وافرًا من الفلسفة والتعليم الكلاسيكي. يقول عن نفسه أنه نشأ وثنيًا، ويعطينا وصفًا تفصيليًا للخطوات التي اتخذها معه الله ليتعرف على الإيمان الصحيح. كان هيلاري يعتقد من الناحية المنطقية أن الإنسان مخلوق حر، ذو مبادئ، وموضوع في هذا العالم ليمارس الصبر والنسك والفضائل الأخرى، التي بها ينال المكافأة بعد انتهاء هذه الحياة. ثم أخذ يسعى في شغف ليتعلم عن الله، وبسرعة اكتشف كذب الاعتقاد بتعدد الآلهة، واقتنع أنه لا يمكن أن يكون هناك إلا إله واحد، وأنه لابد أن يكون أبديًا وغير متغير وكليّ القدرة والعلة الأولى ومُبدع كل الأشياء. بهذه الخلفية وبهذا الاعتقاد تقابل مع الكتاب المقدس وتأثر بشدة من الوصف السامي الذي به يصف موسى الله ومن الكلمات التي تعبر عن وجوده الذاتي: "أنا الذي هو I Am Who Am ." كما تأثر أيضًا من فكرة سلطانه الفائق التي عبّر عنها ووصفها الأنبياء. ثم كم َّلت قراءة العهد الجديد الإجابة عن استفساراته، وتعلم من الإصحاح الأول لإنجيل يوحنا أن الكلمة المتجسد، الله الابن، مساوي في الوجود والأبدية مع الآب، وواحد معه في ذات الجوهر. وهكذا إذ بلغ إلى معرفة الإيمان الصحيح نال المعمودية في سنٍ متقدم نسبيًا. سيامته أسقفًا كان هيلاري متزوجًا قبل مسيحيته وله ابنة اسمها أبرا Apra، وكانت زوجته مازالت موجودة حين اختير أسقفًا لبواتييه حوالي سنة 350 م وقد حاول بكل قوته الهروب من هذه الكرامة ولكن كان هذا دافع للشعب للتمسك باختياره أكثر، وبالفعل لم تخب توقعاتهم إذ ظهرت فضائله وصفاته المتميزة التي لفتت الأنظار إليه، ليس في بلاد الغال فقط بل وفي الكنيسة بأسرها. كان هيلاري واعظًا وشاعرًا، وكان يعتبرها مسئولية حياته أن يشهد عن الله لكل العالم ويقود الناس كلهم إلى محبة الله، وكان دائمًا يدعو الجميع أن يبدأوا كل أعمالهم 2 In Matt. hom. 2. 105

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 64
passages.text: عشر بندًا شرح فيها العقيدة المسيحية السليمة، وحرم فيها كل من يتعدّاها، وهي التي سميت فيما بعد " الحرومات الإثني عشر ". إلا أن نسطور احتقر الرسالة والحرومات وقام بكتابة بنود ضدها، وهكذا انقسمت الكنيسة إلى قسمين: الأول يضم كنائس روما وأورشليم وآسيا الصغرى وهذه الكنائس أيّدت البابا كيرلس في رأيه، والثاني يضم كنيستي إنطاكية والقسطنطينية التي هي كرسي نسطور. مجمع أفسس أمام هذا الانقسام طلب البابا كيرلس من الإمبراطور ثيؤدوسيوس أن يعقد مجمعًا لدراسة الأمر، فاستجاب الإمبراطور لطلب البابا وأرسل لجميع الأساقفة بما فيهم نسطور لكي يجتمعوا في أفسس، وكان اجتماعهم يوم الأحد 13 بؤونة سنة 147 ش الموافق 7 يونيو سنة 431 م وقد انتهى المجمع بحرم نسطور ووضع مقدّمة قانون الإيمان. نفيه وحين وصلت قرارات المجمع إلى الإمبراطور ثيؤدوسيوس الصغير ثبّتها، وأمر بنفي نسطور بعيدًا عن القسطنطينية. قرّر الإمبراطور نفي نسطور إلى ديره الأول أيروبيوس الذي نشأ فيه، كما نفى عددًا كبير من الأساقفة من أتباعه، ومكث هناك في الدير أربع سنوات. غير أنه لم يهدأ بل ظلّ ينفث سمومه بين الرهبان مما أغضب الإمبراطور، فأصدر أمره بإحراق جميع مؤلفاته ونفيه إلى بلاد العرب ثم أخميم، التي كانت عاصمة للإقليم التاسع من أقاليم جنوب مصر ال 22 ، حيث كان المسيحيون هناك شديدي التمسك بإيمانهم ولا يُخشى عليهم من وجوده مقيمًا بينهم. ظل مقيمًا هناك حتى مات منبوذًا مكروهًا من الجميع، ودُفن في أخميم سنة 450 م وقد اعتاد أقباط أخميم أن يرجموا قبره بالحجارة، ويلقوا عليه القمامة والتراب حتى تكو َّن من ذلك كوم أو تل نسطور في النصف البحري الشرقي للمدينة. المطران الأنبا بيشوي: مذكرات في اللاهوت المسكوني. ✞ نِكتاريوس البطريرك القديس St. Nectarius حين اعتزل القديس غريغوريوس النزينزي رئاسة كرسي القسطنطينية في سنة 381 م بعد أن جلس عليه مدة قصيرة خلفه نِكتاريوس في هذا المنصب. كان من سكان طرسوس Tarsus بكيليكية Cilicia، وقصة اختياره لهذا المنصب طريفة. ذلك أنه أثناء انعقاد المجمع المسكوني الثاني في القسطنطينية عزم نِكتاريوس على زيارة أهله في طرسوس، فذهب إلى ديودور Diodorus أسقف طرسوس - والذي كان حاضرًا المجمع - ليسأله إن كان يريد إرسال أية خطابات إلى طرسوس. حينما وقعت عينا ديودور على نِكتاريوس تأثر جدًا بأخلاقه ونظراته، واقترح علي ميليتيوس Meletius بطريرك إنطاكية أن يخلف غريغوريوس على كرسي القسطنطينية. ضحك ميليتيوس للفكرة، ولكن اسم نِكتاريوس أضيف للقائمة التي قُد ِّمت للإمبراطور، ولدهشة الجميع اختار الإمبراطور ثيئودوسيوس نِكتاريوس، مع أنه لم يكن 20

passages.label: كاتيكيزم الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية, p. 77
passages.text: انقسام الكنيسة! نعم وإن مارسنا ربوات الأعمال المجيدة، فإننا إن مز َّقنا ملء الكنيسة نسقط تحت عقوبة لا تقل عن تلك التي يسقط تحتها من أفسدوا جسده 230 [. 994. ما هو دور الذين يتمت َّعون بحياة الملء في تعاملهم مع الضعفاء؟ يقول الرسول: "وأنا نفسي أيضًا متيقن من جهتكم يا إخوتي أنكم أنتم مشحونون صلاحًا ومملوؤون كل علمٍ، قادرون أن ينذر بعضكم بعضًا" )رو 15 : 14 .( إذ تحد َّث عن التزامهم كأقوياء أن يحتملوا ضعفات الضعفاء، وكيهود متنصّرين أن يقبلوا الأمم في الإيمان بفرحٍ وسرورٍ، أراد أن يُلَط ِّف الحديث معهم، فلا يجعل من وصيته أمرًا ثقيلاً على نفوسهم، لهذا بادر يمدحهم مُظهِرًا أن ما يطلبه منهم ليس بالكثير بالنسبة لقامتهم الروحيّة وإدراكهم. ويلاحظ هنا رقته في الحديث من جهة الآتي: أولاً: لم يقل إنه سمع عن صلاحهم، وإنما هو مُتيق ِّن، ليس محتاجًا إلى من يشهدون لهم أمامه. وكأنه يقول إن كنت أوصيكم أو أقسو عليكم بالانتهار، فأنا مُتيق ِّن من جهتكم إنكم مشحونون صلاحًا! ثانيًا: يُعَل ِّق القدّيس يوحنا الذهبي الفم على تعبيره: "أنكم أنتم مشحونون صلاحًا"، بالقول: ] لأنكم قساة أو مبغِضون لإخوتكم لذلك أنصحكم أن تقبلوا عمل الله فلا تهملوه أو تُحَط ِّموه، فإني أعرف أنكم مشحونون صلاحًا؛ وإنما يبدو لي هنا أن أدعوكم لكمال فضيلتكم 231 [. ثالثًا: في رقّة يحثّهم كما في اتساع القلب أكثر فأكثر بحُبّ الآخرين حيث لا ينقصهم ملء الصلاح والمعرفة والقدرة. من جهة القلب هم صالحون لطفاء مُحِب ُّون؛ من جهة الفكر لهم ملء العلم والمعرفة، ومن جهة الإمكانية قادرون. هذا كله أعطاه الجسارة ليطالبهم أكثر فأكثر! رابعًا: يكتب القدّيس بولس إليهم بروح الأخوة المتواضعة التي أعطته دالة ليتجاسر فيكتب إليهم لا كمن يوصيهم بأمرٍ غريبٍ عن حياتهم، وإنما يُذَك ِّرهم لينموا بالأكثر فيما يمارسونه فعلاً، إذ يقول: "ولكن بأكثر جسارة كتبت إليكم جزئيّا أيها الإخوة، كمُذَك ِّرٍ لكم بسبب النعمة التي وُهِبَت لي" )رو 15 : 14 .( يقول القدّيس يوحنا الذهبي الفم : ] تواضع فكر بولس، لاحظوا حكمته... إنه ينزل من كرسي الرئاسة هنا وهناك ليتحد َّث إليهم كإخوة وأصدقاء في نفس الدرجة 232 [. خامسًا يُعلِن الرسول أنه مُلتزِم بالكتابة إليهم، لأنه يمارس خدمته الرسولية التي أُفرِز لها كرسول للأمم، فإن كانت روما عاصمة العالم الأممي في ذلك الحين فهو يشعر أنها يجب أن تكون مركز عمله. هذه هي النعمة التي وُهِبَت له من الله، خدمة الأمم، التي لا يتوق َّف عن التمت ُّع بها قط. سادسًا: يقول: ")تكونوا( مملوئين من ثمر البرّ الذي بيسوع المسيح لمجد الله وحمده" )في 1 : 11 .( البرّ هو السيد المسيح. فالإنسان المسيحي لابد أن يثمر في هدوء وسلام، أما ثمر البرّ فهو الأعمال الصالحة. إذ نُغرَس في المسيح يسوع، ونُطعم فيه، لا نعود نكون بعد أغصان برية، بل أغصان الكرمة الإلهية الحام

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 77
passages.text: يحتجز القديسين ماركوس Marcus ومارسيليانوس Marcellianus . وقد نال فيما بعد إكليل الشهادة. A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. IV, page 42. ✞ نيقولاوس الأسقف القديس St. Nicholas نشأته كان من مدينة مورا أو باتارا Patara بليكيا Lycia إحدى مقاطعات آسيا الصغرى، وكانت ميرا Myra العاصمة قريبة من البحر، وهي مقر كرسي أسقفي. اسم أبيه أبيفانيوس وأمه تونة، وقد جمعا إلى جانب الغنى الكثير مخافة الرب، ولم يكن لهما ولد. ولما شاخا تحنن الله عليهما ورزقهما هذا القديس الذي امتلأ بالنعمة الإلهية منذ طفولته. ربّياه والداه تربية حسنة، ونشأ تحت رعاية الكنيسة في نقاوة القلب. وفي سن الخامسة بدأ يتعلم العلوم الكنسية، ويومًا بعد يوم أضاءت تعاليم الكنيسة عقله وحم َّسته إلى التدين السليم. في تلقيه العلم أظهر من النجابة ما دل َّ على أن الروح القدس كان يلهمه أكثر مما كان يتلقى من المعلم، فقُد ِّم شماسًا. رهبنته ترهب في دير كان ابن عمه رئيسًا عليه، فعاش حياة النسك والجهاد والفضيلة حتى رُسِم قسًا وهو في التاسعة عشر من عمره. وأعطاه الله نعمة عمل الآيات ومنها إخراج الشياطين وشفاء المرضى، وكان يبارك في الخبز القليل فيشبع منه عددًا كبيرًا. أعمال الرحمة توفي والداه وهو شاب تاركين له أموالاً وثروة، فقرر أن يكرّس ميراثه في أعمال الرحمة. سرعان ما حانت له الفرصة لتحقيق اشتياقه، ذلك أن أحد رجال باتارا فقد كل أمواله لدرجة أنه لم يجد ما يقتات به. وكان عليه أن يزوج بناته الثلاث، إلا أنه لم يستطع ذلك بسبب فقره، فنوى الرجل البائس أن يسلمهن لأعمال الدعارة. حين سمع القديس نيقولا بهذا الأمر أخذ مائة دينار وجعلها في كيس وتحت ستار الظلام ألقاه من شباك منزل الرجل، الذي لما انتبه من نومه ووجد الكيس فرح كثيرًا وزو َّج بهذا المال ابنته الكبرى. ثم كرر القديس نيقولاوس )نيقولا( نفس الأمر مع الابنة الثانية. ولما جاء دور الابنة الثالثة كان الأب يسهر ليراقب ويتعر َّف على شخصية هذا المحسن الكريم. لبث ساهرًا في المرة الأخيرة وحالما شعر بسقوط الكيس وسط منزله لم يأخذه بل أسرع إلى خارج البيت ليرى من الذي ألقاه فعرف أنه القديس نيقولاوس، فخر َّ عند قدميه وشكره كثيرًا لأنه أنقذ فتياته من فقر المال وما كن يتعرضن له من الضياع. أسقف ميرا قبل انتخابه لرتبة الأسقفية رأى ذات ليلة في حلم كرسيًا عظيمًا وحلة بهية موضوعة عليه وإنسانًا يقول له: " البس هذه الحلة وأجلس على هذا الكرسي ". 33

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 101
passages.text: ولما تناقشا في الأمر طويلاً أمال الله قلبه إلى رأيها، وألهب الروح القدس أعماقه بنار الحب الإلهي. فزهد أموال العالم وعاش في حياة مقدسة. وكانت ميلانيا قد تزوجته وهي في سن الثالثة عشر فقط، وعاشت معه سبع سنوات هكذا في عفة. خدمتها كانت ترسل أموالاً إلى كنائس مصر وإنطاكية وفلسطين. وجعلت عبيدها في منزلة اخوتها وأطلقت من أراد منهم المضيّ. وباعت أملاكها في أسبانيا وفرنسا وصقلية وأعطتها للأديرة والمحتاجين، وكما كانت تقول حتى لا تتحمل عبء هذه الثروات الثقيل . التحقت ميلانيا الصغرى بأحد الأديرة وعاشت كأبسط راهبة في حياة نسكية وزهد مع حرارة الروح والسهر في الصلاة. كانت تأكل طعامها كل خمسة أيام، ولكن من أجل كل النساء اللواتي كسبتهن للمسيح كانت تأكل معهن كل يوم مرة. الراهب بنيانوس نما زوجها في الحياة النسكية وسكن مع حوالي ثلاثمائة راهبًا في دير أنشأه، وكان مداومًا على قراءة الكتب المقدسة وعمل بيديه في البستان، وتمكن من اكتساب رجل يدعى باخوميوس من عائلة كبيرة للمسيح، وزع من أمواله على الفقراء وأوصى بالباقي للمحتاجين بعد موته. هكذا عاشت ميلانيا وزوجها في حياة سعيدة. بستان القديسين، صفحة 41 . ✞ ميلتيادس البطريرك القديس St. Miltiades كان أصلاً من أفريقيا وانتُخِب بطريركًا لكرسي روما في 2 يوليو سنة 311م على الأرجح، لذلك ترتبط ذكرى هذا البطريرك بنهاية عصر الاضطهاد في الكنيسة. ذلك أن الإمبراطور قسطنطين بعد أن هزم ماكسنتيوس Maxentius في معركة Milvian Bridge في 28 أكتوبر سنة 312 م زحف إلى روما، في أوائل عام 313 وأطلق حرية العبادة لكل الأديان بما فيها المسيحية في أرجاء الإمبراطورية الرومانية. وأعقب ذلك السماح للكنائس بالحصول على مزايا وإطلاق سراح المسيحيين المأسورين في السجون والمناجم، واحتفل الجميع بانتصار المسيح بترانيم المجد لله نهارًا وليلاً، مُصل ِّين أن يستمر السلام في الكنيسة بعد طول الاضطهاد. لكن في وسط بهجة الكنيسة حدث اضطراب نتيجة ظهور مشكلة انشقاق في كنيسة أفريقيا، ذلك حين اختير سيسيليان Caecillian أسقفًا على قرطبة بينما اعترضت مجموعة بقيادة دوناتُس Donatus على هذا الاختيار، بسبب اتهامهم لسيسيليان أنه سَل َّم الكتب المقدسة لمضطهديه تحت تأثير التعذيب. طلب قسطنطين من ميلتيادس فعقد مجمعًا في روما من الأساقفة الإيطاليين والغاليين وقرروا فيه أن اختيار ورسامة سيسيليان كان شرعيًا. وقد امتدح القديس أغسطينوس حكمة واعتدال ميلتيادس واصفًا إياه: "الرجل الممتاز والابن الحقيقي للسلام وأبو المسيحيين". تعتبره الكنيسة الرومانية من الشهداء بسبب العذابات التي تحملها على يد ماكسيميان Maximian قبل رسامته، وكانت نياحته 634

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 104
passages.text: في الرئاسة على كنيسة الإسكندرية فأسرعا إليه، وللحال رسم كاهنين أحدهم في السجن والآخر في المناجم، وادّعى لنفسه العمل الأسقفي في الكنيسة أثناء غيبة أسقفها الشرعي. أسرع القديس بطرس بالعودة إلى الإسكندرية وقاوم ميليتوس فحدث تأزمًا وانشقاقًا دام زمانًا طويلاً، حتى أيام القديس أثناسيوس. وقد زاد لهيب الأزمة في فترة الهدوء التي لحقت اعتزال دقلديانوس الحكم، فقد أصدر البابا في عيد القيامة عام 306 أربعة عشر قانونًا تعالج موقف الجاحدين الراجعين... في رسالته الدورية التي تدعى بالرسالة القانونية، وقد حملت ترفقًا بمصير الساقطين. أما ميليتوس فبالرغم من تجريده بواسطة مجمع إسكندري إلا أنه استمر في سيامته للكهنة والأساقفة. وقد وجد له عونًا بين المعترفين في المناجم، وإذ حكم عليه بالعمل في المناجم اشتهر كمعترف. بلغ عدد التابعين له عام 325م كقول البابا أثناسيوس 28 أسقفًا، لكن "ما كان لأتباع مليتوس أهمية تذكر سوى تأثيرهم كأساس ارتكزت عليه الآريوسية فى مراحلها الأولى وكموضع إقلاق لأثناسيوس"، فقد مثّلوا خطرًا في سندهم للآريوسيين ضد البابا أثناسيوس، حيث لفقوا له عدة اتهامات عام 331 م بقصد تشويه سمعته. ظل ميليتوس في عناده حتى بعد انتقال خاتم الشهداء إلى السماء إذ تمرد على خليفته البابا أرشيلاوس، ثم تمادى في طغيانه إلى حد دفعه إلى أن يشكو البابا ألكسندروس إلى الإمبراطور قسطنطين. وقد تلمس لنفسه الأعذار في شكواه من هذا البابا وسلفيه بأن ادعى أنهم جميعًا قد غالوا في الترفق بالتائبين متناسيًا ما تردى هو فيه من جريمة عبادة الأصنام. وقد استمر في تمرده حتى انعقاد مجمع نيقية المسكوني الأول. لما نظر المجمع في تهمة هذا الأسقف رأى أن يترفق به فاقتصر على تجريده من حق الانتخاب في إيبارشيته وأية إيبارشية أخرى، وحفظ له لقب أسقف كلقب شرف فقط. وقال في قانونه السادس من قوانينه العشرين: "إن من يقام أسقفًا بغير مصادقة المتروبوليت )أي أسقف العاصمة( فإن هذا المجمع العظيم يحكم بأن لا يعد أسقفًا". كذلك حكم المجمع أن الأساقفة الذين رسمهم ميليتيوس لا يعدون ضمن رجال الكهنوت إلا إذا صادق البابا السكندري على أسقفيتهم. القمص تادرس ملطي: الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية كنيسة علم ولاهوت. ✞ ميليتيوس بطريرك إنطاكية راجع: الأسقف ملاتيوس القديس. ✞ ميليسيوس الأب كان هذا القديس ناسكًا ومجاهدًا طول أيامه ساكنًا مع تلميذيه في مغارة بجبل خوراسان. 637

who added: “Be strong; first have the communion of the Holy Sacraments... 
and after three days, I shall come back to take you with me.” 
On telling the elders about his vision, they wept, bid him farewell , and 
sought from him to remember them in Heaven . He, in turn, asked from them 
to remember him in their prayers, and he reposed on the third day, with the 
elders all around him. 
 [The Synaxarion: 5 Baramhat] 
 
SERAPION, BISHOP OF THMUIS, ST. 
This St. Serapion was given the title Scholastic, due to his mastering of both 
the spiritual and temporal knowledge. For some time, he was the dean of the 
Theological (Catechetical) School of Alexandria, however, because of his love 
to the ascetic life, he became a hermit in the desert and a friend of St. Anthony 
the Great (251-356 AD). St. Serapion had to forsake his seclusion, to sit on the 
bishopric throne of Thmuis (Temy) in Upper Egypt, near Diospolis (Luxor). 
His Defense of the Orthodox Faith: 
St. Serapion att ended the Council of Serdica in the year 343, where he 
joined the 20th Pope St. Athanasius the Apostolic (328-373) in defending the 
Upright faith. According to St. Jerome, he was also exiled by Emperor 
Constantius II (337-361 AD). He partook of opposing the Macedonian and the 
Arian heresies and authored an excellent book against the Manicheans heresy. 
Some of His Writings: 
St. Serapion authored many books, most of which were lost , but his most 
famous work was Euchologion, discovered and published at the end of the 19th 
century. 
According to the historian Socrates, St. Serapion often repeated the 
statements that summarized the exaltation of Christianity, saying:  
“The mind is purified by spiritual knowledge (i.e. , by holy meditation and 
prayers), the spiritual passions of the soul are purified by the charity, and the 
irregular appetites are purified by abstinence and penance.” 
With St. Anthony the Great: 
According to St. Jerome, St. Serapion was a personal friend of St. Anthony 
the Great, and his name was mentioned twice in the book “ Life of Anthony” 
written by the Pope St. Athanasius the Apostolic. The first time, when the pope 
was talking to the brethren about the visions of Abba Anthony, who often used 
to suddenly interrupt his speech f or a while before he resume s it again, and

87 
 
grandfather’s brother. When Simeon’s father died, he wanted to convert from 
Judaism to become a Christian. An angel of the Lord appeared to him, told him 
to go to Abba John (Yohanna), the bishop of Jerusalem, who taught him the 
principals of Christianity and the Incarnation of Jesus Christ; but did not dare 
to baptize him in Jerusalem for fear of the Jews. 
The Virgin St. Mary appeared to Simeon and told him to go to the city of 
Alexandria in Egypt to see the 16th Pope of Alexandria St. Theonas (282-301). 
Accompanied by an angel in a human form, he reached Alexandria and went 
to the Pope St. Theonas. The pope was informed about him in advance through 
an angel, who told him how great that man would become. The pope welcomed 
him, instructed him , and baptized him under the name of Serabamon , which 
means “Who was Born in the faith of his Fathers,” according to the 19th pope 
St. Alexandros I (312-328 AD), the author of his biography.  
In Alexandria, Serabamon kept studying the Holy Bible and contemplating 
in the Passions of the Lord Christ for His love of humankind. He was supported 
by Pope Theonas and his disciple deacon Peter (Botros), who dearly 
appreciated Serabamon because of his great eagerness towards studying and 
worship. Deacon, Peter noticed how his face shined with joy and gladness 
when he was pursuing that. Once, Peter was astonished when he foun d 
Serabamon explaining clearly to him what he did not understand , as if a 
prophet or one of the Evangelists has interpreted them to him. When the deacon 
Peter hastened to tell the pope about the wisdom of Serabamon and the depth 
of his spiritual knowledge and his amazing ability to interpret the Holy 
Scripture, the pope remembered what the angel said about the saint , and he 
told the deacon about that. 
His Monastic Life: 
Some monks came from the Monastery of the Glass, west of Alexandria, to 
invite the pope to hold the prayers of the Resurrection feast in their monastery. 
Serabamon, who admired the monk 's wisdom and tranquility, inquired from 
deacon Peter about their lives; and asked for the permission of the pope to 
accompany the monk’s back to the monastery. There, he loved seclusion. And 
in a very short time, he memorized the New Testament by heart, in addition to 
parts of the Old Testament, the sayings and sermons of many of the saints, in 
particular those of St. Ignatius the enlightened and St. Polycarp. 
Helping Pope Peter the Last Martyr: 
When pope Theonas reposed and was replaced by his deacon Peter as the 
17th Pope and the last martyr (302 -311), pope Peter remembered his beloved 
spiritual friend Serabamon . He called him to help in the work of the 
patriarchate, in particular those about teaching. But being a lover of the life of

passages.text:
95 
 
On hearing about it, his fellow citizens came carrying arms to kill the 
governor and to set him free. However, when the saint told them that it was his 
desire to be martyred in the name of Christ, they went their way. 
His Torture: 
The governor took him along on a boat to Alexandria, where he tortured 
him with the Henbazin; cast him in a pit of fire, and put him in a pot filled with 
molten tar. In all of this, God kept healing him. And when they finally crucified 
the saint and continued beating him with a rod, an angel of the Lord came down 
and released him. 
The governor then handed the task of torturing him to a prince called Orion, 
who took him by boat to his town . They landed the boat someplace by night; 
to be surprised in the morning to reali ze that they landed at the home town of 
the saint. Amazed, Orion heard a voice saying to him: “This is his home town.” 
After violently torturing him, they cut his holy head by the sword. He received 
the crown of martyrdom , and Orion took off his shirt, wra pped it around the 
saint's body, and delivered it to his family. 
.[The Synaxarion: 27 Toba] 
 
SERAPION, THE GREAT, ST. 
A hermit in Mount Nitria , whose name is mentioned along with S S. 
Macarius, Pamponius, Heraclius and other saints . They became famous and 
drew many around them, in the days of Emperor Constantius II (337-361 AD), 
and kept the Upright faith, set by the Fathers of the Nicene Council. 
St. Serapion the Great was a contemporary of St. Anthony the Great, and he 
was visited by St. Paula , the Elder i n 386 AD, by Melania , the Elder in 387 
AD, and by Palladius in 390 AD... 
 [A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. IV, p. 614] 
 
SERAPION, THE REPENTANT 
This man was a Christian native of Alexandria, Egypt . It happened that he 
became weak during the persecution of Emperor Decius (249-251 AD) and 
ended up burning incense before the idols . His episode was used by the 14 th 
Pope St. Dionysius of Alexandria (246-264 AD), as practical evidence against 
the heresy o f the Novatians who were very adamant not to accept the 
repentance of those who denied faith during the persecution The pope wrote to 
bishop Fabius of Antioch (253 -256 AD), one of this heresy followers, 
explaining how wrong that heresy was.

passages.text:
99 
 
The saint was martyred in 302 AD. 
 [Butler: February 23] 
SERENUS; SAINTS BY THAT NAME 
More than one martyr carried the name Serenus: 
1- Serenus and Serenus : two martyrs among the students  of Origen (184 -
253 AD), who happen to carry the same name . They were tortured during 
the persecution stirred up by Emperor Severus (222-235 AD). They were 
martyred along with a third martyr by the name Plutarch . The Western 
Church celebrates them on the 28th of June. 
2- Father Serenus of the desert of Nitria : who was a climax in asceticism 
and had many virtues . He was visited by Father John Cassian (360 -435 
AD) in the year 395 AD . They discussed two subjects . In the first one, 
father Serenus talked to him abo ut the Nature of the Spirit, the rapid 
movement of the thoughts, the influence of the evil spirits upon them, and 
the importance of fixing the desire on God. In the following discussion, he 
talked to him about the nature of the evil spirits, their fall, su bordination, 
and occupation. 
 [A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. IV, pp. 615-616] 
 
SERGIUS OF ATRIPE AND HIS COMPANIONS 
(The martyrs) 
This saint was born in the city of Atripe, by a good father called Tadros and 
a pious mother called Mary. When he reached 20 years of age, he decided to 
die in the Name of the Lord Christ. He went to Cyprian , the governor, and 
before him, he confessed the name of the Lord. 
A Night Vision in Prison: 
After torturing him by several kinds of tools, he was cast in prison. In a 
night vision, he saw himself in heaven, where he saw the dwelling places of 
the saints, which brought comfort to his soul; and the Lord Christ healed his 
wounds. 
Martyrdom of Fr. Mansoon: 
On hearing about the strife of Sergius, a priest called  Fr. Mansoon went to 
Atripe accompanied by two deacons . They confessed the Lord Christ before 
the governor, who ordered beating them with ferocity. There, a great multitude 
gathered around the priest, sympathizing with him; and he addressed them and 
counseled them to hold fast to the Upright faith in the Lord Christ, he prayed

passages.text:
89 
 
to the church. 
His Prophecy about Ariana: 
Before the boat started to sail from Alexandria, St. Serabamon told the 
governor Ariana: “Ariana! The Lord Christ is going to call upon you to go to 
His wedding. And, when He does , hasten without slothfulness to respond to 
his invitation. You will strive, you will overcome Diocletian by your 
perseverance and will receive the crown of martyrdom.”  The governor 
naturally mocked that prophecy, counting it as fantasy; until the time came 
when Ariana received the Christian faith and persisted on being martyred. 
Pope of Alexandria Alexandros I wrote: 
* O Saint Serabamon! Who would be wise enough and prudent to 
describe the loftiness of your virtues?! 
* Who is eloquent enough to narrate your miracles, O wearer of God! 
* Who is the researcher who could show the extent of your strife, O the 
utterer of Divinities, the perfect in every goodness; who strove for the sake of 
the flocks of the Lord Christ; and suffered to guide the multitudes, and lea d 
them away from vanity; following the lead of Paul the Apostle, who guided 
multitudes to the sure way of the Truth. 
 [Manuscript# 214 in the Library of the Syrian Monastery; published by Fr. 
Serabamon St. Anthony] 
 
SERABAMON, THE HEGOMEN, ST. 
Hegomen of the Monastery of Abu-Yeĥness: 
This St. Serabamon , the hermit , became the hegomen (abbot) of the 
monastery of Abu-Yeĥness. He was a monk in that monastery from an early 
age. He remained in his worship and in serving the older monks for 32 years 
until he was ordained as a hegomen on the monastery to supervise its affairs . 
Since then, he increased his devotion and asceticism. Although, he used to fast 
the whole day, from the day he became a monk until the day he reposed. 
After 20 years in this fellowship, he cl osed on himself in a room in one of 
the churches and was not seen for almost ten years, during which he broke his 
fast only on Saturdays and Sundays.  
A Cross of Fire: 
When it was time for him to depart from this world, an angel of the Lord 
appeared to him in a night vision. The angel handed him a Cross of fire, saying: 
“Take this in your hand.” He said to the angel: “How could I hold fire with my 
hand?” The angel answered him: “Do not be afraid, for the Lord Christ will

91 
 
they would assume that the saint has seen a vision. St. Anthony used to tell St. 
Serapion about these visions. It was also said that St. Anthony while sitting on 
the mountain, he often saw what was going on in Egy pt. The second time , 
when he knew that his departure was near, he requested that his clothes be 
distributed, giving one of sheepskin to Pope Athanasius and the one he has 
gotten new from bishop Serapion to be given back to him worn out, to keep. 
Heading a Monastic Congregation: 
According to the historian Sozomen, before St. Serapion was ordained as a 
bishop, he was the abbot of a monastic congregation in Upper Egypt, and that 
he was well known for his fantastic sanctity and eloquence. His close friend, 
Pope Athanasius, also mentioned in his letter to Dracontius, that he was the 
abbot of a significant number of monks. 
His Support of Pope Athanasius: 
St. Serapion supported the Pope in his strife against the Arianism . Being 
like his right hand , the pope used hi m as his deputy during his frequent 
absences from the throne. In the year 340 AD, the pope let him declare the date 
of the Passover; and it is believed that he let him write the Passover papal 
messages during the two years 341 and 342 AD. 
His Exile and Departure: 
On the 18 th of May 353 AD, Pope Athanasius sent a delegation of five 
bishops and three priests, headed by bishop Serapion, to Emperor Constantius 
II after his conquests and reigning over both the East and the West. The papal 
delegation was carrying to the emperor a document signed by 80 bishops from 
Egypt in support of Pope Athanasius and refuting the evil reports presented by 
the Arians against him.  However, the emperor 's response was to send St. 
Serapion to exile, for the sake of his Upright faith ; and hence was called the 
Confessor. This saint was chosen based on his ability to defend the Upright 
faith, and his firm stands in encountering the emperor and opposing the Arian 
pressure. It was said that St. Serapion reposed in his exile around the year 370 
AD, even though the exact date is not certain. 
Letters of St. Athanasius to Him: 
St. Athanasius the Apostolic sent him five dogmatic letters: 
1- A letter sent in 339 AD, while in exile, concerning the death of Arius, in 
which St. Athanasius denied that Arius changed his views or that he 
reconciled with the Church before he died. 
2- Four very important letters about the Holy Spirit, which the pope wrote in 
response to a request from St. Serapion , who was complaining that the

passages.text:
94 
 
 [Baring-Gould: October 30] 
 
SERAPION, THE ABBOT, ST. 
This St. Serapion was a priest and one of the most famous Fathers. He was 
mentioned in the book: On Illustrious Men written by St. Jerome, as follows: 
“We saw him in the region of Arsinoe (Fayyum) , an elder father in charge 
of many monasteries that embraced about 10,000 monks , and he cared for all 
their needs. Those who harvested the fields used to bring to him 12 bushels of 
wheat, to give to those in need in the area. He used to distribute these needs by 
his own hands, and to send to those in Alexandria their portions as well. 
The Fathers of the wilderness used to do that regularly, always taking care 
of the poor in Alexandria . But, because of being occupied with the life of 
spiritual strife, they used to just fill boats with food and clothes and send them 
every year to the capital; on account of that, the poor around them in the desert 
were not that many. 
We also saw in the region of Babylon (Old Cairo) and Memphis (El -
Badrashin) so many great Fathers, who were adorned with good deeds, blessed 
and well accepted by God .” The name of St. Serapion was also mentioned in 
the biography of the Libyan recluse Marcus Atheniensis, who cared to bury his 
body. 
 [A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. IV, p. 613] 
 
SERAPION, THE CORINTHIAN MARTYR 
This St. Serapion was originally from Corinth in Greece. He was martyred 
in Egypt, along with Niceporus, under the rule of Emperor Numerian (283-284 
AD) in the year 284 AD. 
 [A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. IV, p. 613] 
 
SERAPION, THE EGYPTIAN MARTYR 
A Desire for Martyrdom: 
This St. Serapion was a wealthy inhabitant of Binosah (Babousah) in Lower 
Egypt, with a strong love of giving alms. At the time of persecution, he heard 
that Armanius govern or of Alexandria arrived in the area to torture the 
Christians. Serapion came to encounter him, along with a friend called 
Theodorus and a third, a shepherd of cattle, named Thomas. And, when they 
confessed the Lord Christ before him, the governor cast them in prison.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 92
passages.text:
92 
 
teaching against the Holy Spirit, considering Him as a created being, albeit 
higher than the angels, was very quickly spreading . Those letters are 
counted as the first methodical theological research about the Holy Spirit. 
St. Serapion Writings: 
1- Against the followers of Mani: a work that revealed the eloquence of St. 
Serapion in both the theological and philosophical fields. He only criticized 
the main points in the views of the followers of Mani, in particular their 
Dualism view, (concerning the god of light and the god of darkness); their 
objection about the Old Testament and some parts of the New Testament . 
He also proved the contradiction and lack of logic within their views. 
2- His Letters: A comforting letter he wrote to bishop Evgokius who was ill; 
a letter to the monks in Alexandr ia, in which he used the expression 
“Homosius Trias ,” meaning (The Trinity equal in Essence); and a 
condolence letter to some disciples of Abba Anthony after he reposed in 
the year 356 AD. 
3- Other works which, according to some scholars, were his, like A Sermon 
on Virginity ; A Letter to the Confessors ; and some fragments of 
Interpretations of the Book of Genesis, referred to by St. Jerome. 
4- The Divine Liturgy by St. Serapion 1 This version represents the 
Ecclesiastical Liturgy in Egypt in the 4th century (Probably referring to an 
earlier period). This Liturgy carried a reflection of the views of the School 
of Alexandria in the 3rd century concerning the Divinity of the Logos ‘The 
Word,’ after adding to it what suited the 4th century in response to the Arian 
heresy. 
So many prayers that came in this Liturgy are the same as those included in 
the Liturgy of St. Mark, concerning the Anaphora (The Ecclesiastical system) 
of the Ethiopian Church. 
All prayers address God, being the Father of the Only Begotten-Son, and it 
gives Him thanks for the sake of His compassion, proclaimed through the 
salvation works of our Lord Jesus Christ. 
Of the Divine Liturgy by St. Serapion: 
• I implore You, O Lord, to send Your Holy Spirit to our minds . Grant us to 
understand Your inspi red Holy Bible , to be able to  interpret them with 
uprightness and worthiness. 
So that all believers present here would benefit from them. 
Grant us the spirit of light, to recognize You as the Truth. And Jesus Christ 
whom You sent (John 3:17). Grant us the Holy Spirit, to be able to proclaim 
 
1 Fr. ‘Tadros Y. Malaty’ covered this Liturgy in his book “Christ in the Eucharist Sacrament”…

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 88
passages.text:
88 
 
contemplation, he soon returned to his monastery, to be called by the pope now 
and then, to enjoy his company and his shining countenance. 
Bishop of Nicius: 
Almost ten years in his papacy, the diocese of Nicius became vacant by the 
repose of St. John . Pope Peter called the monk Serabamon and ordained him 
as a bishop on that diocese, which made the congregation there very happy. 
On his hands, God performed so many miracles and signs; among them was 
that near his city, there were locations for idol worship, which he kept praying 
to the Lord Christ until these sites were all destroyed and inundated by water . 
The idol worship was ultimately uprooted from his whole diocese. He also 
managed to eradicate the heresy of Sabilius, who taught that the Father, the 
Son, and the Holy Spirit were one Hypostasis. 
 Performing Signs and Miracles: 
His biographer Pope Alexandros I talked much about how St. Serabamon 
opposed Arius and Meletius. He also said about the saint: “ Living in his city  
became like living in the monasteries of monks . The miracles and signs 
performed by him were not less than those performed by the Apostles Peter 
and Paul. He healed the sick and drove the unclean spirits out, screaming and 
begging him not to torture them with his prayers.” 
His Care for the Poor and the Rich: 
His city became like one family; the rich were urged by him to provide the 
poor generously with their necessities. 
His Martyrdom: 
After Emperor Diocletian (284 -305) denied the faith, he was told how 
bishop Serabamon hindered idol worship by his teachings. When the emperor 
visited Alexandria, he called him in. Once the saint arrived at Alexandria, he 
was arrested and spent the night in prison, wh ere he joined Pope Peter and 
some priests who saw his countenance shine like an angel. Emperor Diocletian 
tortured the bishop with every tool he had , and the Lord Christ kept healing 
him of every wound . And when the emperor saw how a multitude of people 
proclaimed their faith in the Lord Christ because of him , he decided to give 
him to Ariana the governor of Ansenah to torture him and to cut his head off if 
he persists on his faith. Then, it happened that Ariana was in Alexandria at that 
time, so he took the saint with him by boat. When they reached Nicius, and the 
boat stopped and could not be moved, they took the saint to the northern side 
of the city, where they cut his head off , and he received the crown of 
martyrdom. Afterward, his people came and moved his body with great honor

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 105
passages.text:
105 
 
eternity. The emperor called him and asked him to live in the royal court and 
to accompany him whenever he would go to the Church. And,  Innocentius I 
(401-417 AD), the pope of Rome at that time, was inspired by God that 
Severianus would eventually be entrusted on a great multitude, so the pope 
honored him and revered him, and he became beloved by all. 
In the Greek City of Gabala: 
When St. Severianus noticed how everyone was honoring him, he decided 
in secret for fear that he would lose his labor, to forsake the glory of this world. 
And, an angel of the Lord appeared to him and told him to go to a city called 
Gabala in Greece, where he woul d be in charge of a multitude of believers. 
Then, he set forth at night with his disciple Tadros, whom he clothed with the 
monastic attire. They both were guided by an angel to a monastery headed by 
a saintly man. That Abbot was told in a night vision abou t the coming of 
Severianus, and he came out to receive him and told him about what he saw. 
As he became well known in that region, an uncountable number of people 
came to see him. Emperor Theodosius II (402 -450) reconstructed an old 
monastery for him to dw ell in, and he came to be the cause of comfort for so 
many souls. He continuously taught and guided his monks to become as holy 
as angels. On his hands, God made so many signs, among which was that the 
daughter of the governor of the city was possessed by an unclean spirit. She 
told her father: “If you send Severianus out of our city, I shall get out of your 
daughter.” On learning about it, the saint wrote on a piece of paper: “In the 
name of Jesus Christ, go out of her.” Once the girl read what was written in the 
article, the unclean spirit screamed and came out of her. 
When some sorcerers, along with some soldiers, came to force themselves 
upon his monastery, God struck them with blindness for three days until the 
saint prayed on their behalf, and God healed them. 
Ordained as a Bishop on Gabala: 
Philadelphus, the bishop of the city of Gabala, was told by God through a 
dream that St. Severianus would sit on his throne after his departure. So, he 
informed his people about it. When Severianus, eventually was o rdained as a 
bishop on the city of Gabala, he strove to shepherd his people. It happened that, 
in that city, a Jew called Sectar was boasting about his wide knowledge, and 
he came to debate with St. Severianus. He ended up, along with so many 
sorcerers, be ing convinced of the soundness of the Christian Faith and 
proclaimed their belief in the Lord Christ. In his time, Egypt flourished with 
her monks, the way Constantinople flourished with having St. John 
Chrysostom.

PIUS I, POPE OF ROME 
Saint Pius I (140 -155 AD) succeeded St. Hyginus (136 -140 AD) on the 
See of Rome. He was formerly a citizen of Aquileia in Italy and said to be the 
brother of Hermas author of the book The Shepherd in the 2nd century AD.  
He was ordained as a bishop around the year 140 AD. He cared to oppose 
the heresies faced by the Roman Church in his time, by the followers of 
Valentinus and Marcion. The first Valentinus, originally from Egypt, and he 
dwelt in Rome between the years 136 and 165 AD, hoping to be ordained as 
a bishop. His book carried a lot of Gnostic thoughts. While the second 
Marcion, was considered one of the most influential Gnostics personalities.  
Pope Pius I cared so much to commit the priests to practice the Holy 
Sacraments with great caution and elaboration. So, he issued a creed that 
says: “A priest who spills the chalice after the sanctification, has to remain in 
a condition of repentance for 40 days, and if he spills a drop of it, he has to 
remain in a condition of repentance for three days; along with wiping the 
place of a spill with towels  and burning them.” He also cared to incr ease the 
number of ministers serving the Kingdom of God, so he ordained 12 bishops 
and 18 priests. He was said to be martyred on the 11 th of June in the year 155 
AD, even though some scholars in the West, believe that he reposed without 
having his bloodshed. 
 [Butler’s: Lives of Saints; July 11] 
 
PERGENTINUS (The martyr) 
This saint was one of those who enjoyed the crown of martyrdom in the 
days of Emperor Decius (249 -251 AD) in the city of Arezzo in the region of 
Umbria. St. Pergentinus and his brother Laur entinus were of a noble family; 
they were arrested while still young students, brought before the governor 
Tibertius and charged of being Christians. He set them free, probably for the 
sake of their noble origin or for their young age; counting the mild 
chastisement was enough to make them stop practicing their worship and to 
live in fear and terror. However, once they found themselves free, they set 
forth to practice their Christian worship publicly, and with greater zeal, they 
even began to preach among t he pagans. God granted them the grace to 
perform miracles, that drew many people to the Christian faith. The governor 
put them again under arrest, then gave the order to cut their heads off, to

465 
 
prayers, and to be healed by the miracles granted to him by God. 
In Faran: 
It was also said that by Divine order, he set forth to the wilderness of 
Faran (in Saudi Arabia), where he remained for five years bringing the lost 
souls back to the fold of  faith. Then, St. Pijimi returned to a cave near his 
birth-town of Feesha. That cave became a center for preaching the Gospel 
and to guide the deviants, as well as a place to comfort the  tough and the 
sick. 
An Encounter with Abba Shenouda: 
It was also said  that Abba Shenouda the Archimandrite, in a night vision 
saw that he was carried to heavens and was shown the place prepared for St. 
Pijimi. He was quite impressed and decided to go to Feesha to get his 
blessing. There, after he rested and had some food , both saints praised God, 
prayed, and were comforted by the word of God. 
His Repose: 
When St. Pijimi was told about the day of his repose , he informed his 
disciple, and on the 1st day of Kiahk, he was inflicted by intense fever. On the 
11th of Kiahk, he saw a group of saints coming for him, along with angels, to 
carry his soul to its place of comfort. 
 [A monk in the Syrian Monastery (Virgin Mary’s Monastery): 
 The Biography of the Great Saint Abba Pijimi, the Hermit] 
 
PIOR, ABBA 
Abba Pior (Pihur; in Coptic) his name means (Of the god Horus) and he is 
a different saint from Abba Or the abbot.  He loved the monastic life at a 
young age, and he set forth to St. Anthony the Great in the year 325 AD and 
became one of his disciples for a few years. When he r eached his 25 years of 
age, he longed for a life of seclusion , so he asked the permission of St. 
Anthony and set forth to the region of Nitria around the year 330 AD.  There, 
he dwelt in an isolated cell between Nitria and Scetis. However, he kept 
coming back to Scetis for the rest of his life.  Abba Pior dug a well and kept 
drinking its bitter water for 30 years until he reposed. His visitors used to 
bring their own water with them to drink. It was said that God made the bitter 
water sweet in his mo uth. He kept growing in his asceticism until he got to 
eat only dry bread with five olives a day and persisted on not seeing any of 
his relatives.

PIAMON, THE VIRGIN, ST. 
St. Piamon lived with her mother in one of the villages in Upper Egypt. 
She lived with a holy monastic spirit, spending her life in spiritual watching, 
eating once every day at sunset , and earning her living weaving linen. That 
blessed virgin was worthy of enjoying the gift of knowing what was going to 
happen before it would happen. 
So, one time there was a controversy between her village and a 
neighboring one because of the  irrigation of their land  from the Nile’s water. 
As a result of the quarrels, some of the inhabitants of both villages were 
killed. So, the inhabitants of the other village who were known for their 
violence, planned on a sudden attack on their opponents. Th e Lord revealed 
that planning  to that virgi n Piamon. She hastened to tell the matter to the 
elders of her village , who had a great fear of confronting them, so they 
planned to ask for reconciliation. So, they sought from her if she wished to 
save her village and her household to go to meet with them by herself! 
Not wishing to go to them, she instead ascended to the roof of her house 
and spent the night in unceasing prayers and metanoias, crying out to God, 
saying: “O Lord, the Judge of the whole earth; Who has no pleasure in 
oppression; I implore You O Lord when the prayers and supplications of your 
maidservant reach You, let Your power stop the enemy at the spot where they 
are now.”  Then, three miles from her village, those violent people felt a 
superior power that froze them , and they could not mov e forwards anymore. 
They were told later that it was because of the prayers of that saint. They 
instantly sent to the other village to seek reconciliation, with a message in 
which they told them: “Give thanks to God; for the prayers of Piamon which 
kept us from coming against you.” 
 [W. Budge: The Paradise of the Holy Fathers, Vol. I, pp. 152-3] 
 
PIERIUS, ST. 
Father Pierius has been the dean of the School of Alexandria in the 2nd half 
of the 3 rd century, in the days of Pope Theonas (282 -301 AD). He was a 
cultured priest, a prominent interpreter of the Word of God and a great 
preacher. The historian Eusebius (260 -340 AD) said about him: “He was 
known for his intense poverty, along with his richnes s in the philosophical 
knowledge, his depth in spiritual contemplations, his strife in the 
interpretation of the spirituals and his eloquence in the public debates in

The two guards were cast again in prison, where Lucina served them. 
Pompinius replaced his father Paulinus as the jail officer, and he declared that 
those two guards were magicians. Then, he ordered that they get executed by 
the sword. In this way, they received the crowns of martyrdom. 
  [Baring-Gould: Lives of the Saints, July 2]  
 
PTOLEMAEUS (The martyr) 
During the long Church history, many people have carried the same name 
of Ptolemaeus; among them: 
• Ptolemaeus, the disciple of Valentinus in the 2 nd century AD, which was 
mentioned by St. Irenaeus. 
• Ptolemaeus, the martyr: celebrated in the West on the 19 th of October. He 
was martyred in Rome around the year 161 AD. His contemporary St. 
Justin, the martyr, has testified to him. 
It was said that a married woman was living in a sinful life, and then 
became aware of the Christian faith through this St. Ptolemaeus. After she 
repented, she started to lead a pious life.  Having tasted the sweetness of the 
fellowship with God and enjoyed the holy life, her heart was so inflamed by 
zeal, that she kept asking her husband to receive the faith also. However, he 
kept insulting her and badly treating her that she had to leave him. So, the 
husband told the governor that his estrange d wife was a Christian, and 
accordingly, she was arrested. In the court of justice, her mentor St. 
Ptolemaeus stood before t he governor Urbicius to defend her, and on 
proclaiming his faith, he was condemned to death himself. 
A Christian man by the name of Lucius, who was there during the trial, 
protested before the governor that Ptolemaeus was condemned for no crime 
he committed, which would be contrary to the wisdom of the emperor and 
the council of the elites.  This man also fell under the same verdict. Then, the 
same situation was repeated with a third man, although his name was not 
mentioned. 
 [Justine Mart: Apology 2:2; Eusebius: Hist. Eccl., vol. IV, 17:2-13]  
 
• Ptolemaeus, the soldier: (20 December) was mentioned by St. Dionysius, 
the 14th pope of Alexandria (247 -264 AD) in a letter he sent Fabian the 
bishop of Antioch. The pope narrated what happened in Alexandria during 
the persecution in the era of emperor Decius (249 -251 AD). Among those

Jerome's response. 
Once more, when a controversy between St. Jerome and Rophinus erupted 
about Origen's teaching, although they were good friends since their 
childhood, St. Pammachius declared his denunciation of their fierceness in 
the argument. 
When his wife Paulina passed away in the year 397 AD, both St . Jerome 
and St . Paulinus, the bishop of Nola, wrote him letters of condolence and 
advised him to funnel all his abilities to wards deeds of love . St. Paulinus  
wrote to him, saying: “Your wife now is a deposit for you, and an intercessor 
for your sake before the Lord  Jesus Christ. She would be receiving through 
you a lot of blessings in Heaven when you distribu te her treasures over here 
on earth. Don't remember her by vain tears, but by participating in the deeds 
of mercy. She would be honored by your virtues and fed by the food you 
offer to the poor.” St. Jerome also wrote him another letter inviting him to a 
life of dedication. 
St. Pammachius did distribute much of his wealth on the poor, to practice 
a monastic life; that St . Jerome wrote to him saying: “Although Paulina has 
fallen asleep, the church has gained the monk Pammachius.  According to his 
birth and marriage, he is a nobleman. He is generous in his giving and loft in 
his humility” [Letter # 66 ]. He also said in the same letter, that what 
Pammachius has gained now was the fruit of Paulina; for what she longed to 
see him as while she was alive, has been r ealized by her death . By doing so, 
Pamachius proved to be the wisest of the wise, the greatest and the noblest 
among them, and the most prominent monk. 
Also, St . Pammachius established with Fabiola an inn (hospital) in the 
area of Portus, to be a refuge fo r the strangers who were coming to Rome, in 
particular the sick and the poor among them . In his love for the unity of the 
church, St . Pammachius opposed the Donatic dissension 1 with a spirit of 
humility. He sought from them  to return to the bosom of the c hurch. For his 
good ecclesiastical work, St . Augustine, the bishop of Hippo, wrote St . 
Pammachius to thank him in the year 401 AD. 
St. Pammachius turned his house in Coelian Hill into a church , and 
according to some, the church of SS. Giovany and Paulo (John and Paul) was 
built on its location later on. 
St. Pammachius reposed in the year 410 AD, during the attack of the 
Gosians and the Alaric on Rome . He is celebrated by the w est on the 30 th of 
August. It was said that he was ordained as a priest, but th at was doubted by

St. Pacian had a famous expression: “My name is Christian and my title is  
Universal (Catholic) .” He departed on the 9th of March in the year 390 AD. 
      [Butler's Lives of Saints, Mar. 9] 
 
PAESA, ST. 
Lady St. Paesa was born in the city of Menouf to wealthy parents during 
the 4th century AD, and she was raised in a holy life. Since her childhood, she 
loved the worship of God and serving the poor . When her parents departed, 
she longed to join a house of virgins . She started distributing her wealth on 
the needy, and she gave hospitality to strangers in her ho me. However, the 
devil did not leave her alone but provoked some wicked people to lure her 
heart gradually to evil, until she completely got transformed and gave herself 
up to sin; and turned her house to a brothel. 
On hearing about what happened to her, the fathers of the Scetis were very 
sad, so  they spent some time in prayers and fasting for her, and then they 
sought from St . John the Short to go and talk to her . St. John the Short 
yielded to their reques t. When the time came for her to receive him; he 
entered into her house while singing the psalm: "Though I walk through the 
valley of the shad ow of death, I will fear no evil;  for You are with me” (Ps. 
23:4). When he sat down, he looked at her and said, "Why did you belittle the 
Lord Jesus Christ, and follow this evil way?" She trembled and her heart was 
melting from the words of the saint who bent his head and started weeping . 
Inquiring from him why he was cr ying, he told her that he could see demons 
playing on her face. She asked him if there would be possible repentance for 
her. The saint opened before her the door of hope, providing that she would 
abandon that unclean place and go with him to the wilderness . When it was 
evening, he told her to lie down far away from him . Then, when he got up at 
midnight for his prayer, he saw a pillar of light coming down from Heaven 
and angels carrying her soul . Approaching, he found out that she already 
passed away. He prostrated himself to the ground thanking God for His work 
with her, to hear a voice, saying that her repentance was received at the 
moment she uttered it, for she did it from the depth of her heart. 
He buried her body and set forth to the wilderness to tell the fathers about 
what happened, for which they glorified God . The church celebrates her

counted the priests in Rome slothful and easygoing; and violently attacked the bishop of Rome... He 
drew some bishops to his side, but the 14th  pope of Alexandria St. ‘Dionysius’ (247 -264 AD)

(John 12:35). However, because he was in a rush to see his sick brethren; he 
asked the Lord to hold the sun until he would reach them; which the Lord 
did, and when he saw how his disciples were astonished, he said to them: 
“Don't you remember the Lord's words; If you have faith as a mustard seed, 
you will say to this mountain, “Move from here to there, and it will move, and 
nothing will be impossible for you” (Matt. 17:25). 
Another time, when another one of his disciples reposed in the Lord, and 
he was surrounded by the brethren, the father came and kissed his (body) 
corpse and addressed him, saying: “Do you want, my son, to depart now to 
God, or you would rather remain in the body..?”  Instantly the dead man 
replied: “It is better for me to forsake my body to be with Christ.” The 
blessed father then said to him: “Therefore, my son, lie in peace; and 
supplicate for my sake to God.” All those around were astonished and said: 
“This is truly a man of God.” He shrouded him and kept reading the psalms 
all night, then buried him. 
Another time, standing before the deathbed of one of his disciples, who 
was known for his slothfulness and laziness, the brother kept weeping to beg 
the father to pray for him to be given another chance instead of the years he 
lost in slothfulness. Firmly, yet with love, the father rebuked him, and said: “I 
am ready to seek from God for your sake if you promise not to add to your 
sins new ones.” He fervently implored the Lord, then told the brother that 
God gave him three more years. The brother lived those three years in 
fantastic strife, and once those years came to an end, the fath er came to see 
his disciple before his departure. According to St. Palladius, this saint was not 
a regular man, but he came to be a chosen vessel by God whose actions 
amazed everybody! 
In the simplicity of heart and fantastic faith, God performed countless  
miracles through St. Petarpemtis. According to his disciples, he walked on 
water. When they left him in a closed shut upper room, the angels carried him 
to the place he wished to reach, and he told his disciples that, in a night 
vision, God revealed to hi m the Heavenly Goodness prepared for the true 
monks, which no one could utter or describe.  All that for the sake of his 
amazing faith together with the simplicity of his heart and his humility filled 
with love for God and men. 
 [St. Jerome: History of the Monks; ch. 16] 
 
PETER I, THE 17th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
(The Last of the Martyrs) 
This saint was the fruit of the prayers of his mother, Sofia, the wife of a

felt a vast difference between this praise and what he used to hear in his 
pagan worship. He found himself knocking on the door of the building with 
his tiny hands, then by his feet. When the gatekeeper told the Pope Pontianus 
(230-235 AD) who happened to be there, that a boy was kicking the gate with 
his little feet; he instructed him to open it , saying: “For such will be the 
Kingdom of Heaven.”  When the boy entered into the hall to see a group of 
believers praising God, he simply set forth toward the pope to ask: “May you 
please teach me this amazing song about God in heaven who does whatever 
He pleases?” The pope asked him about his parents, to know that his mother 
passed away, his father and grandfather were still living and that t hey were 
not Christians. The boy remained about three hours listening attentively to 
the pope, until his heart was inflamed with faith. 
His Father Proclaimed His Faith: 
With joy, the boy set forth to tell his father what happened to him. Being 
prudent, the father listened to him to the end, probably not to lose him; but it 
so happened that the father himself, drawn by the talk of the boy, set forth 
with him to the pope to seek his counsel and he joined the rows of the 
catechumen, together with his son to get eventually baptized. 
When the father reposed while his son was 20 years old, the young man 
distributed all his inheritance to the poor and the needy.  He was loved by 
Emperor Philip the Arab (244 -249 AD) and his son , who received 
Christianity on his hands. 
However, during the time of Emperors Valerian and Gallienus (253 -268 
AD), Pontinus escaped to Cimella, near the city of Nice in France, where he 
was arrested by governor Claudius . The latter delivered him to wild bears in 
the amphitheater. However, those bears devoured the executioners but did not 
harm the saint. In anger, the governor ordered that the saint ’s head be cut off. 
His relics were kept in the monastery of St. Ponte, near Nice, whereas his 
head was kept in Marseilles. He was martyred around the year 257 or 258. 
 [Baring-Gould: Lives of Saints, May 14] 
 
PORPHYRIOS (The martyr) 
The Synaxarion of the 3 rd of Baramhat mentions another martyr with a 
similar name Porphyrios (Porphyry).  Most probably, this saint was martyred 
in the days of Emperor Diocl etian (284-305 AD). He was a rich man of the 
city of Banias, who loved the poor and visited those imprisoned. On seeing 
the governor walking in front of his house, he proclaimed his Christian faith 
and ultimately received the crown of martyrdom.

whenever his mind would start to protest against those insults , he would 
address it, saying: “Where am I, compared to St. George the Martyr and what 
he endured, or to St. John the Baptist whose head was cut off by Herod? Where 
am I compared to what the other martyrs had suffered?”  
Because of such tribulations, he som etimes confined himself in faraway 
locations for several months, which he would spend in fervent prayers and 
extended fasting. Looking down on the repentance of his heart, love , and 
strong faith, the Lord Christ appeared to him five times in indescribable glory 
and comforted him. By such apparitions, he was encouraged, endured 
suffering, and maintained his silence. 
God’s Comfort amid the Sufferings: 
On hearing about him, the mamluk sultan Barquq (1382-1399 AD) desired 
to see him. And when the mamluk prince Sodon called him and asked him 
about his life and works , he refrained from answering him . Then, the prince 
ordered to drag him along the streets, spit on him, pluck the hair off  his beard 
and strike him 400 times with a rod until his blood spilled off . In all that, the 
saint kept his silence. Then, they cast him together with his disciple in prison, 
where the Lord Christ appeared to them and healed them. And, when eight 
Coptic prisoners sought from him to pray on their behalf, on the same day, the 
pope came to prison with an order to release them . St. Roweiss often foretold 
the believers about things that would happen to them in the future, and warn 
them against tribulations that would dwell on them. 
He was a contemporary of the 87 th Pope Metheos I (1378-1408 AD). And 
when his disciple came to tell him that the mamluk prince Yalbogha arrested 
the pope together with a number of Christians, he prophesied to him that the 
Virgin St. Mary would take care of the whole situation . Indeed, this actually 
happened, when another prince attacked him, broke down the gates of the 
prison, released the pope and those who were with him . Then, that other 
mamluk prince arrested Yalbogha, then struck him and killed him. 
His Illness and Repose: 
The saint ended up his strife with a severe illness , which he endured with 
incredible perseverance, that he was called ‘The New Job.’ During that illness, 
he was bed-ridden for a whole nine years in silence, sighing, weeping, praying 
for the sake of those who came to visit him. He was healing the sick, while he 
himself was suffering from severe sickness. Then, once he came to know that 
it was time for his departure; he blessed his disciples one by one, made the sign 
of the Cross on every part of his body; and he asked for the presence of the 
Virgin Mary at the moment of his repose. One of the saint’s disciples said later 
on: “At his departure, I have seen a woman shining like the sun, standing next

both letters, St. Vigilius indicated his longing to get the same glory gained by 
those three preachers , which he believed to have been denied him for his 
unworthiness. 
His Martyrdom: 
The crown St. Vigilius longed for; he has gotten after a little while . In one 
of his preaching trips in the secluded valley of Rendena, he happened to kick 
the statue of the god Saturn to the ground by his spiritual jealousy. So, the 
pagans took hold of him and stoned him to death. His martyrdom was in the 
year 405 AD , and his relics  are said to be in Trent along with those of St. 
Maxentia, St. Claudian, and St. Majorian. These saints are said to be his mother 
and two of his brothers. 
 [Butler: June 26] 
 
VINCENT (The martyr) 
This saint Vincent was a deacon in the city of Gascony in southwest France. 
He lived near the end of the 3rd century. It seemed that he was arrested because 
he showed some objection to a celebration held for a pagan feast. Then, he was 
brought before the governor, who ordered his men to spread the saint’s body 
on the ground and tie his stretched hands and feet to huge rocks on four corners. 
While St. Vincent was tied in that way, they started to scourge him violently . 
Then they had his head cut off . By that way, he received the crown of 
martyrdom. In the 6th and the 7th centuries AD, so many Christians came from 
all over Europe to his tomb to have his blessing. 
[Butler: June 9] 
 
VINCENT, THE BISHOP OF SARAGOSSA (The martyr) 
This St. Vincent was ordained as a deacon by St. Valerius, the bishop of 
Saragossa (290-315) in Spain. And, despite his young age, the bishop sent him 
to preach and give sermons to the congregation . When Emperors Diocletian 
(E: 284-305) and Maximian (W: 286-305) issued the 2nd and 3rd decree against 
the Christians in the year 303, Dacian (Dacianus) the evil governor of Spain at 
that time, killed 18 believers in Saragossa and arrested St. Valerius and St. 
Vincent. After a little while, he sent them to the nearby city of Valencia, where 
its mayor cast them into prison to suffer hunger, torture, and reproach with the 
hope that those sufferings would shake their steadfastness . He was surprised

‘Anthony,' among whom are: 
ANTHONY, THE SYRIAN The martyr: 
He was a 20 years old Syrian, a stone builder who was known for his great 
zeal against the idol worshipping. He lived as an anchorite for two years; then 
he returned to his hometown. There, he found the people worshipping the false 
gods. So, he went into their temple and broke all the idols down. He was 
expelled from the city, and he went to ‘Apamaea'. And, when its bishop 
assigned him to build a Ch urch, the pagans were stirred up against him and 
killed him. 
ANTONIUS AL-BEBAWY: The martyr: 
St. ‘Anthony’ (Andona) was born in ‘Beba’ in Upper Egypt by pious and 
merciful parents. Hearing about the sufferings of the martyrs, he set forth to 
‘Arianus,' the governor of ‘Ansena.’ and confessed the Lord Christ before him. 
The governor ordered his men to throw spears at him, but he was not harmed. 
Then, for the fear of that the audience would be encouraged to believe in his 
Christ, he ordered him chained and se nt him to ‘Armanius,’ the governor of 
Alexandria. He sent with him ‘Abimachus’ and two other saints. ‘Armanius’ 
put the three in prison, crucified ‘Anthony’ upside down and tortured him, but 
God was glorified in him. Then, he was sent to the governor of ‘Al-Farma,' 
where he met with ‘St. Mina’ in the prison and both rejoiced by seeing each 
other. The governor of ‘Al-Farma’ ordered combing ‘Anthony’s body with 
sharp iron-teeth combs, and then he cut his head off by the sword. The saint 
received the crown of martyrdom. 
 
ANTHONY, FATHER OF THE MONKS, ST. 
He is considered worldwide as ‘The Father of the Monastic Family ’ and 
‘The Founder of the Monastic Movement ’ in the whole world, even though 
there have been some monastic movements prior to his. 
The saint was born in the village of ‘Komn Al-Aros’ – Beni-Sweif around 
the year 251 AD, to wealthy parents. When his father died, he stood before his 
corpse, contemplated in the mortality of the world, and his heart kindled 
toward eternity. In the year 269 AD, entering into the church, he heard the 
gospel saying: “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to 
the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me ” (Matt. 
19:21). Anthony considered it a personal message for him, and it touched  his 
life. Moreover, when he returned home to his young sister ‘Dios,' he 
proclaimed to her his decision to sell his portion of the inheritance and give its 
proceeds to the poor, to dedicate his life to worship God. On her part, his sister 
also insisted on joining a convent in Alexandria.

Book 3: The Church: The Kingdom of God 
667 
old, after leading an angelic life on earth, St. Anthony the Great met him. St. Paul addressed 
him by name, and they talked about the wonders of God and praised Him. At sunset, a raven 
flew down from a palm tree and brought a full loaf of bread to them, even though it was the 
raven’s habit to bring only half a loaf to St. Paul. On the third day, St. Paul asked St. Anthony 
to bring him St. Athanasius’ vestment, which he then gave to St. Anthony to bury him in it. 
When St. Anthony returned, he found that St. Paul had departed while bowing down in 
prayer. Then, two lions came and dug in the sand to bury St. Paul. 
St. Anthony the Great:  He was born around 251 A. D. in the city of Coma, Egypt 
(Qiman El-Arous). When he was eighteen years old, he heard the Gospel reading: “If you 
want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in 
heaven; and come, follow Me” (Matt. 19:21), and so he sold his possessions, placed his sister 
in a house of virgins, and dwelt in a small hut to learn from a saintly hermit there. After some 
time, he went into the western desert to struggle on his own in a tomb, that was carved in the 
mountain. At the age of thrity -five, he settled at the eastern bank of the Nile at Pispir ( Dayr 
al-Maymūn), where he lived as a hermit, so many came to him and became his disciples. He 
went into the inner desert at Mount Colzim to live in peace and silence. Nonetheless, his love 
compelled him to visit Alexandria to support the martyrs in 316 A. D., and to support St. 
Athanasius against Arianism in 352 A. D. Many people came to be his disciples, and he 
departed in 352 A. D. 
St. Pachomius (Father of the Koinonia):  He was born in upper Egypt around the year 
290 A. D. He became Christian in the city of Esna in Upper Egypt because of their generosity 
and their love for their enemies. He left the army and was baptized around the ye ar 290 A. 
D. He became the disciple of St. Palamon the hermit, till an angel appeared to him and guided 
him to establish the system of the monastic communal life (coenobitic monasticism). He was 
a successful leader who loved the salvation of souls, so he e stablished many monasteries in 
Upper Egypt following strict rules. He also established a convent for nuns under the 
leadership of his sister. His monastic rules were translated to Greek and Latin. St. Basil the 
Great used them, and they were used in the Gaul in the fifth century. They were also adopted 
by Benedict, the father of western monasticism, and by Caesarius of Arles. 
St. Ammonas: He was contemporary of St. Anthony. He was born in 275 A. D., and 
when he was twenty-two years old, his uncle forced him to get married, so he lived with his 
wife as ascetics in Nitria. After eighteen years, his wife asked him to live in solitude away 
from her, so he went out to Mount Nitria and many gathered around him. So, he established 
the semi-eremitic monasticism, in which the monks are not required to have daily fellowship 
in worship or in meals, except for Saturdays and Sundays only. Usually, the monks of this 
order lived in cells or caves that were close to each other, around the church. 
St. Macarius the Great: (around 300–390 A. D.) He is the founder of the semi-eremitic 
order of monasticism in the wilderness of Scetis. He visited St. Anthony at least twice. His 
father forced him to get married, but then God allowed his virgin wife to depart

197 
 
The young man dwelt beside the River Nile and spent all his time praying 
in strict asceticism. Yet, when thoughts of boredom attacked him, he cried out 
to the Lord to guide him. An angel of the Lord appeared to him in the form of 
a man wearing a long robe, with leather cross-like Eskeem and a cover on his 
head. He sat weaving palm leaves for some time, got up to pray, then returned 
to work, and so on. The angel said to Anthony: “If you do so, you will never 
get bored." That  came to be the attire of the monks, and the work of hand 
happened to be one of the basics of the monastic life. 
One day, a woman and her maidservants came down to the river to wash 
their feet. Turning his head away, waiting for their departure, they start ed to 
undress to bathe. When the saint admonished her on such a behavior, she 
answered him: “If you are a monk, you should dwell in the inner wilderness, 
for this is not a place befitting for monks." On hearing these words, the saint 
said to himself, “This is the voice of the angel of the Lord rebuking me." He 
instantly forsook the location and set forth to the inner wilderness. That was 
around the year 285 AD. The saint dwelt in a cave on Mount ‘Al-Kalzam’ to 
practice the life of seclusion, North-West of the Red Sea. However, in that new 
location, the demons kept fighting against him, sometimes in the form of 
women and other times in the way of horrible wild beasts. 
His Order of Seclusion: 
In about the year 305 AD, he had to break his seclusion to meet with  some 
beginners who came to him longing to be trained under his supervision. He 
helped and guided them, then resumed his life of seclusion later on. Thus he 
was the founder of the movement of monasticism, his life revealed the concept 
of the Christian monasticism, particularly the order of seclusion: 
4- St. Anthony came out to be a monk without any intention to become a 
member of the clergy. His movement was a civic one, not a clerical one; he 
did not want to interfere with the ecclesiastical structure. Even, when 
Emperor Constantine I sent to him seeking his blessing, he delayed his 
response to the message, and when asked by his disciples why he did so, he 
said, “I am preoccupied to respond to the message of God, the King of 
kings." However, when he was pressu red, he answered the emperor’s 
message, for the sake of the Church peace. 
5- His intense love of seclusion did not close his heart toward the holy 
congregation, but, in his seclusion, he believed in being a member of the 
Church. That is why he eventually came  down to help Pope Athanasius 
the Apostolic (who was once one of his disciples). Moreover, on his 
entrance into Alexandria, the whole city was shaken, and its inhabitants 
came out exultant to welcome the man of God; that even some Arians 
came back to the Church.

up, approached the saintly hermit, kissed him , and greeted both the king and 
the queen. After that, all stood with submissive and a contrite heart to pray and 
worship. Then, the monk came to give each of them what was needed for their 
hand-work. They worked in silence while singing praise until the ninth hour, 
when a servant brought food to them, which they ate after giving thanks to 
God. The hermit came to know that the king and the queen ate only once daily 
at sunset; watch the night praying  until midnight and live together  with a life 
of virginity. After having dinner with them, the saint bid them farewell, and the 
king, the queen, and the monk did not let him go until they had his blessings . 
St. Yusab returned to Scetis (el-Esqeet), beating his chest.  
And, he lived rejoicing until he reposed in peace. 
 [The Hermit Fathers, p. 25]  
 
YUSTUS ST. ANTHONY, THE MONK 
The monk Yustus (Justus) St. Anthony was born in the village called Zarabi 
near the M uĥarraq monastery in the province of Assiut in the year 1910 . He 
was given the name Naguib. He worked with his father as a tailor , and he 
learned and mastered the Coptic language . He was ordained as a deacon . 
Naguib went to the monastery of St. Paul in the Eastern desert. There, he spent 
two years as a novice. Then, he moved to the monastery of St. Anthony, where 
he was ordained as a monk in November 1941. 
He was always Expecting the Coming of his Master: 
From the very beginning, in his spiritual strife , he rarely closed his eyes . 
Still, he stayed all night wandering around inside the monastery, as though he 
was anticipating the coming of his Lord. And, whenever he needed some rest, 
he would sit underneath a tree for a short nap. In his early stages of strife, he 
used to lie down on the stem of a fallen tree on the ground, to keep himself 
from a comfortable sleeping, and to remain awake for praying all night long. 
Whenever he met with someone, he would ask him: “ What is the time 
now?” as though anticipating the time of his departure. At the beginning of his 
monastic life, he was fighting against evil thoughts. He was able to overcome 
them by staying awake and reciting the Lord’s Prayer in a loud voice, on and 
on, until they would go away. 
Concerning the Holy Bible, he memorized the Psalms and the epistles of 
Paul the Apostle by heart. And, he loved to read the Holy Bible in the Coptic 
language. Concerning his food, he used to eat just a little amount, mainly from 
the bread crumbles, which would fall off the main dinner table, after he would 
soak them in the water while he would give the rest of his food portion to the 
workers and the stray cats . Monk Yustus always lived poor. He never carried

of St. Paul, and shook their heads as if they were asking St . Anthony what to 
do. St. Antony knew that they were sent from God. He marked the place on 
the ground and they dug the grave with their claws ; according to St. Antony's 
directions. St. Anthony then buried the holy body. 
St. Anthony carried the garment of palm t ree fibers and presented it to 
Pope Athanasius who gr eatly exulted to have it, and kept wearing it every 
year in the feasts of Christmas, Theophany , and Resurrection . Many signs 
were shown by that garment. 
In the location where St . Paul the First Hermit used to live, a monastery 
was built where earthly angels dedicated all their lives to that of joyful praise 
for the Lord. 
 
PAUL, THE MONK 
About Abba Ur (Hur), we know that he had a disciple by the name of Paul 
(Boulus) who cared much for the life of prayers, even though he 
misunderstood its meaning . He considered his prayers as a race to recite the 
greatest number of church praises. H e was eventually corrected by St . 
Macarius.  
About him it was said: 
He did not approach the hard handworks or the assignments of selling and 
buying; except for the littl e things he eats every day . However, he was very 
advanced in one thing, which was praying without ceasing. He set for himself 
a rule; to pray 300 prayers every day. He used to put some little pebbles in his 
pocket, and then he used to hold in his hand one of them for every prayer he 
prayed. One day, he came to St . Macarius, saying: “Father, I am very sad .” 
When the elder monk asked him the reason for his anguish, he answered: “I 
heard about a virgin who spent thirty years of her monastic life, reciting 500 
prayers every day . On hearing that, I despised myself, for I am not able to 
pray more than 300 prayers every day.” 
Here, St. Abba Macarius told him: “I lived for sixty years in the monastic 
life, reciting only fifty prayers every day; work ed for  what was e nough to 
earn my need of food; and receive d the brethren who come to seek my 
counsel. Now, here you are who pray 300 prayers every day, condemned by 
your thoughts. You probably, either do not pray them with purity; or you can 
do more of other things and you do not want to.” 
 [The Diocese of Beni-Suef: The Garden of Monks; pp. 24-25] 
 [Budge: The Paradise, vol. 2, art. 356]

162 
 
According to St. Athanasius, while Abba Anthony was sitting one day by 
his monastery, he saw somebody ascending to heaven, and a multitude of saints 
was welcoming him. Inquiring about him, he was told that he was Abba Amon. 
Thirty days later, some hermits came over from Mount Nitria, to inform St 
Anthony that their father has departed to heaven. 
The C optic Church celebrates his feast on the 20 th of Bashons; and the 
Greek Church on the 4th of October. 
 
 
 
 
AMON, THE RYTHIAN, FR. 
He was called that way because he lived in the region of ‘Rythio’ by the city 
of ‘El-Tur’ in Sinai. He was an Egyptian monk who lived as an anchorite in the 
region of ‘Kanub’ (Abu Quir) at the beginning of the fourth century AD. When 
the persecution was stirred up by Emperor ‘Valens’ (364-378 AD), he was 
exiled to Palestine, and from there, he returned to the wilderness of Sinai. He 
witnessed by himself the invasion of the pagan Arabs on the monasteries of 
Sinai when they destroyed the monasteries and dispersed their monks. At that 
time, Amon set forth to ‘Rythio,' which became the center of a gathering of the 
monks of Sinai. He li ved there for a long time until Rythio ’ was invaded as 
well. And, he then left it and set forth to ‘Manf,' then to Scetis to live among 
its hermits as a disciple to Abba Bemen. When he once asked Abba Bemen 
about the evil thoughts; his answer was: “It is within the power of the enemy 
to bring them to our minds, but it is within our power not to accept them!” 
 
AMON, ABBA 
This saint was the disciple of Abba ‘Poemen’ (Bemoa). He came once to 
visit Abba ‘Sisoes’ (Shishoy) in wintertime. And he noticed that Abba  Sisoes 
was very sad and depressed after he left the life of seclusion in the wilderness, 
so he said to him: “Why are you so sad, O father? How could you have 
managed to live alone in the wilderness at your advanced age? ” The old man 
looked at him with admonishment and said: “What are you saying Amon?! Is 
feeling freedom in the desert not better than anything else?!” 
 
AMON, THE BISHOP OF HERMOPOLIS
