After several years, the first Armenian version of the Holy Bible was 
translated from the Syriac language. It was said that St. Mesrop was the one 
who brought the New Testament and the Book of Proverbs to the Armenian. 
These translations were revised in Edessa (El -Roĥa) by two of his disciples. 
Then, a final revision was made by comparing them to the Septuagint version 
of the Old Testament. Also, they managed to translate the Holy Liturgies into 
the Armenian language.  
St. Mesrop preached and taught in Armenia and Georgia, established 
schools, and set another alphabet for Georgia, then he returned to his 
hometown. There, he created a particular school by the encouragement of St. 
Isaac, and he supervised its operation. In this schoo l, he translated so many 
books from the Greek and the Syriac languages to the Armenian language 
with the help and guidance of so many other saints. St. Mesrop reposed when 
he was eighty years old, on the 17th (19th) of February 441 AD.  
 [Butler: February 17 (19)]  
 
METHODIUS, BISHOP OF OLYMPUS (The martyr) 
The Western Church celebrates st. Methodius (Eubilis) on the 20 th of June 
and on the 18 th of September. St. Methodius became the bishop of Olympus 
in Lycia in the southern part of Asia Minor, then became the bishop of Patara. 
He has martyred in the year 311 AD in Chalcis in Greece. He was forgotten 
or disregarded by the historian Eusebius of Caesarea, probably because he 
opposed Origen. This saint was not the same as Methodius, the bishop of 
Petaris in Syria or the bishop of Phoenicia, who was martyred in Syria.  
His Culture and Views: 
St. Methodius seemed to have read Plato's works and admired his dialogue 
style since he authored his essays using the same method. He opposed 
Origen's views about the prior existence of the souls, the resurrection of the 
bodies with the spirit, and that the body is a prison for the soul.  
His Martyrdom: 
According to St. Jerome, St. Methodius received the crown of martyrdom 
during the last days of the persecution stirred up by Emperor Diocletian (284-
305 AD). However, others insisted that he was martyred at the time of 
Emperors Decius (249 -251 AD) and Valerian (253 -260 AD) in Chalcis in 
Greece. Yet, other scholars dismiss the idea of St. Methodius early 
martyrdom, on account of  that he was briefly mentioned by Eusebius of 
Caesarea (265-339 AD), as being one of his contemporaries.

Do not go out for meetings or eat in happy banquets, because this generates 
in you a false appearance which would bring you sorrow and restlessness. 
People are so anxious to find so mebody like that.” The brother asked him 
again: “Then, what can I do ?” The elder father answered: “Wherever you 
dwell, behave the same way as all the others. Whatever the trustworthy pious 
are doing, you do too ; then, you will find comfort. Humility is to be equal to

deviating from it, they will view you on the same level as all the others , and 
they will never disturb you.” 
Being Pleased with People Hostile to Him: 
Fr. Motius's discip le Fr. Isaac told about his mentor that the older saint 
first built a monastery in Arakla, then moved to another location, where he 
also made a monastery. In that second location, there was a brother who 
always opposed him and disturbed him, and became lik e a thorn in his side. 
The elderly saint abandoned that location and went to his village, where he 
built a monastery which he closed on himself. Eventually, the elders of the 
monastery which he deserted came to him along with the brother who was 
hostile to him and planned on asking him to accept him in his new monastery. 
When they approached the place where Fr. Motius was and knocked on the 
door, the elder put a ladder and looked down from the window. Recognizing 
them, he asked: “Where is your luggage?” The y answered: “We left it with 
the brother so & so. ” Once Fr. Motius heard the name of the brother who 
used to disturb him, he broke the door open out of joy and ran to where the 
brother was. He worshipped before him, brought him into his cell, and 
honored him for three days. The brother was so pleased with such an attitude, 
which he did not expect. Later on, the brother left with the rest of the visitors.  
St. Motius was ordained as a bishop, on account of that he had the grace to 
perform signs and miracles, so was his disciple Isaac, who was ordained as a 
bishop as well.  
[Publications of the Light: The Sayings of the Elder Fathers, Lebanon 1983]

persecution stirred up by  Emperor Diocletian (284 -305 AD). His biography 
indicates that he was a prominent sermon -giver who preached in Amphipolis 
in Macedonia.

devil, in the form of an old monk went to St. ‘Christodolus,’ and told him: “At

the Divine Love, who goes above all obstacles setting forth to the spiritual 
work with a solemn Evangelic Ecclesiastical mind.” 
Her grandfather Flavius Ablabius was an influential governor of 
Constantinople and a very close friend to Emperor Constantine I  (306-337 
AD). After the death of the emperor, when Ablabius sided with the 20th Pope 
of Alexandria St. Athanasius the Apostolic who had powerful enemies at the 
court of the new pro -Arian E mperor Constantius II  (337-361 AD); he was 
dismissed from the imperial court and Ablabius retired to his estates in 
Bithynia. In 338 AD, Constantius II condemned Ablabius to death following 
false accusations of intending to usurp the throne . The emperor had her 
grandfather Ablabius executed in front of his own house . However, St. 
Olympias' father Seleucus, was also a governor.  
She was born around the year 368 AD , and when she became fatherless 
while still a young girl, she was cared for by her uncle Procopius, a friend of 
St. Gregory of Nazianzus . She was raised and educated by Theodosia, the 
sister of St . Amphilochius, the bishop of Iconium, a close friend of St . Basil 
the Great . She was influenced, as well, by the great St . Melania the Elder 
(341-410 AD). 
Known for her exalted beauty and riches, she got married while she was 
sixteen years old to Nebridius governor of C onstantinople, who soon died . 
When Emperor Theodocius I (379-395 AD) intended to get her married to his 
relative Elpidius; she firmly refused, saying: “If God wanted me to live as a 
wife, He would not have taken from me my husband Nebridius .” To apply 
pressure on her, the emperor held all her possessions in trust for her until she 
would reach thirty years of age; he also denied her seeing the bishops or 
partaking of the c hurch worship. She wrote to thank him for relieving her of 
the trouble of managing her wealth and to tell him that she would be happier 
if he would distribute all her possessions on the poor . The emperor was 
impressed by her message, and in particu lar, that she set forth to the e ast to 
practice the monastic life with a kindled zeal for four years. So, the emperor 
gave her back all her possessions in the year 391 AD. 
St. Olympias went to St . Nectarius, the archbishop of Constantinople 
(381-397 AD), to declare her wish to dedicate her life to God . So, he set her 
as a deaconess, although she was  still young. Since that time, she established 
a house for virgins (located between the Church of Peace and the Church of 
Hagia Sophia). She also cared for the service of the poor and the sick that so 
many people sought her help.  
As St. John Chrysostom was ordained as an archbishop of Constantinople 
(398-404 AD), he had high regard for St . Olympias since he found in that 
deaconess widow a fiery heart who generously gave all her possessions to

Their Trial: 
In the morning, the governor called them and attempted again to seduce

Their Martyrdom: 
Provoked to anger, ‘Arianus’ ordered cutting their heads off . They forced 
‘Dolagi’ to sit down and started to slay her children one by one on their 
mother’s knees. While they were slaughtering her children, she kept praying 
and singing. Finally, they cut her head. The pure bodies of these saints are still 
kept to this very day in the church , which carries their name in the city of 
‘Esna.’  
The Church celebrates the feast of their martyrdom on the 6th of Bashons. 
The original small church of Mother ‘Dolagi’ remained underground level 
for some time, until the reposed Brigade-General ‘Abadir Adib’ built a church 
at the same location above ground level.

DOMADIUS, THE SYRIAN 
(The martyr) 
Receiving Faith: 
This saint was raised in Persia, where he was taught astrology. He had a  
strong desire to be a Christian. So, it happened that in the market place, he met 
with a Persian monk called ‘Aughalis,’ from whom he learned the way to God. 
He was so jubilant that he kept teaching his household the way to faith. Then, 
he got baptized. 
His Monastic Life: 
Later on, he went to a monastery and became a monk . He lived a great 
ascetic life that brought on him the envy of some brethren . When he sensed 
what was happening, he left them and went to the monastery of St. ‘Sergius,’ 
where he became a disciple to one of their hermits for ten years. During all that 
time, he ate nothing cooked.

MARY (The martyr) 
This saint was born in Atrib. Later on, she got married to a good man 
called Theodore and gave birth to a son, whom they called Sergius. When her 
son went to the governor Kyriacos and confessed h is Christianity, the 
governor tortured him, brought the statue of an idol, and ordered him to 
worship it. The young man, instead, kicked the statue and it fell down 
shattering into pieces. Before such a scene, the governor Kyriacos instantly 
believed in Christianity, saying, “A god, who cannot save himself, how could 
he save others? ” The minister Ohius then came forward and took over 
torturing Serguis with fire and other means. When Serguis’ mother and sister 
arrived at the torturing spot, they kept weeping for seeing him in that manner. 
However, that minister ended up having Serguis’ head cut off by the sword. 
His mother, Mary, his father, and his sister then came forward and 
confessed the name of the Lord Christ, and had their heads cut off by the 
sword too. They all received the crowns of martyrdom on the 13th of Amshir. 
 [Female Martyrs of Christianity, p. 91] 
 
MATHOY, FATHER 
Ordained as a Priest: 
It happened that the elder Mathoy (Mathos) once came out of Raythu to go 
to Magdelon with his brother. The bishop of the area took hold of him and 
ordained him as a priest. Afterward, while they were having dinner together, 
the bishop said to him, “Forgive me, father, I know that you did not want 
that, but I dared to do it to be blessed through you.” The elder Mathoy 
humbly answered, “To some extent, my mind did wish it, however, 
something was disturbing me, that I do not want to get separated from my 
brother because I am not used to do my prayers alone.” The bishop  told him, 
“If you think he is worthy, I may ordain him as a priest too.” Fr. Mathoy 
answered, “I do not know if he is worthy or not; all I know is that he is much 
better than me.”

Fr. Jacob told the following story about Fr. Ma thoy, “I was once visiting 
Fr. Mathoy, and when I intended to leave, I told him, ‘I wish I could visit the 
“Cells.” He answered, ‘Please, Greet Fr. John , for me.’ When I conveyed the 
message to Fr. John, he said, ‘Fr. Mathoy is an Israelite indeed, in whom  
there is no deceit”  (John 1:47).’ A year later, when I conveyed the good

Tadros the Bishop:  
The one thing we know about this saint is that he wrote to St. Augustine 
(354-430) requesting his advice about what to do with the priests who 
apostatized from the heresy of Donatism. That heresy caused a dis agreement 
in the Church, and assume d that the power of baptism depended upon the 
holiness of those who performed the Sacrament and that dissent also rejected 
the repentance of the sinners. 
St. Augustine asked the bishop to receive the priests who apostatized from 
this heresy with the proper compassion . Yet he should, at the same time, 
proclaim clearly to them that he did not accept their previous  opposition and 
that he despised th at heresy. However, he should not disregard the Name of 
God they carry; and should proclaim to them that he believed in their baptism, 
their priesthood, and their vows of virginity . He should accept them, but not 
their sins. St.Augustine requested from bishop Theodorus to show his letter 
[#61] to the others for them to be aware of his point of view concerning that 
subject. 
 
THEODOSIA (The martyr) 
St. Theodosia (Thaodosia) was originally worshipper of idols. She was the 
mother of the martyr Proconius (Aproconius/Procopius) of Jerusalem, and 
after his Christian father Christophorus passed away, she offered precious gifts 
to Emperor Diocletian (284 -305 AD) to appoint her son as a governor on 
Alexandria. The emperor did make hi m a governor and commanded him to 
persecute the Christians there and torture them . However, on his way from 
Antioch to Alexandria, the Lord Jesus talked to him from heaven, and a Cross 
of light appeared to him . So, he believed in the Lord Christ, and his p agan 
mother did report him to the emperor . The emperor asked the governor of 
Caesarea to investigate the matter and to handle his torture if needed. 
St. Proconius was put through so many tortures until he was on the brink of 
death. And, when he was cast in  prison, the Lord Christ appeared to him and 
healed him. When he was called from prison the next morning, and his mother 
St. Theodosia saw him without any wounds, she realized the magnificent 
power of his faith in the Lord Christ. Then, she proclaimed her faith in the Lord 
Christ, and she was joined by two princes and 12 other women in declaring 
their faith in the Lord Christ. All those who joined her had their heads cut off

records.question: How did St. Moses the Black meet his sister Sarah, who was martyred with him?
records.answer:
St. Moses the Black and his sister Sarah were both born to wealthy Christian parents and shared a deep commitment to their faith. After their parents passed away, St. Moses initially planned to marry Sarah off so he could pursue a monastic life. However, Sarah expressed her desire to follow the same path, leading them both to distribute their wealth to the poor and dedicate their lives to God. St. Moses placed Sarah in a convent, while he joined a monastery near Alexandria, and for ten years, they lived apart, focusing on their spiritual lives and prayers without seeing one another [1][2].

Their reunion occurred during a time of persecution against Christians instigated by Emperor Decius. St. Moses sent a message to Sarah to bid her farewell and inform her of his intention to embrace martyrdom. In response, Sarah sought permission from her Mother Superior to leave the convent and joined her brother. Together, they boldly confessed their faith before the governor, enduring torture before ultimately being executed by beheading. They both received the crowns of martyrdom on the 22nd of Mesra [1][2]. 

Thus, their meeting was not only a reunion of siblings but also a powerful testament to their shared faith and commitment to Christ, culminating in their martyrdom together.

giving his sister Sarah in marriage and handing their whole wealth to her. 
However, when he discussed the idea with his sister, she responded to him by 
saying: “If you get married first, then I would follow suit.” He told her: “I 
have committed so many sins, which I intend to atone for by leading a 
monastic life, for I cannot get married and care for my salvation at the  same 
time.” She answered him: “How would you cast me in the snares of this 
world, and care only for your salvation?” Then, he answered her: “Whatever 
you choose will be yours.” She responded: “All that you would do, I shall 
also do, for we are of one fath er and one mother.” Then, they distributed all 
their wealth to the poor and the needy. St. Moises brought his sister Sarah 
into a house of virgins, and he joined a monastery near Alexandria, and for 
the following ten years, they did not see one another.  
Their Martyrdom: 
Then, when Emperor Decius (249-251 AD) incited persecution against the 
Christians, in the days of the 14 th Pope St. Dionysius the Great (246 -264 
AD), so many believers were martyred. At that time, St. Moises sent to his 
sister to bid her fa rewell, and let her know of his decision to be martyred in 
the Name of the Lord Jesus Christ. She hastened to her mother -superior, 
sought to be released, got the blessings of her sisters, and joined her brother 
on his way to Alexandria. There, they both co nfessed together the Lord Jesus 
Christ, and after being tortured by many tools, they had their heads cut off by 
the sword, and they received the crowns of martyrdom.  
 [The Synaxarion: 26 Mesra] 
 
MOISES, BISHOP OF OSIM, ST. 
St. Moises (Moses) was one of th e prominent fathers and saints of the 
church in the 8 th century AD. He was raised on the love of virginity and 
purity since his childhood, and he studied the church's various subjects.  
St. Moises became a monk, since his youth in the wilderness of the Sce tis, 
where he lived in the obedience of a great hermit for eighteen years, during 
which he walked along the road of virtue and harsh asceticism. He became 
known for his virtues that he was chosen to be the bishop of Osim (Ouseem), 
in the district of Embaba in the Beĥeira governorate. His life as a bishop was 
an extension of his monastic one in the wilderness. He was living in a life of 
deprivation and was known for his piety, courage, and zeal on the Orthodox 
faith. He used to spend most of his time in wors hip, that it was said that he 
did not see anyone, except on Saturdays and Sundays.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 65
passages.text:
65 
 
After spending so many years in a continuous spiritual strife, she reposed 
in peace at the right old age. 
 
SARAH (The martyr) 
She Selected the Monastic Life: 
This Sarah and her brother Moises were born to pious Christian parents . 
When their parents died, her brother planned to give her in marriage so that he 
would become a monk . However, she told him that she , too, had the same 
intention. So, he put her in a convent and joined a monastery near Alexandria. 
The two of them worshipped God in prayers and suppli cations for ten years 
without seeing one another. 
Her Martyrdom: 
When Emperor Decius (249 -251 AD) stirred up persecution against the 
Christians during the time of the 14 th Pope of Alexandria St. Dionysius the 
Great (246-264 AD), many believers were martyred. Moises sent to his sister 
to bid her farewell and to let her know about his decision to offer himself for 
martyrdom. So, Sarah asked  for the permission of her Mother -Superior, and 
then she joined her brother . They went together to confess the Lord Chris t 
before the governor . After viciously torturing them, he ordered to cut their 
heads by the sword. And, they both received the crowns of martyrdom on the 
22nd of Mesra. 
 [Female Martyrs in Christianity, p. 35] 
 
SARMATAS (The martyr) 
Becoming a Disciple to Abba Anthony: 
Both St. Sarmatas and St. Macarius the Great were together as disciples of 
Abba Anthony the Great (251-356), the Father of all the Monks. After his spirit 
was saturated with the Divine teachings and the role model of His great teacher, 
Sarmatas left the Eastern desert. They set forth to a mountain by the Nile in the 
region of Pispir (now Deir el -Maymun), opposite Arsinoe in Fayyum, where 
Abba Anthony lived before he moved to the inner wilderness . In that region, 
there was a great monastery who se monks chose Sarmatas to be their abbot . 
The blessings of St. Sarmatas' spiritual father, the Star of the Wildness, dwelt 
on him to shine with the light of Christ.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 256
passages.text:
256 
 
in the form of a girl. She managed to convince him to  spend the night at her 
place. Then, she claimed to him that she was the daughter of one of the kings 
and that she wanted him to marry her, quoting the honor of the marriage of 
the fathers: Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He accepted her request. Then, she 
claimed that she was a Jew, and he had to convert to her religion to be able to 
marry her. So, Moses was blinded, and he denied his Christ. Then, she (the 
deceptive devil) took him back to the wilderness, where a whole gang of 
devils ridiculed him and made so much fun of him. Finally, the hermit woke 
up and cast himself on the dust and kept crying and supplicating to the 
Compassionate God to forgive him. God sent him Abba Samuel, who told 
him that he would be departing after three days. Then, he took him to the  
church, where he gave him Communion in the Holy Sacraments after 
confessing all that the devil has done to him. St. Moses, the hermit, reposed 
in peace and was buried by Abba Samuel, who wrote his biography, and 
handed it to someone traveling to Alexandria for the benefit of the believers.  
 [The Hermit Fathers, Part 2, p. 25] 
 
MOSES, THE LIBYAN, ST. 
This saint was from Libya. He was so humble and compassionate all the 
time that God granted him the grace to perform the miracles of healing the 
sick. He once said: “When I was young, I lived in a monastery. There, it 
happened that eight monks dug a well, and seventy others built a wall around 
it, in the hope that they would get water from it. They dug it down to the 
depth of about twenty yards, but no water was found. They were very much 
grieved and intended to fill it up with dirt. However, by noontime, w hen 
Abba Pieour came over suddenly to the location of the well and was 
informed about what they were doing, he rebuked them saying: ‘Why did you 
despair, O you of little faith? ’ Then, he went down to the bottom of the well, 
and he prayed there. Afterward, he pushed an iron rod in the well bottom 
three times, saying: ‘O God of the saints, I pray, do not waste the effort of 
these men, but send them plenty of water.’ In a short while, the water erupted 
from the well and wetted everyone around.  
After praying a  thanksgiving prayer, Abba Pieour intended to go in his 
way. They tried to make him have a meal with them, but he said: ‘I have 
accomplished what I came here to do, I did not come here to eat.’”  
This was a good lesson for the brethren about faith and the trust in God.  
 [The Paradise of the Saints, p. 69]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 239
passages.text:
239 
 
the eyesight to read the Scriptures, the ears to hear the Divine sermons and 
the strength to stand to pray.” 
Becoming a Hermit: 
When the Abbot of the monastery heard about the asceticism of St. Misael 
and came to visit him, Misael told him: “After three days, some men in 
soldiers attire will come to seek me from you. Have neither fear nor sadness, 
because it is the will of God, and allow me to go with them, and you shall 
know that there will be a famine on the land in this coming year, but I shall 
come back to you then.” On hearing this, the Abbot purchased an excellent 
quantity of grains, and eventually, the men in the soldiers' attire came, took 
Misael, and went their way. When the famine came, the governor came with 
his men to confiscate whatever he would fin d in the monastery of grains, but 
a group of those soldiers stood in his way, and the governor had to back off in 
failure. Then, the Abbot wanted to welcome those soldiers and to offer them 
food to eat, but they said to him: “We do not need anything of the  sort.” 
Then, one of them came forward, held the old monk's hand, and said to him: 
“I am your son Misael, and those men in the soldiers' attire are hermits, who 
came here last year to take me away with them. Now, I implore you to go to 
Abba Athanasius, the  bishop of my hometown, tell him about me and seek 
from him my inheritance, then use it to build a church in my name and invite 
the father bishop to consecrate it.” 
So, Abbot Abba Isaac went to the bishop, and he was given 700 measures 
of gold and 900 meas ures of silver, many books, and 500 heads of sheep, 
besides many fabrics and vessels. The Abbot demolished the old house, 
purchased the neighboring land, and built a church there. While the father 
bishop was consecrating it, St. Misael, together with the f ather's hermits, 
came to attend the consecration ceremony. Then, St. Misael approached Abba 
Isaac and told him: “Next year, you will depart from this world.” Then, he 
went his way with the rest of the hermits.  
 
MOUGI (The martyr) 
Refer to the two martyrs Thecla and Mougi. Their biography could be 
found under the letter ‘T.’  
 
MOISES AND HIS SISTER SARAH, (The martyrs) 
These two saints were born to wealthy Christian parents. When their 
parents passed away, St. Moises (Moses) intended to become a monk after

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 253
passages.text:
253 
 
going. When they insisted on having him, he came car rying a bag of sand 
with a hole in the back, which he explained by saying: “My sins run out 
behind me and I do not see them, but today I am coming to judge the errors 
of another. ” On hearing this, the assembled monks forgave their sinful 
brother.  
For some reason, it was proclaimed an obligation in the Scetis to fast for a 
week. During that week, some guests came to visit Fr. Moses. He prepared 
food for them to eat. On seeing smoke rising from his cell, the brethren said 
to one another: “Look, Moses has bro ken his fast and is preparing food for 
himself. We shall talk to him about it.” When they got to know the facts, they 
said to him: “Father Moses! You have disregarded the commandment of men, 
but kept that of God (i.e., giving hospitality to strangers).”  
His Martyrdom: 
Then, it happened that the Barbarians came to attack the monastery, an 
incident St. Moses knew by Spirit beforehand, and he sought from the 
brethren to escape. However, seven brethren stayed behind, and they asked 
him: “Are you not going to escape, father?” He answered: “For a long time, I 
waited for this day, for the words of the Lord Jesus Christ to be fulfilled: “ All 
who take the sword will perish by the sword” (Matt. 26:52). They said to 
him: “We shall stay with you and will not escape.” H e told them: “There, 
they are already at the gate.” The Barbarians entered the monastery and killed 
them all. However, when one of the seven escaped to the stronghold out of 
fear, he saw seven crowns coming down from heaven on the seven martyred 
monks. The n, he hastened to come down and ran forward to receive his 
crown of martyrdom.  
So, Abba Moses completed his strife on the 24 th of Paona in the year 408 
AD, when he was seventy -five years old (or eighty -five). He earned three 
crowns: the 1 st for love and i ntense asceticism, the 2 nd for monasticism and 
priesthood, and the 3rd for martyrdom. He was counted the first martyr in the 
Scetis, and he had so many great teachings. His body was kept along with 
that of his spiritual guide Abba Isidore in one tube at th e Paramus monastery 
in Natrun Valley.  
Of his Sayings: 
• To a brother in the Scetis who sought from him a word of encouragement, 
he said: “Go and sit in your cell, it will teach you everything.” 
• The man who flees from the world is like ripe grapes, but he who dwells 
among the distractions of men is like sour grapes.  
• If we keep the commandments of our fathers, I promise you that the

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 255
passages.text:
255 
 
would be unreasonable for a man to leave  his dead son, and go to mourn 
that of his neighbor. 
To die about your neighbor means to worry about your sins and not to 
care for the sins of any man, good or bad. You should not do wrong to 
anyone, or think bad about anyone else in your heart or despise anyone for 
doing wrong. You should not obey anyone who harmed his neighbor or 
rejoice for him. You should never slander anyone, but always say that God 
knows everybody's heart. Do not go along with the man who talks bad 
about his neighbor, because it would  make you fall in condemnation. Do 
not have hatred against anyone. Do not have a grudge in your heart against 
anyone, and do not hate the man who is hostile toward his neighbor. This 
would bring you peace. 
[Sayings of the Strong Saint Abba Moses, Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria-
Diocese of Los Angeles] 
 [Moses the Black: On the Internet Site of OrthodoxWiki] 
 [Moses the Black: On the Internet Site of Wikipedia] 
 
MOSES THE HERMIT 
St. Moses, the hermit, was born in Alexandria. Once he reached the age of 
thirteen years, he set forth to the wilderness of the Scetis. There, he dwelt for 
twenty years in a small cell next to one of the older monks. Then, he went 
deep in the wilderness an d lived for thirty -five years in a spot having olive 
and palm trees. There, he ate according to his needs whatever would fall from 
the trees, drank from the rainwater, dressed in palm leaves, and befriended 
the wild beasts.  
His Multiple Falls and Repentances:  
Satan envied this hermit, so he appeared to him in the form of an older 
man. The older man told him that he used to live a corrupt life, but he 
repented and distributed his wealth to the poor. He lived in one of the Five 
Western Cities (Pentapolis) near Cyrenaica (Barqa), and that God revealed to 
him that the hour of his death was approaching. They walked together in the 
wilderness until they reached a grand mansion. Then, the older man told the 
hermit that after his death, that mansion would be his, if he would marry his 
daughter. Moses was deceived and thought that the older man was on the 
brink of extinction, so he accepted his offer. However, once he declared his 
acceptance, he found himself amid the wilderness, hungry and afraid. He 
could not see any mansion there, and he realized that it was a trick from the 
devil. He felt how he was so weak and offered sincere repentance.  
Once St. Moses also went to Alexandria, where the devil appeared to him

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 250
passages.text:
250 
 
master got rid of him. He turned into a gangster who lived on robbing and 
killing people. He had a large, muscular stature, which helped him to become 
the head of an evil gang.  
Having Faith in the Lord Jesus Christ: 
Even though an extreme evil -doer, yet he kept raising up his eyes towards 
the sun, believing that it was the true God, seeking fr om it to proclaim itself 
to him. Then, he heard a voice telling him to go to the wilderness to 
encounter the monks of the Scetis, whose fame was widely spread all over 
the area at that time. He went there, carrying his sword, where he happened 
to meet with  St. Isidore (The Priest of the Cells ) coming out of his cell and 
heading to the church. Terrified by his appearance, the saint asked him: 
“What do you want from here, O brother?” Moses answered: “ I heard that 
you are a good servant of God . Therefore, I es caped and came to you to let 
God save me the way he saved you.” He continued in persistence and with 
submission, saying: “I want to remain with you, despite my countless sins 
and my great evils.” 
St. Isidore kept asking him about his past life and where he  has been. 
Moses confessed to him all the sins he committed. On seeing how he opened 
his heart to him, St. Isidore started to teach him and preached him at length 
the word of God, he told him about the judgment to come and then left him to 
contemplate.  
For hating evil and deciding to rid himself of it, Moses shed so many 
tears, and deep remorse swept his soul and disturbed his sleep, like a dreadful 
ghost. Then, he went to St. Isidore, prostrated himself before him, and in a 
loud voice, he confessed all hi s evil crimes again, with such contrition of 
heart that drew his compassion. He took him to Abba Macarius the Great, 
who put him under his care, taught him and guided him, gave him the grace 
of baptism, then put him back under the supervision of St. Isidore.  
His Monastic Life: 
After a while, Moses sought from Abba Isidore to make him a monk. 
However, Abba Isidore started to explain to him how tough the monastic life 
is with the constant fight against the demons and the other physical needs. He 
told him as a way of testing him: “It is better for you son, to go and live in 
the populated areas,” but after seeing his real intention and solid stand, St. 
Isidore sent him back to Abba Macarius the Great, the father of the 
wilderness.  
Moses stood in the church and  confessed publicly about all his sins and 
evil deeds. Abba Macarius said afterward that he saw during Moses 
confession a whiteboard with black writings, and with every sin Moses

62 
 
SARAH AND HER TWO SONS (The martyrs) 
In Antioch: 
St. Sarah was born to Christian parents at the end of the 3 rd century AD in 
the city of Antioch. When she grew up, she was given in marriage to someone 
called Socrates, a leader in the army of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD), and 
one of the elites in Antioch. This Socrates happened to be a friend of the martyr 
Abadir. However, he abandoned his faith to please the emperor . He also 
claimed to his wife that he did that out of fear of the emperor. 
Baptizing Her Two Sons: 
Sarah was granted with two sons . And, when she wanted to have them 
baptized, she could not do it in Antioch. So, she sailed to Alexandria to have it 
done there, On the way, a strong storm started , and the ship was on the brink 
of sinking . Sarah, for fear that her sons would die without being baptized, 
raised a long prayer, plunged them three times in the water , then faced East, 
and said: “I baptize you in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.” 
Then, she made a cut in her right breast, and with her blood, she made the sign 
of the Cross on the foreheads of her two sons . Then, it happened that the sea 
calmed down, and they reached Alexandria safely. Sarah went to the 17th pope 
Peter the Seal of the Martyrs (302 -311), to have her infants baptized by him . 
However, when the pope attempted to baptize them three times and each time 
the water froze like a rock, he asked Sarah about her story. She told him about 
what happened to her at the sea . The pope praised God and kept repeating: 
“And we confess One baptism for the forgiveness of sins.” 
Her Martyrdom: 
When Sarah returned home , and her husband got to know what she has 
done, he angrily told the emperor, who called her before him. He rebuked her 
and accused her of committing adultery with the Christians in Alexandria. She 
sharply rebuked him and told him that Christians do nothing of that sort / The 
emperor ordered his men to tie her hands behind her back and to place Sarah 
lying down with her two sons on her belly, then to burn all three of them alive. 
She kept praying to her Creator and Redeemer . and their souls ascended like 
fragrant incense before the Divine throne. And, they all received the crowns of 
martyrdom.  
This martyr presented a living example across the generations of the zeal of 
the believer on the salvation of his brethren; and of how, in case of extreme 
emergency, the believer (a layman) could baptize one another, by wounding 
himself and making the sign of the cross on him by his blood in the Name of

records.question: What year did St. Barbara move to Egypt and where did she live there?
records.answer: The passages do not specify the exact year St. Barbara moved to Egypt or the specific location where she lived there. They mention that she was born in a village near the city of Nicomedia and that she was martyred, with some historians suggesting she might have been martyred in Heliopolis, Egypt, but they do not provide details about her relocation to Egypt or her residence there. Therefore, I could not find enough about that in the loaded sources.

courage, talked to him about her faith in Christ.  
St. ‘Barbara’ was then whipped until her b lood started pouring. They also 
tore her flesh by hitting her with sticks full of sharp nails. During that time, she 
kept silent and continued praying to her God. Then, they clothed her in rough 
sackcloth over her torn body full of wounds, and she was cast  in a dark 
dungeon. 
While she was suffering from her wounds, the Lord Christ appeared to her 
in the dungeon, comforted her, and healed her completely. 
When the governor called for her on the next day, he was astonished to find 
her exultant with no traces o f any wounds on her body. He grew much more 
violent and sought from the executioners to comb her body with sharp iron 
combs, to put flames on her sides, and to cut off her breasts. Then, he ordered 
them viciously to lead her naked along the streets of the town. At this point, 
she cried out to the Lord to cover her nakedness, and God responded by 
engulfing her in Divine light. 
On seeing her amid her incredible sufferings, a girl by the name of ‘Juliana’ 
bitterly cried; and the governor ordered to torture her along with St. ‘Barbara,’ 
and to cast them together in the same dungeon. There, they kept praying all 
night long. 
Their Martyrdom: 
Governor ‘Martinianus’ gave the command to cut the heads of the two saints 
by the sword. While being lead to the arena outsi de the city, they kept on 
praying. And once they arrived there, ‘Dioscorus’ sought from the governor to 
let him kill his daughter by himself, and he was allowed. So, both St. ‘Barbara’ 
and St. ‘Juliana’ finally received the crowns of martyrdom. Their bodies were 
placed in a church outside the city of ‘Galatia.' 
St. ‘Barbara's father perished shortly after their martyrdom, and so did the 
governor who tortured her. The water of the basin that had the cross over it in 
the bathhouse had the power to heal everyone who washed with it. 
The body of St. ‘Barbara’ is kept now in a church under her name in Old 
Cairo. And, according to some historians, she might have been martyred in 
Heliopolis, Egypt. 
 
BARBASYMAS, THE BISHOP , ST. 
(The martyr) 
St. ‘Barbasymas’ (Barba'shmin) succeeded his brother St. ‘Shahdost’ as a 
bishop on the diocese of ‘Seleucia-Ctesiphon’ in the year 342 AD. 
This saint was inflamed with zeal on faith and the care of God’s people, and 
this stirred up the devil to consider him of being an enemy of the  Persian

298 
 
they allowed those two hermits to worship another God on that same mountain. 
Forty young pagan men dedicated themselves to kill the two hermits, but God 
kept them safe and hid them away from their sight. 
Their Martyrdom: 
Then, it happened that ‘Maximianus, the partn er of Emperor ‘Diocletian,’ 
came to Egypt to supervise by himself the persecution and to enjoy seeing by 
his own eyes the shedding of the blood of Christians. 
The priests of the great idol went to complain to the emperor about what 
took place, and how thei r god declared his anger because of the presence of 
those two hermits on their mountain. At the same time, the Archangel 
‘Michael’ appeared to the two saints to tell them that the emperor would be 
seeking them and that the heavenly crowns were prepared for  them. The two 
saints then set forth from the mount to the messengers of the emperor and went 
with them to proclaim their faith before him. He gave the order to cut their 
heads off, and they received the crowns of martyrdom on the 7 th of the month 
of Kiahk. 
 [The Synaxarion; Edition of Rene Basset] 
 
 
BARBARA, ST. 
(The martyr) 
Saint ‘Barbara’ has gotten great fame in the East and the West; she endured 
so much to hold dearly to her faith. The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on 
the 8th of Kiahk and the Western Church as well as the Greek Church on the 
4th of December. 
Her Upbringing: 
She was born in the village of ‘Gamis’ near the city ‘Leopolis’ in 
‘Nicomedia,’ at the beginning of the 3rd century AD, during the days of 
Emperor ‘Maximinus I ’ (235-238 AD). He r father ‘Dioscorus’ was a firm 
believer in his pagan worship and strongly hated Christians.  
On seeing how beautiful she was and worrying about the corruption of that 
time, her father built for her a high tower and surrounded it by guards, and 
filled it with idols and all kinds of entertainments. He also provided her with 
great teachers who cared for her advanced learnings. 
‘Barbara’ having been a lover of meditation, she used to lift her eyes to look 
at the sun, the moon, and the stars, praising the God who created the earth with 
everything on it for the sake of humans. 
One day, some of her Christian servants told her so many good things about

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 156
passages.text:
156 
 
Gethsemane. While they were going in their way, some Jews came and tried 
to prevent them from burying her. When one of them stretched his hands to 
hold the coffin, his arms separated from his body and remained hanging until 
he believed and showed remorse on his evil deed. By the supplications of the 
saintly disciples, his arms were attached back to his body.  
It happened that Thomas the Apostle was not present at the time the Virgin 
St. Mary reposed. However, in his way back to Jerusalem, he saw her 
shrouded body being carried by the angels to be taken up to heaven; and he 
was advised by one of the angels to hasten and kiss her pure body,  which he 
did. When he arrived to join the disciples, and they told him about her 
departure, he said to them, “I shall not believe unless I see her body, for you 
already know how I doubted the resurrection of the Lord Christ.” They took 
him to her tomb and  were shocked and surprised to see it empty. However, 
Thomas, the Apostle, told them how he saw her pure body with the angels 
carrying it up to heaven. The Holy Spirit told them that God did not intend 
for her pure body to remain on earth, and the Lord Chr ist promised his pure 
disciples to let them see her in the flesh again, and they waited for this true 
promise until the 16 th of the month of Mesra when it was fulfilled. She lived 
on earth 60 years: she spent 12 years in the Temple, 30 years in the house o f 
the righteous Joseph the Carpenter, and 14 years in the house of St. John the 
Evangelist, according to the commandment of the Lord, who said to her: 
“Woman! Behold your son,” and to John: “Behold! Your mother” (John 
19:26-27). The first church, which was  built in the name of the Virgin St. 
Mary, was in the city of Philippi, in Greece. That happened after the 
preaching of St. Paul and St. Barnabas to the Gentiles in that city, and when 
many of them believed, they built that church. 
The Virgin St. Mary prov ided twice special blessings to the Land of 
Egypt. The first time when she fled to Egypt with the infant Jesus and St. 
Joseph the Carpenter, running away from king Herod who intended to kill the 
infant. the second time when she appeared in spiritual ways, inside and 
outside the domes of the church consecrated in her name in the area of El -
Zeitoun, in the suburbs of Cairo on the 2 nd of April 1968 (24 Baramhat 1684 
AM). Her appearances continued for many consecutive nights. 
The Church celebrates the Birthday of St. Mary on the 1 st of Bashons, her 
Entrance into the Temple on the 3 rd of Kiahk, her Departure on the 21 st of 
Toba, the Ascension of her body to Heaven on the 16th of Mesra, Building the 
first Church in her name on the 21 st of Paona, Consecrating the church in her 
name in the ‘Muĥarraq’ monastery, which the Lord Christ blessed by his 
presence along with His Apostles, on the 6 th of Hator and her Apparition in 
the church of El-Zeitoun on the 24th of Baramhat.

In the year 1961, Pope Cyril VI  (1959-1971) made mother Kyria the 
mother-superior of St. George Convent in Old Cairo. As a mother-superior, she 
cared for the spiritual activities and established a library for the convent, which 
included so many manuscripts. She was known for her generosity, even for the 
stray pets like dogs and cats, and for distributing monthly help to the unknown 
poor families. God granted her the grace of knowledge about so many events 
before they happened. Also, St. George the martyr appeared to her to inform  
her about the time of her departure from this world.

309 
 
and the serpent you shall trample underfoot. ” (Ps. 91:13). Then, God took 
away the wild nature from the serpent and turned it into a companion of the 
saint for the following 20 years. 
As the sw eet fragrance of Christ spread from the saint, multitudes came 
from all over the country, seeking his blessings and prayers. 
His Support for those in Anguish: 
In his days, the church passed through very intense anguish, at the end of 
the 8th Mamluk reign of the sultan ‘Khalil ibn-Qalawoon’ (1260-1293 AD). He 
closed the churches all over Egypt, except for those in Alexandria, and he 
issued a decree that did commit all Christians to wear blue turbans . As for St. 
‘Barsum,’ he kept praying in the church, refusing to wear a blue turban. When 
some reported him to the ‘Sultan,’ he ordered him to be whipped, cast in jail, 
then released him to dwell on the roof of the church, where he kept praying 
with metanoias  and tears to God, to take His wrath away from his peopl e, 
forgive their sins, and make compassionate those who ruled over them.  
When he was reported again to the ‘Sultan,’ he was whipped and cast in jail, 
then released to set forth to the monastery of ‘Shahran’ in the vicinity of the 
‘Press of Helwan,’ where he lived a very harsh monastic life; but was supported 
by God, who granted him the grace to perform miracles and signs . So, many 
of those who were suffering came forth to find in him a heavenly comfort, and 
by his prayers, God eventually lifted the anguish.  
On the 5th day of the Coptic little month of ‘Nasie’ (the forgotten days), the 
saint reposed in the Lord at 60 years of age. 
 [Library of ‘Mahabah’: Abba Barsum El-Ărian, Cairo 1978 
  – including many of his miracles] 
 
BARSUMA, BISHOP OF NASSIBINS 
He wa s a Nestorian bishop on ‘Nassibins’ (Nisibis), before whom the 
Persian king opened the doors of his palace to spread the Nestorian heresy. He 
attempted to make ‘Nassibins’ an independent diocese from the diocese of 
‘Selucia–Ctesiphon,’ and he also established a theological school there. 
 
 
BARSUMAS, THE SYRIAN ABBA, ST. 
The Coptic Church celebrates the feast of the repose of St. ‘Barsumas’ the 
Syrian, the abbot of the Syrian monks, on the 8th of Amshir. He reposed in the 
year 458 AD. His family was from the region of ‘Samosata.’ Before his birth, 
a saintly man of God prophesied to his parents: “You will produce a good fruit,

and then she crossed the river walking on the water. Seeing that miracle, the 
priest Zosimus attempted to bow before her. She cried out loudly, “O Father 
priest, what are you doing? Did you forget that you are carrying the Holy 
Sacraments?” She then approached, worshipped with reverence, took the 
Holy Sacraments, then raised her hands toward heaven, crying out: “Lord, let 
your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen Your Salvation .” (Luke 
2:29-30) She asked him to come to her in the following year, in the same 
place, to pray for her. She made the sign of the Cross on the river, crossed it 
back walking on the water, and disappeared from his sight. 
Her Departure: 
In the following year, and in the appointed time, the priest se t forth to the 
designated place, where he found the saint worshipping to the ground, with 
her face directed toward the East, and her hands motionless. Perceiving that 
she was already dead, he worshipped beside her, cried, and prayed on her the 
funeral prayers. Up to this moment, he realized that he did not even come to 
know her name; but when he got close to her, he found a written message 
saying, “Father Zosimus! Bury here the body of the miserable Mary and 
leave to the dust this sinful body. Pray on my behalf.”  
Fr. Zosimus realized that she died the year before after she had the Holy 
Sacraments he brought for her. It is believed that she reposed in the year 421 
AD. Returning to his monastery, Fr. Zosimus kept saying to himself: “Indeed, 
the tax -collectors, the sinners and the adulterers will precede us to the 
Kingdom of Heaven.” St. ‘Mary’s life was a big motivator for so many to 
expand their spiritual strive. The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on the 
16th of Baramouda every year. 
[Fragrant Bouquets from the Biographies of the Righteous and Saints, pp. 249-253] 
[The Vita of St. Mary of Egypt written by St. Sophronius, the patriarch of 
Jerusalem (634–638 AD)] 
 
MARY, THE ISRAELITE (The martyr) 
During the early life of St. Mary, the Israelite, she did not know the Lord 
Christ, and she led a sinful life. When she wanted to repent and to return to 
the righteous life, the Lord sent to her a saintly man who preached her and 
revealed to her the way of  salvation through believing in the Lord Christ. He 
told her that the soul would have to give an answer for all her deeds on the 
Day of Resurrection. After death and departure from this world, everyone 
will be rewarded according to his deeds. The man explained to her the fearful 
punishments for the evildoers. She asked him: "What are the proofs to what 
you have said to me since the ‘Torah’ that God gave to ‘Moses the Prophet’

daughters. 
Paula's heart was day by day i nflamed with the longing to the Heavenly 
life; while the atmosphere in Rome was suffocating for her because of the 
fame of her noble fami ly and the criticism she got from her family elders , so 
she planned to leave Rome and go somewhere else to worship God in 
tranquility and peace away from her family and her old friends. 
In the year 385 AD, she sailed along with her daughter Eustochium  to 
Cyprus. There, they visited St . Epiphanius, the bishop of Salamis , and from 
there, they sailed to Antioch, where they met with St . Jerome. Then all of 
them set forth to the Holy places in Palestine , and from there, they went to 
Egypt to see some of its desert monks and hermits. 
In Egypt: 
St. Paula accompanied St . Jerome on his trip to Egypt and was most 
probably with him when he met with St . Didymus the Blind, the d ean of the 
School of Alexandria. She studied at his school for one month; then set forth 
together with St . Jerome to the wilderness of Nitria. In Nitria , they stayed a 
long time . St. Jerome described the effect of that period on the life of that 
saintly widow, he said that she was excited and joyful to see these saints and 
longed to imitate their lives. The fathers received her with joy, for which she 
glorified God and felt unworthy of such an honor . She met with the two 
Macariuses, St. Serapion and others . She visited them in their cells, 
prostrated herself at their feet, feeling that the Lord  Jesus Christ was in every 
one of them. She tolerated the harsh traveling between the cells and spen t the 
nights in the open wilderness with joy and enthusiasm beyond the endurance 
of any woman . She forgot her fatigue and all her needs because of her 
spiritual joy. 
In Bethlehem: 
In the next year, she set forth to Jerusalem to live in Bethlehem. There, she 
built a guest -house to gi ve hospitality to strangers, a monastery for monks 
and a convent for the nuns. 
In the convent, she  lived along with her daughter Eustochum  a serious 
monastic life, and according to the convent' s rules, all practiced the work of 
the hand, particularly sewing for the nuns or those outside. 
Paula lived among the nuns as a mother who drew them with her love, 
tenderness and she was their role model . Even though she and her daughter 
partook of ministry and work, yet she was firm . If, for instance, she noticed a 
nun talk too much or showing anger ; she would ask her to separate herself 
from the congregation, to pray outside , and to eat her meals alone for a 
certain period.

ascetic life in a small hut in a village for about ten years under the guidance of an ascetic. He 
longed for solitude, and so he moved to Scetis and a cherub accompanied him on the way. 
He loved worship and asceticism, so many came from the East and the West to the wilderness 
to become his disciples. 
St. Shenoute the Archimandrite: He was the abbot of the White Monastery in Athribis 
(or Atripe), in the wilderness of Thebes for over fifty-six years (fourth or fifth century A. D.). 
He led 2200 monks and 1800 nuns. He was called the “Archimandrite” as he practiced 
solitude from time to time, and he encouraged the monks at his monastery to retreat to the 
wilderness after practicing the life of fellowship. In the year 431 A. D., he accompanied St. 
Cyril the Great to the Ecume nical Council of Ephesus. He is known for  purifying Coptic 
literature of Hellenistic cultural influences, and did not allow any foreigners to join his 
monastic communities. For this reason, he was regarded as a political leader and a social 
reformer, besides the depth of his spirituality. 
Amma Sarah : The first monastic group of women in the world was in the city of 
Alexandria, following the rule of St. Syncletica. St. Athanasius documented her biography 
and teachings. Moreover, St. Pachomius established two convents for nuns, while many nuns 
lived in solitude in the desert. Many mothers came from foreign convents to Egypt, like St. 
Melania the Elder (374 A. D.) and her granddaughter Melania the Younger (418 A. D.). Also, 
we cannot forget to mention St. Mary of Egypt who repented in Jerusalem and lived for forty-
seven years in the wilderness across the Jordan not seeing the face of another human being, 
except St. Zosima twice in the last two years of her life.  
Many nuns were given the gift of true leadership and spiritual discernment, like St. Sarah 
of whom it was said that she lived for sixty years on the banks of a river, but never lifted her 
eyes to look at it. Many of her sayings were preserved in the sayings of the desert fathers and 
mothers.  
St. Hilaria: In the fourth century, the daughter of Emperor Zeno fled to Scetis where she 
led a life of asceticism in the attire of a male monk. When her sister, Theopiste, was possessed 
by an evil spirit, the elders of the wilderness sent her to St. Hilaria to pray for her, and did 
not know that St. Hilaria was a woman. She prayed all night for her and embraced her. 
Theopiste was healed, and she told the emperor about the monk, “Hilarion,” who healed her 
and was embracing her, so her father was disturbed. He called for her to come to the palace, 
where she revealed to him that she was his daughter after he had promised not to prevent her 
from going back to her cave. 
St. Syncletica: Some historians regard her to be the equal of St. Anthony, the star of the 
wilderness; for as St. Anthony was the father of all monks, St. Syncletica was a mother to 
that group of virgins which transformed the fertile valley of Egypt into a dwelling place for 
the grace of God. She was born to noble parents who settled in Alexandria to be close to the

passages.text: دعوة للانضمام إلى روما كان من بني مصر الذين اقتنصهم الكاثوليك بعيدًا عن كنيستهم الأصلية، ورسموه أسقفًا باسم كيرلس مقابل الأنبا كيرلس الخامس البابا المائة والثاني عشر. حالما تسلم هذا الأسقف مهامه الرعوية نشر رسالة وجهها إلى الأرثوذكس الأوفياء لكنيستهم في مصر وفي إثيوبيا يناشدهم فيها الانطواء تحت زعامة البابا الروماني بادعاء أن مرقس ما هو إلا تلميذ لبطرس. وعلى الفور أصدر البابا الوقور بيانًا مسهبًا أوضح فيه العقيدة الأرثوذكسية في جلائها، ثم أثبت أن مار مرقس هو أحد السبعين تلميذًا الذين اختارهم الرب للكرازة كما دعى الاثني عشر تمامًا، وقد طُبِع هذا البيان ووُزِع في جميع أنحاء مصر وقرأه الكهنة في الكنائس على مسامع الشعب. لما وجد كيرلس مقار أن البيان البابوي بلغ هدفه وبالتالي فشل هو فيما استهدفه، قصد إلى إثيوبيا وهناك أصابه فشل ثانٍ لأن الإمبراطور منليك الثاني كان شديد التمسك بالأرثوذكسية. وبعد شهور من تلك الزيارة جاء وزير إثيوبي إلى مصر وذهب لينال بركة الأنبا كيرلس الخامس فسأله عما حدث، ووصف له الوزير ما جرى وانتهى بقوله: "إذا توطدت أقدام البعثات الدينية في أي بلد شرقي أضاع استقلاله شيئًا فشيئًا، وإذا به على غير علم منه قد وقع في قبضة من زعموا تمدينه وتعليمه". بطريرك للكاثوليك فعودة للكنيسة ثم رفعت روما هذا الأسقف إلى مرتبة بطريرك، وبعدها فوجئت بما لم يكن في الحسبان، لأن الأنبا كيرلس مقار كان دائم البحث والإطلاع فلم يلبث أن عاد إلى الأرثوذكسية. ظن في بادئ الأمر أن البابا المرقسي الأصيل لن يقبله ضمن أبنائه بسبب كتاباته السالفة ضد الكنيسة القبطية، فسافر إلى الإسكندرية وقابل البطريرك فوثيوس للروم الأرثوذكس وصارحه برغبته في الانضمام إلى كنيسته. وفرح البطريرك الرومي هو ومجمعه بقبول الطلب ولكن رجال الدولة اليونانية رفضوا الموافقة رفضًا باتًا، وبينما كان كيرلس مقار في الإسكندرية وضع كتابًا في جزءين عن العلامة السكندري أوريجينوس بالفرنسية. فلما رُفِض طلبه سافر إلى بيروت حيث انشغل بالكتابة، فوضع كتابين على جانب كبير من الأهمية إذ يقدمان الدليل الواضح الصريح على مدى اقتناعه بالأرثوذكسية، وهذان الكتابان بالفرنسية أيضًا، أولهما: "الوضع الإلهي لتأسيس الكنيسة" وهو في جزءين، وثانيهما: "أخيرًا الحقيقة". ثم أتبعهما بكتاب ثالث عنوانه: "أخيرًا نتكلم"، ردّ به على بعض ما نشره الكاثوليك في مصر. قد تبعت ثمانون عائلة كاثوليكية بطريركها وانضمت إلى الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية وأشهرها عائلة "العتر"، وعلى إثر ذلك أصبح فرنسيس العتر أرشيدياكون الكنيسة البطرسية التي شيدتها عائلة بطرس غالي. ثم حدث أن تقابل بعض من أراخنة الأقباط مع فرنسيس العتر ودار بينهم الحديث حول كيرلس مقار، وفي اليوم التالي ذهبوا لمقابلة الأنبا كيرلس الخامس، الذي ما أن علم به

passages.text: ✞ غالي المعلم جمع الضرائب كان كاتب محمد بك الألفي أحد أمراء المماليك، ثم أسند إليه محمد علي منصبًا كبيرًا بعد غضبه على المعلم جرجس الجوهري، وكان المعلم غالي يسهل لمحمد علي أمر تحصيل الضرائب، ولكن هذا الأمر انقلب وبالاً عليه في النهاية. فكان جشع محمد علي في تحصيل الضرائب لا يقف عند حد، فقد طلب الباشا محمد علي من المعلم غالي ألف كيسًا، فقسم جمعها على المباشرين والكتبة وجمعها في أقرب وقت. محمد علي يغدر به كان جمعها بسرعة موجبًا لغير ما كان يتوقعه المعلم غالي، وسببًا في جلب الغدر عليه وعلى غيره، فإن الباشا بعد قليل أمر بمحاصرة بيته، وبيت المعلم جرجس الطويل، وأخيه حنا، وفرنسيس أخي المعلم غالي، والمعلم فلتاؤس، واثنين آخرين وأخرجوهم من منازلهم بصورة منكرة وسمّروا دورهم، وأخذوا دفاترهم وحبسوهم، وبعد أيام أفرج عنهم على شرط أن يدفعوا سبعة آلاف كيس فقاموا بدفعها. ولم تمضِ سبعة شهور حتى قبض عليهم ثانية وحبسهم في القلعة وختموا على دورهم، ثم عفا عنهم وأعاد المعلم غالي إلى منصبه، على شرط أن يدفعوا أربعة وعشرين ألف كيسًا. وتكرر حدوث ذلك من محمد علي، فكان يغضب عليه تارة ويعزله من منصبه ويرميه في السجن ويضربه مئات الكرابيج، ثم يعيده إلى منصبه بعد دفع مبلغٍ طائلٍ. وعندما أراد محمد علي تغيير هيئة الدواوين واستبدالها بغيرها، لتكون أقدر منها وتفوقها في النظام، حتى تعود بالفائدة على الخزينة، لم يتردد في الإفراج عن المعلم غالي والاستفادة من خبرته وكفاءته، مادام هذا يعود بالفائدة على الخزينة. وبعدما كلّف المعلم غالي بذلك، قسم المعلم غالي البلاد إلى مديريات وأقسام، والأطيان إلى أحواض، وابتكر أشياء كثيرة وحسابات تحقق مقدارًا وافرًا من المال، ولذلك يُنسَب للمعلم غالي تأسيس مصلحة المساحة، كما كان له دوره في تشجيع صناعة الأسلحة محليًا. ومن أعماله الجليلة أيضًا اقتراحه على محمد علي حفر قناة بين بحر الروم وبحر العرب ولكنه لم ينفذ. ونتيجة لنجاحه الكبير قابله محمد علي بالرضا وأثنى عليه ومن ثم َّ اتخذه كاتمًا لسره وخصّه مباشرة الأعمال الحسابية التي ابتكرها، فكانت يده فوق يد الجميع حتى حكام الأقاليم. أطلق إبراهيم باشا رصاص مسدسه عليه استمر المعلم غالي في هذا المنصب حتى مايو سنة 1882م، حين أطلق إبراهيم باشا رصاص مسدسه عليه في مدينة زفتى، أمام ابنه طوبيا فخرّ صريعًا. وهكذا ألقى المعلم غالي جزاء أمانته ووطنيته وخدمته، بعد أن أدى أجلّ الخدمات لمحمد علي ولإبراهيم باشا قاتله. وقد بقيت جثته ملقاة مدة يومين لا يجرؤ أحد على القيام بدفنها حتى استأذن رزق أغا حاكم الشرقية في دفنها، فأقيمت الصلاة على المعلم غالي بكنيسة أبي سيفين بزفتى ثم دفن بجوارها. 32

passages.text: ✞ يوحنا بن زكريا ابن السباع هو أحد مشاهير الرجال في القرن الثالث عشر. كان لاهوتيًا ضليعًا وضع كتابًا بعنوان: " الجوهرة النفيسة في علوم الكنيسة " في 113 فصلاً، أوضح فيها طقوس الكنيسة وتعاليمها. وقد تضمن التعاليم عن التثليث والتوحيد وخلق الملائكة والعناصر والإنسان، ثم شرح الآيات الجوهرية في سفر التكوين والوظائف الكنسية وممارسة السيد المسيح لها على الأرض، فالأسرار المقدسة والبخور والأيقونات والمجمرة والمعاني الرمزية لهذه كلها وكذلك الأعياد الكنسية. وقد وصف المستشرق الألماني جراف يوحنا بن زكريا بأنه من كبار العلماء وبأن كتابه من المؤلفات المسيحية ذات العبارة الفصيحة ودقة البحث. قد طُبِع الكتاب طبعة قديمة وله طبعة حديثة سنة 1902م قام بها الرهبان الفرنسيسكان بالقاهرة. وللأسف لا نعرف شيئًا عن بقية حياته. وطنية الكنيسة القبطية وتاريخها، صفحة 178 . قصة الكنيسة القبطية، الكتاب الثالث صفحة 146 . ✞ يوحنا صاحب الإنجيل الذهبي رهبنته وُلد هذا القديس بمدينة رومية من أب غني يسمى أطرافيوس. ولما كان يوحنا يتلقى العلم طلب من أبيه أن يُجَلِد له الإنجيل الذي يقرأ فيه بالذهب، فعمل له ما أراد ففرح به كثيرًا. واتفق أن أحد الرهبان قد نزل عندهم عند ذهابه إلى بيت المقدس فطلب منه يوحنا أن يأخذه معه، فأعلمه أنه ذاهب إلى القدس وليس إلى الدير، ثم عرفه أنه صغير السن ولا يتحمل عيشة الرهبان التقشفية، غير أن يوحنا كان صادقًا في عزمه فسافر وحده في سفينة إلى دير ذلك الراهب. ولما رآه الرئيس لم يرد أن يقبله لصغر سنه وافهمه أن عيشة الرهبان شاقة على من هو مثله. ولما ألح يوحنا عليه ورأى فيه الرئيس ثبات العزم وقوة اليقين حلق له شعر رأسه والبسه ثوب الرهبنة المقدس، فأجهد يوحنا نفسه بنسكيات وتقشفات زائدة، وكان الأب الرئيس ينصحه قائلاً: "ترفق بنفسك وسِر مثل سائر الاخوة" فكان يقول له: "إن قوة الله وصلاتك عني تعيناني". عودته إلى بيت أبيه بعد سبع سنوات رأى في رؤيا من يقول له: "قم اذهب إلى والديك لتأخذ بركتهما قبل انتقالك من هذا العالم"، وتكررت هذه الرؤيا ثلاث ليالٍ متوالية، فأعلم الرئيس بها، فعرف إنها من الله وأشار عليه بالذهاب. 271

passages.text: انيسيوس Vitellius Anisius ليقتلهما ضربهما "بالعتلة" على رأسهما فنالا إكليل الاستشهاد. Rev. Baring- Gould: Lives of Saints, April 15. 399

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 76
passages.text: منعوه فناداه قائلاً: "تشجع يا جندي المسيح، فإنني أرى ملاكًا فوق رأسك وبيده إكليل جهادك ". ضرب الجلاد رقبته، فطارت رأسه وسلم روحه في يد مخلصه وهو في الثانية والعشرين من عمره. نور يشرق على جسده تُرك جسمه في العراء تحت حراسة مشددة، وفي منتصف الليل ظهر نور عظيم أشرق على الجسد، فذُهل الحراس وارتعبوا. إذ سمع الخليفة المستنصر بذلك أمر بدفنه، فجاء والد الشهيد نيقام ودفن جسده عند كنيسة الملاك المختارة، بجوار بستان المختار الذي غرسه الأخشيد بجوار مقياس الروضة. استمرت هذه الكنيسة قائمة إلى زمن البابا مكاريوس الثاني ) 1102 - 1128 .( بعد ثلاثة أيام من استشهاده جاء البابا خريستوذولس إلى الكنيسة وأمر بأن يُدفن داخل الكنيسة. وإذ أخرجوه من القبر كشف البابا أكفانه ليتبارك منه ودفنه في مقبرة خاصة داخل الكنيسة بإكرام جزيل. إذ هُدمت الكنيسة نًقل الجسد الطاهر إلى كنيسة الملاك ميخائيل القريبة من حصن بابيلون. نبيل فرج ميخائيل: سيرة الشهيد نيقام التائب، مايو 1991 . ✞ نيقوستراتُس الشماس Nicostratus شماس روماني ومن المعترفين، وذلك سنة 253م، وفي الغالب أنه كان في الأصل عبدًا، إذ كان مسموحًا برسامة العبيد بعد موافقة أسيادهم ثم يعقب ذلك إطلاق سراحهم. وفي مجمع ألفيرا Elvira سُمِح برسامة العبيد المعتوقين فقط بعد وفاة مواليهم. احتمل نيقوستراتُس التعذيب مع مويسيس Moyses وماكسيموس Maximus كما كان مثلهم من الملتصقين بنوفاتس Novatus ومؤمنين بعقيدته. ولكنهم عادوا إلى إيمان الكنيسة الجامعة، وسافر نيقوستراتُس مع نوفاتس إلى قرطبة Carthage لدفع هذه العقيدة. A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. IV, page 42. ✞ نيقوستراتُس الشهيد St. Nicostratus قائد primiscrinius في روما عاش حوالي سنة 287م ورد اسمه في سيرة القديس سيباستيان Sebastian إذ آمن بواسطته بينما كان 32

passages.text: ✞ يونيوس الشهيد St. Jonius كاهن وشهيد من بلاد الغال Gaul، تُعي ِّد له الكنيسة الغربية في الخامس من شهر أغسطس. تذكره بعض كتب تاريخ الشهداء باسم يوناس Jonas في 22 سبتمبر A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. III, page 431. 365

passages.text: Eulalius أسقف نزيانزا Nazianzus وابن عم غريغوريوس النزيانزي، وكانت والدته سيدة بارة. أحب يولاليوس هو وشقيقه هيللاديوس Helladius أن يعيشا حياة الوحدة، فاشتريا مزرعة لكي يعتكفا فيها عن العالم، إلا أن البائع كان رجلاً غير أمين حتى أنهما بعد أن أنفقا مبلغًا كبيرًا من المال على المزرعة اضطرا لبيعها بسعرها الأصلي الذي اشترياها به. 341

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 1832
passages.text: ولكنه رغم قسوته وثق بالكاتب يوأنس الذي أصبحت له حظوة خاصة لدى ،قرة فرأى أن يستخدم هذه الحظوة فيما يعود بالخير على .قومه فقال :لقرة إنني" ىَرْأد ببني قومي وأعلم من هو أقدر بينهم على دفع الجزية ومن منهم الفقير .المحتاج فإن شئت يا مولاي جمعت لك الجزية دون أن يستمر هذا الضجر البادي على الشعب ".كله فوافقه قرة على طلبه وصرح له بالتجول في البلاد لجمع ،الجزية فخرج يوأنس من عند الوالي وبدأ عمله .مباشرة توحيد المسيحيين في مصر قد فاضت عليه النعمة الإلهية مكافأة له على تقدمه ،للخدمة فمكنته من أن يتفاهم مع الخلقيدونيين ويعيدهم إلى الإيمان ،الأرثوذكسي كما مكنته من التفاهم مع الغانانيين الذين كانوا قد كونوا شيعة من عهد الأنبا بنيامين البابا الثامن والثلاثين وضمهم اًأيض إلى الإيمان .الأرثوذكسي فأسفرت جهود يوأنس عن توحيد جميع المسيحيين في مصر همّوضم تحت رعاية البابا .السكندري قصة الكنيسة القبطية، الكتاب الثاني صفحة 333 . الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية والروحانية، ص 82 - 83 . ✞ يوبسيكيوس الأسقف الشهيد St. Eupsychius هو أول أسقف على مليتين Meliténe بأرمينيا التي تعي ِّد له في 28 من .مايو يقال أنه استشهد في زمن الإمبراطور غورديان الثالث Gordian III، وذلك في سنة 238 .م A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. II, page 299. ✞ يوبلُس الشهيد St. Euplus 233

passages.text: الحب الأخوي والوحدة 902 . يقول القديس إكليمنضس السكندري: ] الله كل شيءٍ لكل أحدٍ. لهذا فإن كل الأشياء ملكية مشاعة، فليت الأغنياء لا يدعون بأن لهم الحق في أخذ ما هو أكثر من غيرهم. أعطانا الله السلطة أن نستخدم ثروته، لكن حسب الضرورة، وهو يريدنا أن نستخدمها مشاعًا للكل. فمن الظلم أن يقيم شخص وليمة ويتمتع، بينما يعيش كثيرون في فقرٍ 903 [. إن كان الأغنياء يفتخرون بممتلكاتهم، فإنها يوم تُنزَع عنهم لا يختلفون في شيءٍ عن عبيدهم وجواريهم، وإنما غالبًا ما يكون هؤلاء السادة أضعف منهم صحيًا. لهذا لا تعجب إن سمح الله لخدامه 903 Paedagogus 2: 12. 902 Cf. Ignatius, ad Magn., 7: 1. 901 On Naboth, 11. 900 On the Duties of the Clergy, 1:128:132. 899 On Naboth, 1. 898 Letters, 153 to Macedonius, 26. 897 Homilies on John, 15:3. 896 Homilies on Matthew, 77:3. 895 Homilies on 1Cor., homily 11:5. 276

passages.text: تحدث بمجد الرب" )مز 19 : 1 .( يقتصر عمل الملكة )النفس( على تمجيد الله، ويقتصر عمل الجنود السمائيون أن يمجدوا الخالق. كل الخليقة الناطقة أو غير الناطقة، الأرضية أو السماوية، تُمَج ِّد خالقها. أولئك الذين يتركون منازلهم للاجتماع في الهيكل )بحياة غير مقدسة( يستحقون الشفقة، لأنهم لا يستمعون لكلام حق، ولا يقيمون نفوسهم على ضوئها. لقد سبتهم الخطية دون أن يتأثروا، لا يتألمون بسبب خطاياهم التي يتذكرونها، ولا يخشون الدينونة، لكنهم يتصافحون مع بعضهم، ويجعلون من بيت الصلاة مكانًا للثرثرة، محتقرين قول المزمور "في هيكله الكل قائل مجد" )مز 29 : 9 .( أما أنت، فلم تكتفِ بعدم إعطاء المجد لله في هيكله، بل زدت على ذلك مضايقة الآخرين. تريد أن تجذب اهتمام الآخرين نحوك، وبالضوضاء الذي يصدر عنك تمنعهم من الاستماع لتعليم الروح. انتبه إذن لئلا تكون نهايتك مثل نهاية الذين يُجَد ِّفون على اسم الله!... كيف تمجد الله؟... ليت لسانك يترن َّم، وفكرك يفحص الكلمات التي تقولها حتى ترنم بالروح والذهن ) 1 كو 14 : 14 .( فا لا ينقصه المجد، لكنه يريدك أنت! يريدك أن تكون أهلاً أن تُمَج ِّده! فالذي يزرعه الإنسان إياه يحصد أيضًا )غل 6 : 7 .( ليتك تزرع لمجد الله فتحصد الأكاليل والكرامة والتسبيح في ملكوت السماوات. في هيكله الكل قائل مجد" )مز 29 : 9 .( لم تأت هذه الكلمات من فراغ، لأن في هيكل الرب يوجد الذين يثرثرون بلا توق ُّفٍ. وجودهم في الهيكل باطل. ليس باطلاً فقط بل وسبب في دينونتهم 48 [. رابعًا كن جادًا في الصلاة بإيمان واهرب من تشتيت الفكر. يقول القد ِّيس باسيليوس: ] بنا أن نسأل العون الإلهي لا بكسلٍ ولا بفكرٍ مشت َّت هنا وهناك، فإن إنسانًا كهذا ليس فقط لا ينال ما يسأله، بل بالحري يُغضِب الله. لو أن إنسانًا يقف أمام رئيس تكون عيناه ثابتتين في الداخل والخارج حتى لا يتعر َّض للعقوبة، فكم بالحري يليق بنا أن نقف أمام الله بحرصٍ ورعدةٍ؟ لكنك إن كنت تُثار بخطي َّة ما، فلا تقدر أن تُصل ِّي بثبات بكل قو ِّتك. راجع نفسك حتى متى وقفت أمام الله تُرك ِّز فكرك فيه، والله يغفر لك، لأنك ليس عن إهمال بل عن ضعف لم تستطع أن تظهر أمامه كما ينبغي. إن ألزمت نفسك بهذا فإنك لا تتركه حتى تنال. فإن لم تنل ما تسأله يكون ذلك لأن سؤالك غير لائق أو بغير إيمان، أو لأنك قد َّمته باستهانة، أو تسأل أمورًا ليست لصالحك، أو لأنك تركت الصلاة. كثيرًا ما يسأل البعض لماذا نصل ِّي؟ هل يجهل الله ما نحتاج إليه؟ أنه بلا شكٍ يعرف ويعطينا بفيض كل الزمني َّات حتى قبل أن نسألها، لكن يجب علينا أولاً أن نطلب الصالحات وملكوت السماوات، عندئذ ننال ما نرغب لنسأل بإيمانٍ وصبرٍ، نسأل ما هو صالح لنا، ولا نعوق الصلاة بعصيان ضميرنا 49 [. يقول القديس كيرلس الكبير: ] و

passages.label: كاتيكيزم الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية, p. 33
passages.text: عدم وجود وصايا صريحة تأمر بذلك، لكن هذه الصلوات صارت قواعد مستقر َّة في حياة الكنيسة منذ بدء انطلاقها، فقال: ] من ملاحظتنا عدم وجود وصايا خاصة بهذه الممارسات لكن َّه يُحسَب أمرًا صالحًا أن تستقر كقواعد محددة نلتزم بها وتُذَك ِّرنا بالصلاة. وإذ تُعتبَر إلزامي َّة في أوقات مُحد َّدة تسحبنا من أعمالنا لممارسة واجبٍ كهذا وفي نفس الفصل يؤك ِّد ضرورة الصلاة باكر وعشية بجانب الصلوات السابقة، إذ يقول: ] بجانب الصلوات النظامي َّة الواجبة علينا، يلزم على الإنسان أن يُصَل ِّي دون مُذَك ِّر في بدء النهار وبدء الليل كما تحد َّث عن صلاة نصف الليل بطريقة غير مباشرة حينما تساءل عن موقف المرأة التي تتزو َّج غير مؤمن كيف تقوم من فراشها في نصف الليل لتلقي بهذه اللآلئ أمامه. 925. هل التزم المؤمنون بصلوات السواعي في العصر الرسولي؟ جاء في الديداكي َّة "تعليم الرب للأمم بواسطة الاثني عشر تلميذًا: ] تُصَل ُّوا كالمرائين، بل كما أمر الرب في إنجيله. صَل ُّوا هكذا ثلاث مرات في اليوم 88 . ] الوثيقة التي ترجع إلى ما بين عام ٠٧ و ٠٥١ م تكشف لنا عن ممارسة المؤمن لثلاث صلوات يومي َّة في عهد الرسل، وإن كانت لم تحد َّد مواعيدها، فذلك لأن َّها كانت أمرًا مستقرًا عليه، تسل َّمته الكنيسة عن التراث اليهودي وهي صلوات الساعات الثالثة والسادسة والتاسعة. ويرى 89 Jungmann أن هذه الصلوات قد أُخِذَت عن دانيال النبي ) ٦ : ٠١ ( الذي كان يذهب إلى بيته وكُواه مفتوحة في عُل ِّي َّته نحو أورشليم ويجثو على ركبتيه ثلاث مر َّات ويصل ِّي. لم تذكر الديداكي َّة شيئًا عن صلاة باكر والنوم، ذلك لأن المؤمنين كانوا يمارسونها معًا بطريقة جماعي َّة، فلا حاجة للشعب أن يوصى بها. يظهر ذلك مم َّا ورد في الدسقولي َّة كوصي َّة للأسقف 90 : ] الشعب وأُطلب منهم أن يلازموا الكنيسة باكر وعشية كل يوم، لكي لا يتخل َّفوا عنها، بل يجتمعوا فيها كل حين، فلا تضعف الكنيسة بقيامهم خارجًا عنها أشارت الديداكي َّة إلى الصلاة الرباني َّة، لأن المسيحي ِّين كانوا يشتركون في المجامع في الترن ُّم بالمزامير والطلبات ولا يقدرون أن يشتركوا معهم في الصلاة الرباني َّة. كشف لنا سفر أعمال الرسل عن ممارسة الكنيسة الأولى لصلوات السواعي، لذا قيل عن الساعة الثالثة : "كان الجميع معًا بنفسٍ واحدة، لأن َّها الساعة الثالثة من النهار" )أع ٢ : ١ ، ٥ (. وعن الساعة السادسة : "صعد بطرس على السطح ليُصل ِّي نحو الساعة السادسة" )أع ٠١ : ٩ (. وعن الساعة التاسعة : "صعد بطرس ويوحنا معًا إلى الهيكل في ساعة الصلاة التاسعة" )أع ٢ : ١ (. وعن صلاة نصف الليل : "ونحو نصف الليل كان بولس وسيلا يصل ِّيان ويُسَب ِّحان الله" )أع ٦١ : ٥٢ (. يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] أن يُغط ِّي وقت الصلاة الحياة كلها، ولكن حيث توجد ضرورة مُلزمة أن يتخللها ركوع )مطانيات( وترنم بتسابيح. فقد عُينت ساعات للصلوات بواسطة

passages.label: كاتيكيزم الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية, p. 34
passages.text: قبل اختفاء القمر، والآخر بعد ذلك. بهذا يصير التسبيح السباعي اليومي لله نموذجًا لنا 91 [. 926. هل يمكن أن نُتَم ِّم واجبات الصلاة وسط العمل؟ يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] للصلاة والتسبيح كل الأوقات مناسبة... يمكننا وسط العمل أن نُتَم ِّم واجبات الصلاة 92 [. 927. ما هي المناسبة التي وراء كل ساعة من ساعات الصلوات؟ 93 أولاً صلاة باكر. يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] كل ساعة صلاة ذكرى خاصة ببركات الله علينا. يلزمنا أن نُصَل ِّي في الصباح الباكر لكي تكون بدء ميول النفس والعقل مكرسة لله، وأننا لن نلمس شيئًا ما لم نبتهج أولاً بالتأمل في الله كما يقول الكتاب: " تذكرت الرب فابتهجت" )مز 77 : 3 LXX .( ولن نبدأ أيّ عمل ما لم نُتَم ِّم ما هو مكتوب: " إليك أصلي يا رب. بالغداة تسمع صوتي. في الصباح المبكر أوجه صلاتي إليك وأنتظر" )مز 5 : 2 - 3 .( ثانيًا صلاة الساعة الثالثة. يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] أخرى في صلاة الساعة الثالثة حيث نمارسها والإخوة مجتمعون، بالرغم من أنهم تفر َّقوا إلى أعمالهم المختلفة. إذ نذكر عطية الروح القدس التي قُد ِّمَت للرسل في وقت الساعة الثالثة، يلزمنا أن نتعب َّد معًا في اتفاقٍ واحدٍ، لكي نتأه َّل نحن أيضًا أن نَقْبَل تقديسه. يلزمنا أيضًا أن نسأل قيادته وتعليمه حسب احتياجاتنا كما يقول المرتل: " قلبًا نقيًا اخلق فيّ يا الله وروحًا مستقيمًا جدده في داخلي لا تطرحني من حضرتك وروحك القدوس لا تنزعه مني. امنحني راحة عونك أسندني بروحك المحرر" )مز 51 : 10 - 13 .( دع روحك المحب يقودني في أرض الأبرار )مز 143 : 10 .( عندئذ نعود إلى أعمالنا. ومع ذلك يكون بعض الإخوة غائبين بسبب العمل، أو لبُعد مسافة السكن، ومع ذلك يلزمنا أن نُتَم ِّم التزامات الجماعة بدون ترد ُّدٍ. " لأنه حيثما اجتمع اثنان أو ثلاثة باسمي فهناك أكون في وسطهم " )مت 18 : 20 [.( ثالثًا صلاة الساعة السادسة. يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ]في الساعة السادسة أيضًا نقرر ضرورة الصلاة مقتدين بمثال القديسين، كما هو مكتوب: " في المساء وفي الصباح وفي الظهيرة أخبرك ... ولكي نتخل َّص من الضجر ومن شيطان الظهيرة )راجع مز 55 : 17 ؛ مز 90 LXX [.( رابعًا صلاة الساعة التاسعة. يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] الساعة التاسعة ساعة مناسبة للصلاة كما نتعل َّم من الرسل في سفر الأعمال، حيث يُقَال إن بطرس ويوحنا صعدا إلى الهيكل في ساعة الصلاة وكان وقت الساعة التاسعة )أع 3 : 1 [.( خامسًا صلاة الغروب. يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] على هذا إذ ينتهي اليوم، يلزم تقديم شكر من أجل البركات التي نلناها والأعمال الصالحة التي تم َّت خلال اليوم. وأيضًا اعتراف عن الخطايا. وسواء كان الخطأ بإرادة أو بغير إرادة، خفية ومنسية سواء بكلمة أو بفعل أو بأفكار القلب، يلزمنا أن نجعل الله يهدأ من ناحيتنا بصلواتنا. فإن فحص أفع

passages.label: كاتيكيزم الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية, p. 37
passages.text: الروح القدس بوضوحٍ وعورة الطريق إلى ممارسة الفضيلة. يرى كيف يميل الجنس البشري إلى المزامير بكونها أغانٍ منظوم فيها الحق، لصغار السن وصغار النفوس، وإن كان الإنسان ينسى سريعًا كلمات الوعظ والنبوة، إلا أنه لا ينسى المزامير التي يُرَد ِّدها كثيرًا، في البيت، وفي الخارج. وترتيل المزامير يطرد الغضب الذي يجعل من الإنسان حيوانًا مفترسًا، ويسرق منه سلامه، ويملأه ثورة. التسبيح بمزمورٍ يجلب هدوءًا للروح ، فنستقر في سلامٍ، كما يهدئ عواصف أفكارنا العنيفة. فهو يسيطر على الشهوة، ويطفئ النار التي في صدورنا قبل أن تلتهب. أتريدون أن ترتبطوا بصداقةٍ وتصالحوا المتخاصمين ويغفر الأعداء لبعضهم البعض؟ رنموا مزمورًا )مز 96 : 1 .( كيف يمكن لأحد أن يحتضن عداوة لآخر يلتصق به وهو يُسَب ِّح الله بصوت واحدٍ؟ الحب هو أعظم صلاحٍ من الكل، والتسبيح بالمزامير يجلب الحب ، لأنه يُقَد ِّم نوعًا من رباط الوحدة، إذ يجمع الشعب معًا في خورُسٍ واحدٍ متناغمٍ... إنه نقطة البداية للمبتدئين، وعون للذين هم بالفعل في الطريق، ومصدر القوة للبالغين. إن كان التسبيح بمزمورٍ يجلب حزنًا، فهو حزن إلهي، لأن المزمور يقدر أن يهب دموعًا للقلب الحجري ثانيًا: تهب المزامير النفس سلامًا داخليًا، إذ يقول القديس باسيليوس الكبير: ] تهب النفس الطمأنينة وتعطيها السلام وتهدئ فيها بلبلة الأفكار وتراكم الشهوات. هذا الكتاب هو كتاب المحبة... هو سلاح ضد الشيطان... هو سبب راحة بعد تعب النهار... هو تعزية الشيوخ، هو باعث أفراحنا وأحزاننا المقدسة... هو نشيد رائع، هو صوت الكنيسة، هو بخور زكي الرائحة 105 [. ثالثًا تقدم المزامير لكل شخصٍ ما يناسبه من دواءٍ للنفس. يقول القديس باسيليوس: ] الكتاب موحى به من الله، ونافع" ) 2 تي 3 : 16 .( كُتِب بالروح القدس، لكي تجد نفوسنا كل نوعٍ من الدواء لشفائها، مهما كان عددنا، ومنه تختار الدواء المناسب لحالتها. لأن العلاج يسكن خطايا عظيمة )جا 10 : 4 .( يُقَد ِّم الأنبياء نوعًا واحدًا من التعليم، وتقدم الكتب التاريخية نوعًا آخر، والناموس آخر، ويوجد نوع آخر في حكمة الأمثال، أما سفر المزامير ففيه خلاصة كل الفوائد التي جاءت فيها جميعًا. فهو يتنبأ عن المستقبل، ويشير للتاريخ، ويُحَد ِّد قوانين لتجديد الحياة، ويوصي بما ينبغي عمله. هو نوع من الدليل للتعاليم الصالحة في كل شيءٍ والنافعة لكل أحدٍ. يضمد الجرح الحديث، فيشعر المريض بالتحس ُّن، ويعطي شفاءً للمريض، ويحفظ القائمين. وخلاصة الأمر يرفع حرب الشهوات التي تُدَن ِّس النفس بطرقٍ كثيرةٍ، ويجذبها بالفرح والتسبيح، لتنمو في الحكمة كما يقول: ] تطرد الشياطين، وتجلب لنا معونة الملائكة. هي سلاح في فزع الليل، راحة من عناء اليوم. هي الأمان للأطفال، وزينة للكبار، عزاء الشيوخ، وزينة النساء. هي حكمة

passages.label: كاتيكيزم الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية, p. 64
passages.text: بنشره، كما وردت هذه القصة باختصار في كتاب حياة الصلاة الأرثوذكسية في الطبعة الأولى عام 1952 . صدرت عدة كتب عنها بالعربية في لبنان ومصر. هذا الكتاب ليس مجرد قصة لكنه اختبار روحي شيق لازم للإنسان المسيحي، مارسه كثير من الآباء في الكنيسة الأولى بصورة أو أخرى. قيل عن هذا السائح الروسيّ أنه ذُهِل عندما دخل إلى الكنيسة وسمع في الرسالة إلى أهل تسالونيكي “صلّوا بلا انقطاع” ) 5 : 17 ( وصار يُفَك ِّر: هل يمكن للإنسان أن يعمل عملاً واحداً طيلة حياته؟ روى السائح الروسي أنه عاش لا منزل له، بل كان يجول من مكانٍ إلى آخر، لا يحمل إلا سلة على ظهره بها خبز يابس ومعه الكتاب المقدس. إذ ذهب إلى الكنيسة سمع من رسالة بولس الرسول الأولى إلى أهل تسالونيكي الآية: "صلوا بلا انقطاع" ) 5 : 17 ؛ راجع أف 6 : 18 ؛ 1 تي 2 : 8 .( فتح الكتاب المقدس، وقرأ ) 1 تس 5 : 17 (، فصار يفكر كيف يُنَف ِّذ هذه الوصية وهو مشغول بأمورٍ كثيرة، كيف يصلي في كل الأوقات وفي كل مكان. قَر َّر أن يمضي من كنيسة إلى كنيسة يسأل أشهر الوع َّاظ والمرشدين الذين ذاع صيتهم يطلب منهم الإجابة العملية على سؤاله. تحدثوا معه عن أهمية الصلاة وثمارها، لكن لم يجد من يحدثه عن كيفية ممارستها كل حين. سمع عن أحد النبلاء في إحدى القرى الروسية يقضي كل وقته في الصلاة وقراءة الأسفار المقدسة. ذهب إليه وسأله عن كيفية ممارسة هذه الوصية. صمت الشخص قليلاً، ثم قال له: "الصلاة الداخلية الدائمة هي رفع دائم للنفس البشرية أمام الله. وطلب منه أن يصلي كثيرًا ليختبر العذوبة التي يعلمنا الله بها كيف نصلي بلا انقطاعٍ. قال له: "صلِ كثيرًا وبحرارة، فالصلاة نفسها ستعلن لك كيف تصلي بلا انقطاعٍ... لكن الأمر يحتاج إلى وقتٍ طويلٍ". ثم قدم له زادًا ونقودًا لأجل سياحته. اعترى السائح شعور باليأس، إذ لم يفسر له ما يريده. ثم عاد إلى القراءة والتأمل مُفَك ِّرًا في كل ما قاله ذلك الأب، ولكن لم يصل إلى الحقيقة. ولم يعلم لماذا بدأ لا ينام بالليل. مشى ما يقرب من 125 ميلاً حتى وصل إلى ديرٍ، به أب محب طيب القلب، فالتقى به. رح َّب به الأب، سأله: "أيها الأب القديس... أريد أن أعرف كيف يُحَق ِّق الإنسان خلاصه؟ أجابه: "سرّ حسب أوامر الله، وأتلِ صلواتك فتخلص." قال السائح: "لكنني سمعت أنه ينبغي أن أصلي بلا انقطاع، وهذا هو ما لست أعرفه، ولم أستطع ممارسته. أرجوك أن تفسر لي هذا الأمر". أجابه بأن عنده كتابًا للقديس ديمترى أسقف روستوف ) 1651 - 1709 ( عن التعليم الروحي للإنسان الداخلي. فقرأ فيه أن كلمات الرسول بولس بخصوص الصلاة التي بلا انقطاع يجب أن تُفهَم كإشارة إلى الصلاة الفكرية، فالفكر في الواقع يمكنه أن يكون دائم الاستغراق في الله، فيعيش الإنسان بذلك في حياة الصلاة بلا انقطاع. سأله عن الطريق

passages.text: توف ) 1651 - 1709 ( عن التعليم الروحي للإنسان الداخلي. فقرأ فيه أن كلمات الرسول بولس بخصوص الصلاة التي بلا انقطاع يجب أن تُفهَم كإشارة إلى الصلاة الفكرية، فالفكر في الواقع يمكنه أن يكون دائم الاستغراق في الله، فيعيش الإنسان بذلك في حياة الصلاة بلا انقطاع. سأله عن الطريق الذي به يت َّجِه الذهن إلى الله على الدوام دون أن يغفل، بل يصلي دون انقطاع، أجابه إن هذا الأمر صعب حتى على الذين وُهِبوا من الله تلك العطية. ازداد اضطراب السائح، وقضى الليلة عنده ثم عاود السير في الطريق العام مدة خمسة أيام وهو مواظب على قراءة الكتاب المقدس. وفي الطريق التقى بأحد الآباء الشيوخ الذي أخبره عن وجود أب مُختبر في دير بالقرب منهما. تحدث مع هذا الأب وهما سائران نحو الدير في موضوع الصلاة بلا انقطاع. فأبرز له هذا الأب الآتي: 1. هذا السؤال يحتاج إلى فهم روحي وليس إلى تعليم .المدارس 2. يستخدم البعض حكمة العالم غير المجدية في شرح الأمور .الإلهية فيظن البعض أن الأعمال الصالحة هي التي تجعلنا . نصلي وعلى العكس فإن الصلاة هي أم الفضائل والأعمال . الصالحة 3. يدعونا الرسول أن نعطي الأولوية للصلاة لا الأعمال الصالحة، إذ :يقول فأطلب" أول كل شيء أن تُقَام طلبات وصلوات وابتهالات " وتشّكّرات ) 1 تي 2 : 1 .( فبدون الصلاة لا يتم عمل صالح، وبدون الصلاة لا يعرف الإنسان كيف يلتقي مع الله ويدخل معه في . حوارٍ إذ وصلا إلى الدير وهما يتحدثان معًا، قال له السائح أن يتفض َّل ويُخبِره عن كيفية الصلاة بلا 64
